contract.settlement_definition: Three window variants share one both-score wording. Full-match BTTS (147 series, 129 with text): YES when both named sides score 'after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)'. First-half BTTS (46 series): only goals scored during the 1st Half count. Second-half BTTS (10 series, e.g. KXEPL2HBTTS, KXUEFASC2HBTTS): only goals scored during the 2nd Half count, regardless of the half-time score. In every variant own goals count towards the team awarded the goal; BTTS-No is the complement and there is no ladder. None of the 185 BTTS texts read contains a cancellation, postponement or abandonment clause, and the half texts do not say whether a half's stoppage time or (for 2H) extra time is included.

rules_evidence.quote: Own goals count towards the team awarded the goal.
rules_evidence.establishes: An own goal is credited to the beneficiary, so it counts toward that side having scored; a defender error can settle YES without any attacking quality.

rules_evidence.quote: after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)
rules_evidence.establishes: Settlement window is regulation plus stoppage only; extra-time goals in knockout ties cannot rescue a BTTS-No.

rules_evidence.quote: both score a goal in the Montevideo City vs Atletico Mineiro CONMEBOL Sudamericana match
rules_evidence.establishes: A continental club match uses the same both-score wording as domestic leagues, so the two-leg tie context changes incentives but not the contract.

rules_evidence.quote: Only goals scored during the 1st Half count for the purposes of this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: First-half BTTS (46 series in this key) counts only first-half goals, so soc.period_split and half-specific rates, not the regulation lambdas, are the object.

rules_evidence.quote: Only goals scored during the 2nd Half count for the purposes of this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Second-half BTTS counts second-half goals only, so a 1-1 half-time score does not help YES; the second-half rates, which depend on the half-time state, are the object.

rules_evidence.quote: both score a goal in the 1st Half of the Manchester United vs Aston Villa EPL match
rules_evidence.establishes: First-half BTTS re-filed from first_half_and_period uses the same both-score construction restricted to the first half.

variants_and_edge_cases: Knockout/cup ties (KXCOPADELREYBTTS, KXISRSCUPBTTS, KXCONMEBOLSUDBTTS): extra time is excluded, so a 1-0 after 90 that finishes 2-1 in ET is still BTTS-No; the 90-minute-only goal process, not the advancement process, is what must be modelled.

203 live series, 185 with rules text: 129 full-match texts use the regulation-only wording plus the own-goal clause, 46 first-half and 10 second-half texts use 'Only goals scored during the 1st/2nd Half count'; 18 series (e.g. KXSOCCERBTTS, KXCLUBWCBTTS, KXFINALISSIMABTTS) are TITLE_ONLY and assumed to follow the full-match wording.

Half-window variants (KXUCL1HBTTS, KXEPL1HBTTS, KXMLS2HBTTS, KXWC2HBTTS) need half-split scoring rates and half-level dependence; second-half BTTS also depends on the half-time score through chase/park behaviour (stage s6).
Own-goal credit means P(team scores) must include opponent own-goal probability (about 3-5% of goals), a small positive term for weak attacks facing high lines and crosses.

No clean-sheet series is listed under this key; postponement, abandonment and (for 2H variants in knockout games such as KXUEFASC2HBTTS, KXWC2HBTTS) extra-time treatment are not stated in any BTTS text.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league/competition match report goal events with goal credit (own goals credited to the beneficiary), as published by the governing league and tracked by Kalshi's data provider; minute of goal not needed for the full-match contract, needed for the first- and second-half variants (period attribution of stoppage-time goals).

mechanism.summary: BTTS is the intersection of two goal-count events, P(H>=1 and A>=1), so it is governed by the lower of the two scoring rates and by their dependence. Each side's rate comes from opponent-adjusted chance volume and quality, adjusted for the confirmed starting XI and keeper; each side's shutout probability exceeds the Poisson value for teams with concentrated attacks. The two processes are coupled by game state: after the first goal the trailing side chases (raising both sides' chance rates) or the leader parks. Discrete shocks (a red card, a penalty, a keeper swap) and the regulation-only settlement window (extra time excluded, own goals credited) complete the chain. The binary has no strike ladder, so the key modelling objects are min(lambda), zero inflation and the state-conditional hazard. Half variants (1H and 2H BTTS, 56 series: 46 first-half, 10 second-half) need each side's half-specific rate, half-level dependence and, for the second half, the half-time state.

stages.name: Team scoring intensities
stages.description: Each side's regulation goal rate is the product of shot volume against this specific opposition (tempo, territory, set-piece route) and chance quality given lineup and keeper. BTTS needs BOTH rates to be non-trivial, so the binding quantity is min(lambda_home, lambda_away), not the total: a 3.0 total split 2.7/0.3 is a low BTTS price while 1.6/1.4 is high. The weaker side's attack against the stronger side's current back line and keeper is the swing stage. In cross-division cup ties (Copa del Rey, Copa do Brasil, Coupe de France, FA Cup and DFB-Pokal early rounds, the Israeli Cup) the two sides share no league opponents, so the weaker side's lambda, which binds BTTS Yes and the favourite's clean sheet, is set on a common scale by soc.cross_tier_strength_link and then scaled by the favourite's expected rotation (soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch), which raises the underdog's scoring chance when the big club rests starters.
stages.distribution: Poisson-like counts per side with overdispersion; P(side scores>=1)=1-exp(-lambda) is concave, so uncertainty in lambda matters most for the low-lambda side.

stages.name: Zero-state structure and failed-to-score clustering
stages.description: Whether a side draws a blank is not purely a Poisson coin: low-block teams that cede territory but concentrate chances in a few counters/set pieces, and teams with a single focal striker, show more shutouts than their xG implies, while teams with distributed threat show fewer. Keeper shot-stopping and the bottom end of the finishing distribution sit here. This is the stage the ratings-only model misses and where a zero-inflation term lives.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated / negative-binomial count per side; failed-to-score rate varies across teams beyond Poisson with a heavy dependence on single-player availability.

stages.name: Cross-team dependence and score-state response
stages.description: The two scoring processes are not independent: after the first goal the trailing side commits numbers (raising both its attack rate and the leader's counter chances), while a leader that goes two up shuts the game down. Dixon-Coles rho captures only the 0-0/1-0/0-1/1-1 cells; the BTTS-relevant mechanism is the conditional hazard that the still-scoreless side scores after conceding first, versus the leader parking the bus.
stages.distribution: Joint (bivariate) goal distribution with time-varying conditional intensities; positive correlation at low scores, negative at high scores through game-state.

stages.name: Match-day shocks: red cards, penalties, timing
stages.description: Late lineup news (keeper, centre-back, striker), a first-half red card, or a penalty award each move one side's scoring chance by a large discrete amount. A penalty (about 75-80% conversion, awarded in roughly a quarter of matches) is a near-certain route for an otherwise blanked team; referee and VAR tendencies and the lineup timestamp determine how much of this is knowable before kickoff.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete shocks (red card ~8-10% of matches, penalty ~25%) layered on the count process; right-skewed effect on lambda.

stages.name: Settlement mapping
stages.description: Goals are counted in regulation plus stoppage with own goals credited to the beneficiary; extra time, penalties and shootouts are excluded for the full-match texts. Half variants count only goals of the named half, so 45+ and 90+ stoppage attribution to halves must follow the provider's period field; knockout ties with advancement incentives change the 90-minute goal process (cagey first legs) without changing the contract.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the goal event log; only the regulation-window definition and abandonment handling vary.

stages.name: Half-window joint scoring for 1H and 2H BTTS
stages.description: For the 56 half series (46 first-half, 10 second-half) both sides must score inside one 45-minute window: P(YES) is roughly (1-exp(-l_home_h))(1-exp(-l_away_h)) with half rates l_h derived from each team's half share of goals, then corrected for half-level dependence. First-half rates are lower and cagey openings lower both together; second-half rates are conditional on the half-time score, because a trailing side commits numbers while the leader sits deeper, so a 1-0 half-time state raises the trailer's 2H rate and lowers the leader's. A first-half red card shifts both 2H rates.
stages.distribution: Product of two low-mean half counts (half means about 0.5-0.8 per side) with draw-like coupling; P(1H BTTS) typically 0.12-0.25, P(2H BTTS) slightly higher.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted strengths within a league; the cross-division bridge rating puts both sides of a cup mismatch on one scale.

opponent_matchup.note: Weak-attack versus strong-defence pairing is what sets the lower lambda; set-piece routes let low-block teams still score.

role_personnel.note: Single-striker dependence and the starting keeper/centre-back pair drive blank probability.

availability_news.note: Confirmed XIs and the favourite's predicted rotation in cup mismatches.

coaching_scheme.note: Whether a manager chases or parks after the first goal sets the conditional hazard; pressing style sets openness.

environment.note: Weather, altitude and pitch change goal rates by a few percent in aggregate; for a binary requiring both sides to score the effect is second-order and is absorbed by league/venue baseline ratings, so no separate BTTS-specific environment input is proposed.

game_context_script.note: Score-state response after the first goal is the main source of dependence; not pregame-observable but estimable from history.

pace_volume.note: Shot volume sets how many attempts each side gets; tempo raises both lambdas jointly.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing and keeper luck separated from skill, plus excess failed-to-score beyond Poisson.

distribution_variance.note: Low-score dependence and zero-inflation are the distribution inputs that move P(0) directly.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Aggregate state of two-legged cup ties, predicted rotation and dead-rubber leverage shift the weaker side scoring chance and the stronger side defensive intensity; effect sizes for BTTS are still to be estimated.

officiating_rules.note: Referee/VAR-shrunk penalty-award rate gives the discrete route by which a blanked side still scores; card counts (soc.fouls_cards, audited WEAK) are no longer cited as cover.

settlement_contract.note: Regulation-only window, own-goal credit, first-half variant parse flags.

soc.team_fail_to_score_propensity.label: Excess failed-to-score rate (zero-inflation) per team
soc.team_fail_to_score_propensity.mechanism: Teams differ in how often they draw a blank beyond what their mean chance quality implies.
soc.team_fail_to_score_propensity.rationale: A Poisson-from-xG model understates blank frequency for teams whose chance creation is concentrated in one striker or a few counters, and overstates it for diffuse attacks; BTTS-No is mostly the weaker side blanking, so this is the term that mis-prices the favourite-vs-low-block fixtures.
soc.team_fail_to_score_propensity.measurement: For each of the team's last 38 league matches compute P0_m = product over its shots (including penalties) of (1 - xG_shot) using Understat shot xG (own goals excluded); excess_FTS = (share of matches with 0 goals scored) - mean of P0_m, weights half-life 19 matches; shrink toward 0 with weight n/(n+15); separate home/away values. Use alongside the xG rating, not instead. As-of kickoff-1h, prior matches only.
soc.team_fail_to_score_propensity.why: BTTS-No wins are blanks by one side; excess zero mass is the direct driver and is not in any existing input.

soc.trailing_team_response_hazard.label: Conditional scoring hazard of the side that conceded first
soc.trailing_team_response_hazard.mechanism: Intensity of a scoreless team after conceding, and of the leader after scoring, by minute bucket.
soc.trailing_team_response_hazard.rationale: BTTS completion usually happens after the first goal; whether the conceding side then pushes up (and gets chances) or the leader sits deep determines the second scorer, and managers differ markedly. Dixon-Coles rho cannot express this.
soc.trailing_team_response_hazard.measurement: From event-level goals and shots with minute: for each team, rate of its goals per 90 in states 'trailing by 1' and 'level' for minutes 20-80, split by pre-match favourite/underdog role, exponential decay half-life 2 seasons, shrink to league mean with k=300 minutes in-state; output the ratio hazard_trailing/hazard_level as a multiplier on lambda after the first goal.
free_sources: FBref match logs (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED after Opta change)
raw_data: shot/goal events with minute and score state
soc.trailing_team_response_hazard.why: Turns static lambdas into the sequential process that BTTS actually follows.

soc.weaker_side_big_chance_creation.label: Weaker side's big-chance and box-entry creation vs this opponent's defence
soc.weaker_side_big_chance_creation.mechanism: Counts of high-xG chances the likely lower-lambda side generates against opponents of this defensive profile.
soc.weaker_side_big_chance_creation.rationale: P(score>=1) for the weaker side depends on tail events (big chances, counters, set pieces) rather than on its average xG; a team with 0.8 xG/match from two 0.4-xG chances differs from 0.8 from eight 0.1 shots.
soc.weaker_side_big_chance_creation.measurement: For the side with lower pre-match lambda: per-match number of shots with xG>=0.25 (excluding penalties) opponent-adjusted by the opponent's big-chances-conceded rate, 20-match window half-life 10, shrink k=10; also open-play-only vs set-piece split. Label which side is weaker by the ratings difference at as-of time.
raw_data: shot-level xG, situation tags, team ids
soc.weaker_side_big_chance_creation.why: Gives the minimum-lambda channel a quality-weighted measurement instead of a mean.

soc.open_game_index.reason: Composite of historic clean-sheet and failed-to-score rates; it double counts what ratings and the dixon-coles term already encode and is noisy at 38 matches. Superseded by the explicit excess-FTS input.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.reason: Opponent/venue-adjusted attack and defence supply both lambdas; the core of the market.

soc.dixon_coles_low_score.reason: Rho only moves the 0-0, 1-0, 0-1, 1-1 cells; league-level rho is weakly identified and small (about -0.03 to -0.1) so it cannot be primary for BTTS.

soc.gk.reason: Shrunk PSxG-GA is a real but small effect (a few percent on conceding probability); needs the confirmed starter.

soc.xi_strength_delta.reason: Missing striker or centre-back shifts the scoring probability of the relevant side; partial pregame knowability.

soc.finishing_regression.reason: Already embodied if ratings are xG-based; useful only as the shrinkage target, otherwise it double regresses.

soc.keeper_shot_stopping_regression.reason: Defined as shrunk PSxG minus GA, the same quantity as soc.gk's measurement; keeping both inflates the weight on keeper form.

soc.pace_press.reason: Tempo raises both lambdas jointly, which is mostly redundant with xG ratings for BTTS; matters via the weaker side's shot volume.

soc.period_split.reason: Irrelevant to the 147 full-match BTTS series but primary for KXUCL1HBTTS, the one first-half series now in this key (only 1st-half goals count); secondary overall.

soc.score_state.reason: Not pregame-observable; used to fit the conditional-hazard input, not as a direct feature.

m.rules_text.reason: Settlement parse flag (regulation-only, own goals) rather than a predictor; needed so extra time is not mixed into training labels.

soc.lineups_pit.reason: Confirmed XI timestamp is the largest pregame update for keeper/striker; the as-of vintage rule is the key.

soc.shots.reason: Shots for/against largely duplicate xG ratings; shots on target adds only a keeper-workload view.

soc.fouls_cards.reason: Card counts are weak predictors of BTTS; only referee penalty propensity matters and is covered under soc.penalty_rate, not here.

soc.set_piece_matchup.reason: Set pieces are the route by which a low-block weaker side scores; relevant to the min-lambda side.

soc.second_half_state_multiplier.reason: 2H BTTS only (stage s6 and the conditional interaction with soc.half_level_dependence_rho): the half-time score selects the second-half rate multipliers (level keeps both rates near baseline; a one-goal lead raises the trailer's and lowers the leader's); not used for full-match or 1H series.

soc.half_level_dependence_rho.reason: 1H and 2H BTTS only (stage s6): both sides must score inside one 45-minute window, so the dependence between the two half-window scoring processes corrects the product (1-exp(-l_home_h))(1-exp(-l_away_h)); this is a separate parameter from the full-match Dixon-Coles rho.

soc.cross_tier_strength_link.reason: Cross-division cup ties (Copa del Rey, Copa do Brasil, Coupe de France, FA Cup and DFB-Pokal early rounds, Israeli Cup), stage s1: the two sides share no league opponents, so this bridge puts the weaker side's lambda, which binds BTTS Yes, on a common scale; irrelevant within one league.

soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.reason: Cross-division cup ties only, stage s1: a heavily rotated favourite (7+ changes) raises the underdog's scoring chance and lowers the favourite's own clean-sheet probability, scaling the weaker side's lambda after the bridge rating.

soc.second_leg_aggregate_state.reason: Cup-tie BTTS (e.g. KXCOPADELREYBTTS, KXCONMEBOLSUDBTTS), stage s4: in a second leg the aggregate sets which side must score and how open the 90 minutes are, changing the goal process without changing the contract (extra time is excluded from settlement); no role in league fixtures.

soc.rotation_index.reason: Stage s4 lineup-news shock: expected rotation of starters (low-stakes league games, congested cup weeks) changes each side's scoring chance and clean-sheet probability for that fixture; context because it is only knowable partially before the lineup timestamp.

soc.stakes_leverage.reason: Stage s4: dead rubbers and six-pointers change a side's risk posture and so both scoring rates; the direction for BTTS is not established (open dead rubbers and cagey high-leverage games are both plausible), so it is context to be estimated, not a signed adjustment.

soc.half_specific_xg_ratings.reason: 1H and 2H BTTS only (stage s6): per-team half-specific attack and defence rates l_h from each team's half share of goals feed the half-window product; full-match series use soc.xg_adjusted_ratings instead.

soc.penalty_rate.reason: Stage s4 and the event-stream and referee/penalty required_data feeds: a penalty award (about a quarter of matches, roughly 75-80% conversion) is a near-certain scoring route for an otherwise blanked side, so referee/VAR and team penalty propensity move P(weaker side scores); also in the game_total blueprint, carried here explicitly so the archetype's own list supplies what stage s4 asserts.

interactions.mechanism: The weaker side's P(score>=1) is 1-exp(-chances x conversion against this keeper): a high count of big chances only turns into BTTS-Yes if the opposing keeper's shrunk shot-stopping does not cancel it, so the keeper term scales the weaker side's chance-quality channel (direction: strong keeper cuts it).
interactions.how_to_test: Bin matches by weaker-side big-chance count and by opposing keeper shrunk PSxG-GA tercile; compare realised weaker-side scoring rate with the additive model.

interactions.mechanism: Keeper effect applies only if the shrunk-rating starter actually plays; a backup keeper replaces a +0.05 PSxG-GA/shot starter with a replacement-level one, so the keeper term must be conditioned on the confirmed lineup, not season data.
interactions.how_to_test: Split matches by keeper change vs no change and compare residual conceding rate.

interactions.mechanism: Before the first goal the pairing behaves as in a static Dixon-Coles game; after it, the trailing manager's choice switches the match into an open regime, so the effective dependence is positive below one goal and may flip later in the match (hypothesis, timing not established from data).
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate scoring hazard conditional on state at each minute bucket; test if BTTS error clusters in 1-0 games with a chasing side.

interactions.mechanism: Zero inflation is amplified when the focal striker is out: the same excess-FTS teams blank far more often without their one forward, while diffuse attacks barely move.
interactions.how_to_test: Interaction regression of blank indicator on focal-striker absence times excess_FTS.

interactions.mechanism: A weaker side with elite set-piece xG crosses a threshold at which its P(score) stays above the rating-implied level (the 0.55-0.6 figure is an unsourced hypothesis to be estimated) even against a dominant opponent; below the threshold it collapses to counter-attack luck.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin set-piece xG share; compare weaker-side scoring rate vs open-play-only prediction.

interactions.mechanism: For 2H BTTS the half-time state selects the second-half multipliers: a level half-time score keeps both rates near baseline, a one-goal lead raises the trailer's and lowers the leader's 2H rate, which raises P(trailer scores) but lowers P(leader scores), so the net effect on 2H BTTS depends on the asymmetry.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin historical 2H BTTS outcomes by half-time margin and compare with an independent-half model.

interactions.mechanism: Only in cross-division cup ties: the lower-tier side's goal rate comes from the bridge rating gap, and a heavily rotated favourite (7+ changes) raises that rate and lowers its own clean-sheet probability, so BTTS Yes moves up most when a large tier gap coincides with heavy rotation; within-league fixtures are unaffected.
interactions.how_to_test: On cross-tier cup ties, compare calibration of P(weaker side scores) by rating-gap bucket with and without the bridge term, split by realised starters changed by the favourite.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating (1-exp(-lambda)) in each side's rating, so equal rating errors cost more at low lambda
nonlinearities.why: The BTTS probability is a product of two saturating terms; the lower-lambda factor dominates the error and a linear rating-difference feature misprices extremes.

nonlinearities.shape: Small linear-in-shrunk-PSxG effect with a heavy shrinkage factor
nonlinearities.why: Raw PSxG-GA swings of +-0.15 per shot are mostly luck over a season; the usable effect is the shrunk fraction (about 15-25% of raw).

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: affects only the four low cells
nonlinearities.why: Rho adjusts the joint 0-0/1-0/0-1/1-1 probabilities and is exactly zero above 1 goal each, so its influence concentrates on the BTTS-No mass.

unresolved.description: 185 of 203 BTTS series have rules text with one wording per window; 18 are TITLE_ONLY. No BTTS text states settlement for postponement, cancellation or a match abandoned after both sides have scored, and the half texts do not say whether stoppage time belongs to the half or whether a 2nd Half in a knockout game includes extra time.

unresolved.description: Whether excess failed-to-score beyond Poisson is stable across seasons or just noise at 38 matches per team is not established; the shrinkage constant and window are a guess.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Estimate year-over-year persistence of excess_FTS on 8+ seasons of top-5 league data and set shrinkage by empirical Bayes.

contract.settlement_definition: Seven live series, all with rules text, in four mechanisms. KXEPLH2HFINISH: YES when the named club is placed above the other in the final EPL table after all official tiebreakers, deductions and adjustments. KXEPLH2H: outcome markets on the combined results of the two regular-season league meetings (e.g. 'wins one and draws one'). World Cup stage comparisons: KXWCTEAMH2H has outcomes for each team going further and 'Eliminated same stage' (a semi-final loser stays at Semifinals whatever the third-place result); KXWCBESTHOST pays the furthest-advancing host nation, $1/N if several tie. Player comparisons: KXWCMESSIMBAPPE (goals) and KXWCMESSIRONALDO (goals+assists) are titled 'Will X or Y have more ...'; the sampled leg in each is 'Tie', which pays if the two players' 2026 World Cup tallies are exactly equal ('Only goals scored during the 2026 World Cup are considered'); the player legs (one player strictly more) are implied by the title but their text was not sampled. KXPPPKSO: a PrizePicks 1v1 penalty shootout between two influencers, five kicks each on a non-regulation 10x6 ft net, then sudden death.

rules_evidence.quote: A team finishes higher if it is placed above the other team in that final table after all official tiebreakers, point deductions, and other official adjustments are applied.
rules_evidence.establishes: Finish-ahead settles on the final official table including tiebreakers and point deductions, so the tie branch and any pending sanction are part of the event; no tie outcome exists.

rules_evidence.quote: wins one and draws one of the two regular-season league matches against Arsenal
rules_evidence.establishes: The Results series is a partition of the joint outcome of the two direct league meetings (W/D/L x W/D/L for one club), so it needs a two-fixture match-result model, not a season simulation.

rules_evidence.quote: This market resolves based on the final official results of the two regular-season league matches scheduled between Arsenal and Tottenham
rules_evidence.establishes: Only the two scheduled regular-season league meetings count; cup meetings are excluded and a meeting already played fixes part of the outcome.

rules_evidence.quote: If both teams tie for the furthest stage advanced to, then the market titled "Eliminated same stage" resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The World Cup head-to-head is a three-way partition over stages reached, with a dedicated same-stage outcome, so P(same stage) must be priced.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple host nations tie for the furthest stage advanced to, payouts will be as follows:
rules_evidence.establishes: The best-host series dead-heats when hosts reach the same stage, so the joint stage-reached distribution of the three hosts is required.

rules_evidence.quote: records exactly the same number goals as the count of Kylian Mbappé's total goals during the entire tournament
rules_evidence.establishes: An equality event on two players' tournament tallies, dominated by the probability both finish on the same low count (including 0-0).

rules_evidence.quote: Each contestant takes 5 shots each. If tied after 5 shots, 1 shot each until a winner.
rules_evidence.establishes: The PrizePicks series is an amateur 1v1 penalty duel with alternating keeper roles and sudden death, unrelated to professional match models.

variants_and_edge_cases: If two teams finish level on points the outcome depends on the competition's tiebreak order (goal difference vs head-to-head vs play-off), so P(ahead) must include a tie-resolution branch whose rule differs by league (the order differs by league and is unsourced here; it must be read from the competition regulations).

A pending points deduction or administrative sanction can reorder the final table after the last match; a head-to-head contract may settle on the official final table at a stated date rather than on-pitch results.

KXEPLH2H settles on the two regular-season league meetings only; once the first meeting is played the contract reduces to one match result, and a meeting postponed beyond the season end is not addressed.
KXWCTEAMH2H stages are Group, R32, R16, QF, SF, lose final, win final; third-place results are ignored, and when the two teams can meet in the bracket their outcomes are directly coupled.

Player comparison series (KXWCMESSIMBAPPE, KXWCMESSIRONALDO) are three-way (X more, Y more, Tie); the Tie leg has large mass at low equal counts (both 0 or both 1), so availability and team exits matter as much as scoring rates. The texts do not name the source for goal or assist attribution.
KXPPPKSO is an influencer exhibition with a non-regulation net and no published performance history; it has no postponement or no-show clause in its text.

Non-standard finish formats (Ecuador LigaPro hexagonal with carried-over points, Peru/Uruguay/Venezuela playoffs, MLS conferences) make "finish ahead" ambiguous between aggregate table, stage table and playoff result; none are verified.
contract.settlement_data_source: Final official EPL table (KXEPLH2HFINISH); official results of the two league meetings (KXEPLH2H); FIFA official stage results and player statistics (World Cup series); the PrizePicks event result (KXPPPKSO).

mechanism.summary: A head-to-head season finish is a race between two cumulative points totals. State at the as-of date (points, goal difference, games in hand, deductions) is the starting condition; each team's remaining fixtures generate points through a goal model with its own opponents, venues and rest; the two totals are coupled negatively through direct meetings and positively through shared shocks and common opponents, which sets the variance of the gap. Strength itself is uncertain and drifts with injuries, transfers and congestion. The resolution is the final table, with a tiebreaker branch on equal points and a possible post-hoc deduction. Four mechanisms share the key: s1-s5 cover the table-finish contract (KXEPLH2HFINISH); s6 covers KXEPLH2H, which settles on the two regular-season league meetings (a two-match result model); s7 covers the World Cup stage comparisons (KXWCTEAMH2H, KXWCBESTHOST) through the joint stage-reached distribution of the teams compared; s8 covers the three-way player tally comparisons (KXWCMESSIMBAPPE, KXWCMESSIRONALDO); s9 covers the PrizePicks penalty duel (KXPPPKSO).

stages.name: Current table state and games in hand
stages.description: The starting point is the exact points, goal difference, goals scored and fixtures played for both teams on the as-of date, including postponed matches and deductions. The gap relative to the number of fixtures remaining sets how much variance must be overcome: a 6-point lead with 10 games left is very different from the same lead with 3 left.
stages.distribution: Deterministic state with integer points; drives a discrete race outcome whose variance scales with remaining fixtures.

stages.name: Remaining-fixture points distributions
stages.description: Each team's remaining matches generate points via a calibrated goal model with opponent strength, venue and rest; the two teams face different schedules, so the expected points difference depends on schedule asymmetry, not only on current ratings. Rating uncertainty widens the spread of the points-gap distribution beyond independent match noise.
stages.distribution: Sum of independent three-outcome match lotteries per team (points 0/1/3) plus a shared latent strength uncertainty; approx normal for the gap with sd per match to be estimated (a three-outcome points lottery gives roughly 1.2-1.4 points per match for typical probabilities).

stages.name: Cross-team dependence of outcomes
stages.description: The two teams' results are not independent: direct meetings are zero-sum (a win for one is a loss for the other), common opponents produce correlated results, and shared shocks (same European fixtures, similar injury waves) correlate depth. The correlation of the final points of the two teams sets the variance of their difference, and so the probability the leader holds.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution of two points totals with negative correlation from direct fixtures and positive correlation from shared opponents/shocks; difference variance can be well below the independent sum.

stages.name: Squad shocks over the remaining horizon
stages.description: Over a multi-month horizon injuries, suspensions, transfer windows and manager changes shift one team's strength relative to the other; squad depth determines how much a typical injury wave costs. Competing in cups and Europe adds minutes load and rotation that reduces league-priority quality. A manager change inside the remaining horizon is simulated rather than ignored: each simulated week draws a dismissal from soc.manager_dismissal_hazard given the club's simulated results, and after a change the club's rating is re-blended by soc.transfers (prior weight k/(k+m) over m matches under the new manager); the size of the post-change shift is left to the event study.
stages.distribution: Random strength drift over weeks; heavy right tail for key-player long-term injuries; depth modulates the tail.

stages.name: Tie resolution and settlement
stages.description: A tie on points moves the outcome to the competition's tiebreaker (goal difference, goals scored or head-to-head), so the end-of-season goal-difference gap and direct-match results matter in the narrow set of paths where points are level; deductions and the official final table fix the settlement.
stages.distribution: Discrete tie branch (P(equal points) is an unsourced hypothesis of order 5-10% for evenly matched teams, to be measured from simulated and historical tables) resolved by a continuous goal-difference comparison.

stages.name: Direct-meeting result combinations (KXEPLH2H)
stages.description: For the Results series the event is the pair of outcomes of the two scheduled league meetings between the clubs. Each meeting has its own home/draw/away probabilities from opponent-adjusted attack and defence ratings, the venue of that leg and the draw mass from low-score dependence; the joint outcome (for example one win and one draw for the named club) is the product of the two leg distributions conditional on any leg already played, plus a small positive correlation from shared rating error. Lineups matter close to each leg.
stages.distribution: Discrete 3x3 joint over two match outcomes; each leg roughly 0.25-0.30 draw mass; legs nearly independent given ratings, a played leg collapses one margin.

stages.name: World Cup stage comparison between two named teams or among hosts
stages.description: KXWCTEAMH2H and KXWCBESTHOST compare stages reached: each team's stage distribution comes from the group and bracket simulation, but the comparison needs the joint distribution, because two teams in the same group or bracket half cannot both go deep and may eliminate each other directly. The same-stage outcome is large for weak pairs (both out in the group or round of 32), and the host comparison must keep the $1/N tie mass.
stages.distribution: Joint categorical over seven stages for two or three teams; P(same stage) often 0.25-0.45 for comparable mid-tier nations.

stages.name: Comparison of two players' tournament tallies (more / fewer / exactly equal)
stages.description: For the Messi-Mbappe goals and Messi-Ronaldo goal-contribution series the outcome is which player finishes the 2026 World Cup with the higher tally, with a separate Tie leg for identical tallies. Each tally is the player's per-match scoring (and assist) intensity times his matches played, which depends on availability and his team's progress; P(Tie) is the sum over k of P(A=k)P(B=k) adjusted for dependence and is dominated by low counts and early exits, while the player legs split the remaining mass by relative intensity and expected matches.
stages.distribution: Joint of two overdispersed count pmfs; P(Tie) typically 0.15-0.30, highest when both players have low expected tallies; player legs share the rest.

stages.name: Amateur 1v1 penalty duel (KXPPPKSO)
stages.description: The PrizePicks shootout alternates the two contestants as kicker and keeper over five kicks each on a small 10x6 ft net, then sudden death. The win probability depends on each person's conversion as kicker against the other as keeper; with a small net, keeper reach matters more than in professional shootouts. No historical record exists, so the price rests on weak priors from the contestants' content and is close to a coin flip.
stages.distribution: Two binomial sequences of five kicks with unknown per-kick rates (perhaps 0.5-0.8), then geometric sudden death; outcome near 50/50 under symmetric priors.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted team ratings with posterior uncertainty feed both teams' remaining-fixture points.

opponent_matchup.note: Each team's remaining opponents and the direct meetings set the schedule asymmetry.

role_personnel.note: Key-player dependence and replacement quality decide how injuries move the strength gap.

availability_news.note: Injuries and suspensions to key players across the remaining horizon shift the gap; no timestamps for lineup vintage needed for season-long contracts.

coaching_scheme.note: In-window dismissal hazard and the post-change rating re-blend; the size of the new-manager shift remains an empirical question.

environment.note: Venue, altitude and weather act through single matches and average out over 8-20 remaining fixtures; home advantage is already embedded in the match-level goal model, so no separate environment input is justified for a season-end comparison of two teams.

game_context_script.note: Current gap and games-in-hand define the race state; the remaining-matches count determines variance.

pace_volume.note: Possession and tempo volume affect match goal totals but a head-to-head table finish is decided on points, not on counts, so volume enters only through the team rating that feeds the goal model rather than as a standalone input.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing and xG separate luck from skill in the points earned so far, which the rating must regress. For KXPPPKSO the per-kick conversion and save priors of the two contestants are the whole efficiency question.

distribution_variance.note: Joint distribution of the two final points totals (table finish), the joint stage-reached vector (World Cup comparisons) and the joint tally distribution (player comparisons).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Fixture congestion and stakes leverage differ between teams; late-season dead rubbers change effort.

officiating_rules.note: Match-level referee tendencies average out across the many remaining fixtures and have no systematic effect on which of two teams finishes ahead; an official ban or deduction ruling is handled under settlement and tie rules instead.

settlement_contract.note: Tiebreak order, deductions and which table is official.

soc.points_gap_state.label: Points, goal-difference gap and games in hand as of the as-of date
soc.points_gap_state.mechanism: Exact standings state of the two teams including postponed fixtures and deductions.
soc.points_gap_state.rationale: Season-outcome probabilities are path-dependent: the variance to be overcome shrinks with remaining fixtures, and games-in-hand and goal difference matter for ties; this state is the starting condition of every simulation and is not a stored input in the catalog.
soc.points_gap_state.measurement: At each as-of date T-1h: points_A - points_B, GD_A - GD_B, GF_A - GF_B, matches_left_A, matches_left_B, matches_left_both (direct meetings), and any announced deduction applied to the table; recompute after every matchday; units in points and goals.
soc.points_gap_state.why: The race outcome is a function of the gap relative to what remains, so this is the primary state variable.

soc.h2h_zero_sum_fixtures.label: Remaining direct meetings and venue between the two teams
soc.h2h_zero_sum_fixtures.mechanism: Direct fixtures transfer points between the two teams one-for-one.
soc.h2h_zero_sum_fixtures.rationale: A direct meeting is a 6-point swing between the teams, not a 3-point addition to both, and the venue asymmetry (who hosts the last meeting) changes the variance of the gap; ignoring it mis-states the correlation structure.
soc.h2h_zero_sum_fixtures.measurement: Count remaining direct fixtures with date and venue; for each compute P(win_A), P(draw), P(win_B) from the goal model and the expected gap shift; weight by remaining horizon and by home advantage (league-season HFA); store as vector for the simulator.
raw_data: fixtures with home/away team and date
soc.h2h_zero_sum_fixtures.why: Directly sets negative correlation between the two points totals.

soc.shared_shock_overlap.label: Overlap of fixture load and injury exposure between the two teams
soc.shared_shock_overlap.mechanism: Shared congestion (same European competition, same international call-ups) correlates strength shocks.
soc.shared_shock_overlap.rationale: If both teams play in the same continental tournament their rest and rotation shocks move together, which raises correlation of their league results and shrinks the variance of the gap; separate-schedule teams have independent shocks.
soc.shared_shock_overlap.measurement: For each team: set of competitions, match-count and travel in the next 8 weeks and international call-ups; overlap = Jaccard of competitions and the correlation of the schedule load series across the last 3 seasons of pairs of similar teams; used to set the shock-correlation parameter in the joint simulation.
soc.shared_shock_overlap.why: Provides the cross-team shock correlation the pairwise comparison is sensitive to.

soc.pair_player_tournament_tally_joint.label: Joint distribution of two named players' World Cup tallies
soc.pair_player_tournament_tally_joint.mechanism: Equality contracts pay on the two tallies being identical, so the full pmf of each tally and their dependence are needed.
soc.pair_player_tournament_tally_joint.rationale: P(equal) is driven by low counts and by the probability each team exits early; a model of expected goals alone misprices it. Dependence arises if the two teams can meet or share a bracket half; goal contributions add assist attribution noise.
soc.pair_player_tournament_tally_joint.measurement: For each player simulate, inside the tournament simulation (N>=100,000), matches played from his team's path, start probability and minutes (last 12 internationals, shrunk to role prior k=6), and per-match goals (and assists) as negative binomial with mean from international npxG/90 plus penalty duty; record both tallies per draw and compute P(A=B) directly; update after each match day.
soc.pair_player_tournament_tally_joint.why: Prices exact equality of two players' tournament goals or goal contributions. The same joint draws give the two player legs (A>B, B>A) as well as the Tie leg.

soc.influencer_pk_duel_skill.label: Penalty duel skill prior for exhibition contestants
soc.influencer_pk_duel_skill.mechanism: The 1v1 duel winner is set by each contestant's conversion as kicker and save rate as keeper on a small net.
soc.influencer_pk_duel_skill.rationale: Professional shootout data do not transfer to amateurs on a 10x6 ft net with alternating roles; only weak priors from published content and any prior PrizePicks events exist, so the input mostly expresses how far from 50% the price should be allowed to move.
soc.influencer_pk_duel_skill.measurement: Per contestant, Beta prior on per-kick conversion (mean 0.65, strength 10) and on save rate (mean 0.30, strength 10), updated with counted kicks/saves from prior filmed duels (each kick one trial, dated before listing); win probability by exact enumeration of five alternating kicks each plus sudden death.
raw_data: prior duel kick-by-kick outcomes per contestant
soc.influencer_pk_duel_skill.why: Only usable input for the influencer penalty duel.

soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.label: Joint distribution of tournament placings from a full group-and-bracket simulation
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.mechanism: Union, exact-order and any-group-winner contracts are functions of the joint placings of many teams, which bracket structure makes dependent.
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.rationale: Summing marginal title odds is right only for disjoint unions; exact orders (KXWCFINISHINGORDER, KXWCGROUPORDER) and 'any nation of a set wins its group' need the joint draw, and group-mates are negatively correlated. Tiebreak rules and the best-third-place allocation make the dependence discrete and non-trivial.
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.measurement: Monte Carlo of the full competition (N>=200,000 draws) from current team ratings with posterior rating draws per simulation, official group composition, FIFA/UEFA tiebreak order, best-third allocation table and bracket; store per draw each team's placing (group rank, stage reached, final placing 1-4); contract probabilities are frequencies of the defining event; rerun at each as-of time after every match day.
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.why: KXWCTEAMH2H (including its same-stage leg) and KXWCBESTHOST ($1/N dead heat) are functions of the joint stage-reached vector of the compared teams, which group and bracket structure make dependent.

soc.paired_team_correlation.reason: Core to head-to-head: variance of the points difference is determined by the covariance of the two totals, and this is derived from the same simulation; keep but define the covariance structure explicitly.

soc.comp_sim.reason: The season Monte Carlo is the model; it needs the extra state inputs above to be exercised properly.

soc.ratings_uncertainty.reason: Posterior width widens the gap distribution; secondary because it only changes tails and the head-to-head comparison relies on the mean difference.

soc.remaining_schedule_strength.reason: The asymmetry in the two teams' remaining opponents is a first-order driver of expected final gap.

soc.injuries.reason: Season-long availability matters for key players; short-term vintages are irrelevant for a season-end contract.

soc.squad_depth_value.reason: Useful modulator of injury cost, but with weak historical evidence of effect size on points.

soc.tiebreaker_rules.reason: The tie branch can decide the contract when points are level; rule differs by league (head-to-head vs goal difference).

m.rules_text.reason: Needed to know whether the contract settles on final table, deductions and date; not a predictor.

m.external_lines.reason: Outright and match prices are market-derived benchmarks; use for calibration comparison, not as an input.

soc.xg.reason: xG separates luck from skill in points so far; its value is through the rating, not as a standalone feature.

soc.motivation.reason: Stakes leverage matters for dead rubbers, but is itself a function of the season simulation; use as modulator on rotation not as a direct feature.

interactions.mechanism: P(leader holds) follows a normal tail in gap divided by sqrt(remaining fixtures times variance per match times (1 - rho)); correlation lowers the denominator, so the same gap gives a higher hold probability when the teams' results are positively correlated.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit hold probability on gap/sqrt(n_left) with and without a correlation term; compare Brier.

interactions.mechanism: A remaining direct meeting is worth six points of swing; when the gap is at most three points it makes the meeting a decider, when the gap exceeds six it becomes irrelevant, so the effect of the meeting is conditional on the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast outcomes by presence of a remaining meeting and gap bucket (0-3, 4-6, 7+).

interactions.mechanism: A shared European schedule hurts a thin squad far more than a deep one, so the relative strength shift is proportional to overlap times (1 - depth quality), generating gap changes of of unestimated size in the congested window (a hypothesis, not a measured effect).
interactions.how_to_test: Regress points-per-game change over congested windows on depth and overlap.

interactions.mechanism: Only on paths with equal final points does goal difference or head-to-head matter, so the tie rule has weight near the zero-point gap and none far from it; the effect is piecewise and depends on the league's order.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate final tables with each tiebreak order and see how often the order changes the 'ahead' label.

interactions.mechanism: Uncertainty in each team's strength persists over all remaining fixtures (it is not averaged away), so the strength part of the gap sd grows linearly in games remaining while only the match-noise part grows with sqrt (variance quadratic vs linear), especially when one team has a harder schedule.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated gap variance with fixed versus sampled strengths and backtest interval coverage, separating the n^2 strength term from the n match-noise term.

interactions.mechanism: If both players' teams are likely to exit early, the two tallies concentrate on 0-1 goals and equality is likely; if one team goes deep its player's tally spreads out and equality falls, so the bracket paths drive P(equal) more than the scoring rates.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose simulated P(equal) by the pair of stages reached and compare with an independent-exposure model.

interactions.mechanism: For KXWCTEAMH2H the two teams' stage outcomes are independent only if their bracket paths cannot cross before the final; when they share a group or bracket half, one's progress removes the other's, shifting mass away from 'same stage' at late rounds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare same-stage frequencies for pairs in the same vs different bracket halves in simulations and past tournaments.

interactions.mechanism: Finish-ahead contracts depend on two clubs' rest-of-season points; a club underperforming its rating has a raised dismissal hazard, and a dismissal switches its rating regime for the remaining fixtures, so the pairwise order probability is a mixture over change/no-change paths, mattering most when the two clubs are close and many matches remain.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare finish-order calibration with and without the simulated dismissal branch on seasons with in-season changes among paired clubs.

nonlinearities.shape: Sigmoid in gap divided by sqrt(games left)
nonlinearities.why: Win probability of the race follows a normal-CDF shape: flat when the gap is small relative to the remaining variance and approaching 0 or 1 once the gap exceeds about 2 sd.

nonlinearities.shape: Variance grows quadratically (sd linearly) with horizon through the persistent latent strength term, plus a linear-in-games match-noise variance
nonlinearities.why: With a persistent latent strength the sd of that component is linear in games remaining (variance quadratic) while the match-noise component has sd proportional to sqrt(games); ignoring the persistent term understates tails early in the season.
