contract.settlement_definition: Season and tournament outcomes, one binary per team or per outcome: champion of a league, cup, conference or tournament ('is the 2026-27 Bundesliga champion'; split-season and playoff leagues per their own format text); top-N table finish ('is a top 6 finisher in the 2026-27 EPL season', 'finishes in the top 8 in the league phase'); group winner (FIFA tiebreaks); trophy counts and trebles over named competitions (KXSOCCERTROPHIES, KXARSENALCUPS 4+, KXSOCCERTREBLE); team-set unions ('a team from Group L wins', 'any host nation', 'a country that has never won', 'a team from Slovak Super Liga wins the Champions League'); exact finishing orders (KXWCFINISHINGORDER 1-4 via final and third-place match, KXWCGROUPORDER with FIFA tiebreaks); and the World Cup third-place match. KXEPLTOP4 settles on whether the club 'qualifies' (even if it then does not compete), not on rank alone. Resolution is the official final table or competition result; no outright text addresses retroactive sanctions.

rules_evidence.quote: is the 2026-27 Bundesliga champion, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: League title contract resolves on the final champion of the named season, one binary per team; tiebreak and playoff mechanics are inherited from the competition's own rules.

rules_evidence.quote: Only trophies won in the La Liga, Copa del Rey, Supercopa de España, and the Champions League count for purposes of this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Trophy count is a sum over named competitions only; domestic League Cup or other trophies do not count, so the joint path across several competitions (not single title odds) is the object.

rules_evidence.quote: is a top 8 finisher in the 2026 Brasileiro Serie A season
rules_evidence.establishes: Top-X markets are rank-threshold events on the final table for different X per league; the tie order at the boundary is not stated in the sampled text.

rules_evidence.quote: This will be determined by whether or not they qualify; if they qualify but do not end up competing, the market will still resolve to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The EPL Top 4 series is a qualification event: a fifth-placed club that qualifies through an extra European slot could plausibly resolve YES, so slot allocation, not rank alone, defines it.

rules_evidence.quote: 3rd Place Team: 3rd Place Match Winner 4th Place Team: 3rd Place Match Loser
rules_evidence.establishes: The finishing-order contract is a joint event over the final and the third-place match, needing the joint distribution of four placings rather than marginal title odds.

rules_evidence.quote: If a team from Group L wins the 2026 Men's FIFA World Cup
rules_evidence.establishes: Group-of-winner contracts are unions of team title events, so they are sums of disjoint team probabilities with group-mates' bracket dependence.

rules_evidence.quote: Winning one or more of these competitions counts toward this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Trophy-count ladders count titles across four named competitions, so the joint distribution of one club's titles is required.

rules_evidence.quote: If any host nation (USA, Mexico, Canada) wins the 2026 Men's FIFA World Cup
rules_evidence.establishes: The host-win series is a union over three named hosts settling on the tournament winner, so it belongs in the joint-finish stage with host advantage applied.

variants_and_edge_cases: Split-season leagues (Argentina Torneo Clausura, Paraguay APF Clausura, Uruguay, Liga MX liguilla, MLS Cup): 'champion' is the playoff or half-season winner, so table position converts to the title through a bracket or short tournament, not points alone.

Single-elimination cups and World Cup/Copa/Asian Cup outrights: one binary per team across several rounds with extra time and penalties (penalty shootout winner advances), so the settlement event is the final's winner, not 90-minute results.

Top-N series (KXEPLTOP, KXEPLTOP2, KXEPLTOP6, KXLALIGATOP4, KXSERIEATOP4, KXLIGUE1TOP4, KXBUNDESLIGATOP4, KXLIGAMXTOP, KXUCLTOP8, KXUCLTOP) settle on final rank, except KXEPLTOP4 whose secondary text makes it a qualification event; the tie order at the cut is the league's official tiebreak.

Union and order contracts: KXWCGROUPWINNER, KXUCLLEAGUE, KXWCCONTINENT, KXWCNOEURSA, KXWCHOSTWIN and KXWC1STTIMEWIN pay if any team of a named set wins (continent defined by qualification pathway, not geography); KXWCWINGROUP pays if any nation of a set wins its group; KXWCFINISHINGORDER and KXWCGROUPORDER need an exact permutation.

108 live series (ledger count after KXAFCCL2GAME was re-filed to match_result_3way and KXWCFINALMATCHUP to unreg:tournament_bracket_composition), 99 with rules text; 9 without rules text (e.g. KXWCWINMARGIN, KXWC3RDPLACE, KXUCL16, KXUCL8, KXUEL16TWEVIK, KXUSOPENCUP, KXEGYPL). Points deductions, voided seasons and retroactive title stripping are not addressed in any outright text.

Single-match residuals: KXWC3RDPLACE is the third-place match winner (presumably including extra time and penalties; not stated); KXWCWINMARGIN (NO_LISTING; title 'World Cup Winning Margin', Kalshi scope 'Winning Margin') has unknown settlement and is not asserted to be the final's margin. KXAFCCL2GAME (a regulation match-result contract) and KXWCFINALMATCHUP (a bracket-composition contract) were re-filed out of this key and are no longer priced here. Stage s8 covers the two remaining residuals provisionally.

Ecuador LigaPro (KXECULP) carries regular-season points into a hexagonal decided on total points, Peru (KXPERLIGA1) uses Apertura/Clausura and playoff stages, and Venezuela (KXVENFUTVE) a final between half-season winners, so 'champion' differs by league beyond the Argentine/Paraguayan/Uruguayan cases; KXSOCCERTROPHIES also counts a Supercopa de Espana mini-tournament. The Manchester City-type retroactive-sanction case is the reviewer's judgement, not rules text (see retroactive_sanctions).
contract.settlement_data_source: Final official league table or tournament result published by the governing body (league, UEFA, CONMEBOL, FIFA); trophy counts rely on the named competitions' official results; whether later sanctions retroactively change the champion is not stated.

series_mapping_issues.issue: No rules text (NO_LISTING). Kalshi metadata: title 'World Cup Winning Margin', scope 'Winning Margin', template SOCCERWINMARGIN; settlement unknown (not asserted to be the final's margin). Sibling KX*WINMARGIN series in other sports are per-game margin-bucket markets, so a match-margin contract is the better-supported reading; filing under uncertainty, recommended re-file to handicap_and_exact_score once the buckets are known.

mechanism.summary: A competition outright is a sum over scenarios of a latent strength vector, a schedule and a format. Strength is uncertain and drifts; the remaining matches are sampled to produce a joint table; the title, top-N finish or group placing is then read from the sampled tables, with the format converting table position into a champion in split-season and knockout competitions (bracket paths, extra time, shootouts). Multi-competition clubs trade league points for cup progress, and trophy-count contracts need the joint path. Top-N series read the rank against a cut line, and union, exact-order and group contracts need the joint placings of many teams from one tournament simulation. Administrative shocks (deductions, voided seasons) and the definition of the competition-season complete the chain.

stages.name: Team strength and its uncertainty
stages.description: A title or top-N probability starts from each contender's current attack/defence strength, with opponent and venue adjustment and a preseason prior when the season is young. The posterior width matters as much as the mean: two teams with equal means but different uncertainty have different title odds because the maximum of several uncertain totals favours the wider one.
stages.distribution: Posterior distribution of latent strength per team (approx normal on log goal rate); drift over the season via a random walk.

stages.name: Remaining-fixture simulation and table race
stages.description: Points accumulate through 3-outcome matches whose probabilities come from the goal model; the table is a sampled joint outcome across all teams, so title or top-N probabilities are obtained by counting sampled tables. Fixture difficulty and the home/away order of the remaining games differ by team and are the main deterministic asymmetry among contenders.
stages.distribution: Count of table outcomes from a Monte Carlo sum of draws/win/loss lotteries per team; title is argmax of the points vector with tie rule.

stages.name: Competition format conversion
stages.description: Where the title is not the table leader (split seasons, liguilla playoffs, MLS Cup, World Cup knockouts, two-leg ties), a team's table position is converted to the title by a bracket with seeding, home advantage in legs and a penalty-shootout lottery, so the format-specific path probability, not strength alone, sets the price; a one-match final with extra time and penalties compresses strength differences toward 50%.
stages.distribution: Sequence of binary knockout events with win probability for the favourite to be estimated per format (roughly 0.55-0.75 is a hypothesis); product of path probabilities, dominated by bracket draw luck for the elite.

stages.name: Squad shocks, transfers and priority across competitions
stages.description: Over months, key injuries, winter transfer activity, a manager change and the weighting of the league against cups and European competition move strength; a team still alive in several competitions rotates more, lowering league points per game, and this trade-off differs by club ambition. Trophy-count contracts require the joint path across several competitions.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed multi-month strength shifts; correlated across competitions through a shared squad-fatigue state.

stages.name: Rank thresholds and the density at the cut line
stages.description: For top-N series the random variable is the team's final rank relative to N: it depends on the N-th highest points total against the team's own, so the number of rivals within a few points of the cut and the official tiebreak at equal points matter more than the team's average rank. KXUCLTOP and KXUCLTOP8 apply the same logic to the 36-team league phase, and KXEPLTOP4's qualification wording adds the chance that an extra slot reaches fifth place. soc.tiebreaker_rules encodes the static slot-allocation rule; soc.european_slot_spillover adds only the simulated probability that a domestic cup winner already holds a higher slot, which moves the effective cut line.
stages.distribution: Rank of a correlated points vector; P(top-N) is steep (near 0 or 1) for teams far from the cut and most uncertain for teams within about one match of points.

stages.name: Settlement and administrative events
stages.description: Contracts resolve on the final official table or competition result; points deductions, expulsions, cancelled seasons or retroactive title stripping change who is champion after the last whistle, and ambiguous Clausura/Apertura naming requires the exact competition-season definition in the market.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete administrative events (a few percent of league seasons across world football) layered on the sporting outcome.

stages.name: Team-set unions, exact orders and group outcomes from the joint tournament draw
stages.description: Many World Cup and UCL series are functions of the whole simulated tournament rather than one team's title: unions over a named set (group, confederation by qualification pathway, host nations, first-time winners, league of origin) sum disjoint title probabilities, while exact orders (top four via final and third-place match, a group's 1-4 order under FIFA tiebreaks) and 'any nation of a set wins its group' need the joint distribution of placings, because group-mates and bracket neighbours cannot both progress. Marginal title odds are insufficient; the correlation induced by the bracket and shared groups must be kept. Host-nation unions (KXWCHOSTWIN: any of USA, Mexico, Canada wins) need soc.home_advantage set on for each host's matches played in its own country and zero for neutral-venue matches, so the hosts' group and knockout probabilities carry the host edge before summing their disjoint title probabilities.
stages.distribution: Multinomial over permutations from a joint Monte Carlo of groups and bracket; exact-order outcomes have small probabilities (often below 2%) and are sensitive to tiebreak modelling.

stages.name: Single-match residuals inside the outright key (provisional filing)
stages.description: Two series are filed here provisionally because they have no rules text (basis NO_LISTING) and are decided by one match or an unknown bucket scheme. KXWC3RDPLACE: the third-place match (two beaten semi-finalists, motivation and rotation uncertain; whether extra time and penalties count is not stated). KXWCWINMARGIN: title 'World Cup Winning Margin', Kalshi scope 'Winning Margin', template SOCCERWINMARGIN; its settlement is unknown and it is NOT assumed to be the final's margin; if it follows sibling KX*WINMARGIN series it is a per-match goal-margin bucket contract (a re-file to handicap_and_exact_score is recommended once the buckets are known). Both need the match goal model, not the season simulation: the signed regulation goal difference comes from the joint goal-count distribution soc.goal_dist (soc.winning_margin_distribution was audited a DUPLICATE of it and is retired), fed by the two opponent-adjusted intensities; the extra-time and shootout branch applies only where a series settles on advancing. KXAFCCL2GAME and KXWCFINALMATCHUP were previously priced here and have been re-filed elsewhere.
stages.distribution: Three-way or margin distribution from two team intensities; extra-time and shootout branch adds near-coin-flip mass for knockout games.

talent_strength.note: Strength with uncertainty and a preseason/promoted-team prior for early-season prices.

opponent_matchup.note: Fixture asymmetry for leagues; bracket opponents for cups.

role_personnel.note: Depth of the 12th-18th players and key-player dependence.

availability_news.note: Season-long availability and window activity; no match-day lineup vintage is needed for outright markets.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager changes and in-season tactical evolution shift a contender's strength, and the true effect size of a sacking or appointment is not estimated in any input here; the existing catalog only flags it inside soc.transfers.

environment.note: Weather and altitude act on single matches and are absorbed by the team's home advantage in the goal model over a whole season; the one environmental exception, neutral-venue finals and tournament host-country effects, is handled by the bracket input, not a separate environment variable.

game_context_script.note: Table state and format determine what each match is worth.

pace_volume.note: Possession and shot volume matter only through the goal-model strengths for a season-long outcome; no volume statistic is a direct determinant of who wins a title or finishes top-N, so it carries no separate input.

efficiency_conversion.note: Luck-versus-skill split is performed inside the rating fit (xG-based goal model with shrinkage) so soc.ratings carries it; soc.xg is audited WEAK and is no longer cited as standalone cover.

distribution_variance.note: Joint placings from the tournament simulation and strength uncertainty give the tail and dependence shape of union and order contracts.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rotation and priority across competitions come from soc.cup_progression_load; soc.motivation is audited KEEP_CONTEXT (circular with the simulation) and is not cited as cover.

officiating_rules.note: Refereeing tendencies average out over a full season and have no systematic effect on title chances; sanctions and deductions are administrative and are covered under points_deductions and settlement.

settlement_contract.note: Tiebreak order, split-season definition, deductions and exact named competitions.

soc.bracket_path_difficulty.label: Knockout bracket path difficulty and seeding
soc.bracket_path_difficulty.mechanism: Opponent sequence and tie format a team faces from the current round to the final.
soc.bracket_path_difficulty.rationale: A cup outright price is the product of round-by-round win probabilities; two teams of equal strength differ materially if one has a bracket with a top-ranked opponent in the quarter-final, and the draw, seeding and one-leg vs two-leg format change per-round variance.
soc.bracket_path_difficulty.measurement: From the official draw: list each possible opponent path with its probability given seeding constraints; P(path) times round win probability w_r = P(win 90) + P(draw) * 0.5 (extra time/penalties, slightly tilted to the stronger side by 0.52-0.55); for two-leg ties compute via aggregate simulation; as-of = after the draw or last completed round.
soc.bracket_path_difficulty.why: Cup and tournament outrights are determined by path, which no existing input in the archetype captures.

soc.playoff_format_conversion.label: Table-position to title conversion for split-season and playoff formats
soc.playoff_format_conversion.mechanism: Probability of winning the title given final-table place under the competition's playoff structure.
soc.playoff_format_conversion.rationale: In Liga MX, MLS, the Clausura/Apertura leagues and some Argentine/Paraguayan formats the champion emerges from a playoff, so a team ranked first after the regular season has a title probability of maybe 25-35% rather than the 80%+ a pure league implies.
soc.playoff_format_conversion.measurement: For each competition-format: historical P(champion | seed rank) estimated over 10+ seasons with Wilson intervals and shrunk to a strength-based model prediction (k=10 seasons); combine with simulated regular-season rank distribution to give P(title) = sum_rank P(rank) * P(champion | rank).
soc.playoff_format_conversion.why: Converts a table simulation to a champion probability in about a third of the leagues in this ledger bucket.

soc.uefa_league_phase_simulation.label: UEFA 36-team league-phase simulation: finishing-rank distribution, top-8 / 9-24 / 25+ outcomes and tiebreakers
soc.uefa_league_phase_simulation.mechanism: Monte Carlo of the 8 league-phase matches per club against four-pot-drawn opponents, giving the distribution of final rank, points and goal difference and hence direct R16 entry, playoff or elimination.
soc.uefa_league_phase_simulation.rationale: The UCL/UEL league phase (36 teams, 8 unequal fixtures, rank 1-8 direct, 9-24 playoff, 25+ out, goal-difference and goals-scored tiebreakers) replaced the group stage from 2024-25, so there is no long history of P(advance | rank); the rank distribution has to be simulated from team strengths and the actual fixed opponent list.
soc.uefa_league_phase_simulation.measurement: From the official draw list the eight opponents and venues per club; per match win/draw/loss from the opponent- and venue-adjusted goal model (soc.ratings, Dixon-Coles) with team strength sampled from its posterior; 20,000 simulated league phases using UEFA tiebreak order (points, goal difference, goals scored, away goals, wins, away wins, opponents points, disciplinary). Output P(rank r) and P(top8), P(9-24), P(25+) per club, as-of after the last played matchday, recomputed after each result.
soc.uefa_league_phase_simulation.why: Supplies the seeding and bracket side for KXUCL16*, KXUEL16*, KXUCL8, KXUCLTOP, KXUCLBOTTOM, KXUCLLEAGUE-type series where table position, not strength alone, decides the stage reached.

soc.seeded_bracket_path_given_finish.label: Seeded bracket path and opponent set conditional on league-phase finishing rank
soc.seeded_bracket_path_given_finish.mechanism: Maps each league-phase finishing rank (or 9-24 playoff pairing) to the possible playoff, R16, quarter and semi opponents, bracket side and tie venues, so P(reach stage) is a product of path probabilities conditional on rank.
soc.seeded_bracket_path_given_finish.rationale: In the new UEFA format rank 1-8 avoid the playoff and sit on fixed bracket lines while 9-24 face a seeded two-leg playoff; the opponent a club can meet in the R16 depends on its finish, so the same strength gives different stage-reach probabilities by finish and stage-markets cannot be priced from a strength rating alone.
soc.seeded_bracket_path_given_finish.measurement: For each simulated league-phase rank, enumerate playoff, R16, QF, SF opponents from the published bracket lines and seeding rules (no away-goals rule). Each two-leg tie: simulate both legs from the Dixon-Coles lambdas with home advantage, ET if aggregate level (lambda*30/90*0.8), then penalties with p = 0.5 + 0.5*(skill_A - skill_B) where skill is the soc.penalty_shootout_skill n/(n+30)-shrunk value; final is single leg neutral. 20000 draws; P(reach stage) = product along path. As-of after each draw/matchday.
soc.seeded_bracket_path_given_finish.why: Needed because UEFA stage-reach series (R16, R8, finalist, advance) are settled by bracket position determined by the league-phase finish.

soc.club_multi_competition_dependence.label: Dependence of one club's league, cup and Champions League title events
soc.club_multi_competition_dependence.mechanism: Joint distribution of a club winning the league, domestic cup(s), Supercopa and the Champions League, driven by shared squad strength, a shared injury/fatigue shock and the schedule trade-off between competitions.
soc.club_multi_competition_dependence.rationale: KXSOCCERTROPHIES counts trophies across La Liga, Copa del Rey, Supercopa de Espana and the Champions League, so its price is a sum of correlated Bernoulli events; treating them as independent misprices count thresholds, and the sign of the correlation is mixed (shared strength positive, fixture overload negative).
soc.club_multi_competition_dependence.measurement: Simulate the four competitions jointly: club strength s ~ N(rating, sd from soc.ratings_uncertainty) shared across competitions, plus a shared availability shock a ~ Beta fitted to the club's historical share of squad-minutes lost (Transfermarkt injury days), reducing attack/defence by 0.1*(a). Compute the pairwise correlation of title indicators from 20000 draws; compare to historical co-occurrence of league+cup and league+UCL doubles over 20 seasons and shrink the simulated correlation toward the historical frequency with weight 10/(10+n_seasons_with_data). As-of after each round.
soc.club_multi_competition_dependence.why: Provides the dependence structure the trophy-count series needs and which no independent per-competition probability can deliver.

soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.label: Joint distribution of tournament placings from a full group-and-bracket simulation
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.mechanism: Union, exact-order and any-group-winner contracts are functions of the joint placings of many teams, which bracket structure makes dependent.
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.rationale: Summing marginal title odds is right only for disjoint unions; exact orders (KXWCFINISHINGORDER, KXWCGROUPORDER) and 'any nation of a set wins its group' need the joint draw, and group-mates are negatively correlated. Tiebreak rules and the best-third-place allocation make the dependence discrete and non-trivial.
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.measurement: Monte Carlo of the full competition (N>=200,000 draws) from current team ratings with posterior rating draws per simulation, official group composition, FIFA/UEFA tiebreak order, best-third allocation table and bracket; store per draw each team's placing (group rank, stage reached, final placing 1-4); contract probabilities are frequencies of the defining event; rerun at each as-of time after every match day.
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.why: Prices team-set unions, exact finishing orders and group outcomes that marginal title odds cannot.

soc.comp_sim.reason: The season simulation is the necessary engine; its value depends on state inputs and format conversion.

soc.ratings_uncertainty.reason: Strength uncertainty widens tails and changes title odds for equal-mean contenders; essential for outrights.

soc.remaining_schedule_strength.reason: Schedule asymmetry among contenders is a deterministic first-order input in the second half of a season.

soc.tiebreaker_rules.reason: Order of tiebreak differs by league and competition and decides narrow title and top-N races, FIFA group winners and exact group orders (KXWCGROUPWIN, KXWCGROUPORDER).

soc.squad_depth_value.reason: Depth helps only in injury-wave scenarios; its effect size on league points is small and confounded with team quality.

soc.cup_progression_load.reason: Priority and rotation across competitions matters for trophy-count and for the league push of Europe-engaged clubs.

soc.injuries.reason: Season-long availability matters for key-player dependence; short-term timestamps are less relevant for outrights.

soc.transfers.reason: Window activity and manager-change flags move strength discretely; coverage of effect size is thin.

soc.points_deductions.reason: Rare but decisive when pending; belongs in settlement more than strength.

soc.preseason_prior.reason: Only matters in the early-season horizon; its value decays to zero as matches accumulate.

m.external_lines.reason: Bookmaker outright prices are a calibration benchmark, not an input to a model intended to find edge; demoted to context in the archetype (roles patch) so the catalog no longer presents it as a primary driver.

m.ladder_structure.reason: The cross-rung monotonicity check is computed on quoted strike prices, so it is market-derived and used only to validate model output across rungs, not as an input to any stage or coverage claim; the nested-event structure itself is taken from m.rules_text.

soc.xg.reason: Used only through ratings; as a stand-alone input it duplicates the rating's data and adds nothing about outright mechanics.

soc.ratings.reason: Goal-model strengths are the engine inputs; need Bayesian decay and league strength links for cross-competition cups.

soc.motivation.reason: Stakes leverage is a derived output of the simulation; its direct use risks circularity.

soc.abandonment_risk.reason: Voided or abandoned seasons are very rare in top leagues but non-zero in lower-profile ledger entries; contractual not predictive.

soc.top_two_order_statistics.reason: First-minus-second points margin distribution served the champion-margin series, which moved to team_points_and_margin (where it is staged in s3); no remaining title, top-N, union or order contract here settles on a points gap.

soc.goal_dist.reason: Stage s8 residuals (KXWCWINMARGIN if it is a match margin, the third-place match) are priced from the joint goal-count distribution; its goals come from the fixtures dataset, not the structure dataset; context only, not a driver of the season simulation.

soc.home_advantage.reason: Used in stage s7 for host-nation series (KXWCHOSTWIN text): a host nation in its own country gets the national home multiplier and none abroad; irrelevant to club title races.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.reason: Supplies the two match intensities for the single-match residuals in stage s8; the season engine itself runs on soc.ratings and soc.comp_sim.

soc.group_stage_scenarios.reason: Group-winner and group-order series need the enumerated group scenarios; it is a derived simulation view feeding stage s7, not an independent measurement.

soc.european_slot_spillover.reason: The catalog flags it DUPLICATE_OF soc.tiebreaker_rules; rebutted in part: tiebreaker_rules holds the static allocation rule, while this input carries only the simulated probability that a cup winner already holds a higher slot (shifting the cut line for KXEPLTOP4-type qualification series), measured from the cup simulation. Its definition is narrowed to that stochastic part (input_audit/SOCCER_zblk.json); context only.

soc.extra_time_shootout_model.reason: Used in stage s8 only for the third-place match and any knockout residual that settles on advancing; irrelevant to league titles, top-N and unions.

interactions.mechanism: For promoted or rebuilt clubs the preseason prior fixes the posterior mean while its width sets the tails: early in the season title odds of a mid-ranked contender are convex in prior width, and the prior weight fades as matches accumulate, so the interaction is large in the first third of a season and near zero afterwards (hypothesis on timing).
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest title and top-N calibration by matchweek bucket with prior sd inflated versus fixed, and compare Brier score in the first ten matchweeks.

interactions.mechanism: Whether the table converts to a champion by points or by playoff regime switches the sensitivity of title odds to regular-season strength; in playoff leagues rank 1 vs rank 4 differ by only a few percentage points while in pure leagues they differ by tens.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(champion | rank) by format and compare with a points-only prediction.

interactions.mechanism: Cup and European progress costs league points in proportion to how thin the squad is: deep clubs rotate with little loss, thin ones lose several points of league expectation per extra competition round, so load times (1 - depth) predicts league slippage.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress league PPG deviation on congested-week count times squad depth over past seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Cup outright odds are conditional on the draw: after the draw is made the same ratings produce different outright prices, and the effect is largest for strong teams drawn into the same quarter.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare pre- and post-draw price movements to the change in path-difficulty.

interactions.mechanism: Exact group orders and any-nation-wins-group events depend on the joint table, where tiebreak order (head-to-head vs goal difference, fair-play points) decides discrete reorderings; a model with correct marginals but wrong tiebreaks mis-prices permutations far more than single-team group-win odds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated vs realised group-order frequencies in past World Cups with and without the tiebreak module.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex payoff of title odds for non-favourites
nonlinearities.why: Because the champion is the maximum of noisy totals, odds of outsiders rise faster than linearly with posterior width.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in games remaining
nonlinearities.why: Schedule strength has weight proportional to the remaining match count; it is near zero in matchweek 5 and large after matchweek 30, so effect is not linear in the strength score.

nonlinearities.shape: Product-like decay for exact orders
nonlinearities.why: An exact 1-2-3-4 order is roughly a product of conditional probabilities, so small errors in each team's rating compound multiplicatively and the contract is extremely sensitive at low prices.

contract.settlement_definition: YES settles on goals scored within one half only. Winner/Tie texts (e.g. KXEPL1H, KXSERIEA2H, KXUEFASC2H) judge the half 'after 45 minutes plus stoppage time', and a 0-0 or equal half resolves 'Tie'; total texts ('more than N goals in the 1st Half') and spread texts ('win by more than N goals in the 1st Half') say only that goals scored during the half count; 1st-half correct-score texts ('the score at the end of the 1st Half is A 3, B 2') carry no secondary clause at all. Total, spread and winner texts resolve to a fair price if the game is cancelled or rescheduled more than 48 hours away (two weeks for the six World Cup half series KXWC1H, KXWC2H, KXWC1HTOTAL, KXWC2HTOTAL, KXWC1HSPREAD, KXWC2HSPREAD); strikes are x.5 'more than' so no pushes exist. No half text mentions own goals (credit to the beneficiary is presumed, not stated). 177 of 216 series have text; 39 are TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: If no goals are scored during the half, or the teams score an equal number of goals in the half, then the market called "Tie" resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: A 0-0 half and any equal-score half both resolve Tie, so the draw probability for a half is much higher (about 40-45%) than for the full match and is anchored by P(0-0 half).

rules_evidence.quote: Only goals scored during the 2nd Half count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: 2H markets are computed on second-half goals only, independent of the half-time score; the 2H goal rate depends on half-time score state.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is cancelled or rescheduled to over 48 hours away, the market will resolve to a fair price in accordance with the rules.
rules_evidence.establishes: Postponement beyond 48 hours settles to fair price, not No; abandonment inside the half is not addressed in the sampled text.

rules_evidence.quote: after 45 minutes plus stoppage time
rules_evidence.establishes: Period is 45 minutes plus that half's stoppage time for the winner/Tie text; first-half and second-half added time differ in length so exposure differs by half (typical lengths are not sourced here).

rules_evidence.quote: rescheduled to over two weeks away, the market will resolve to a fair price
rules_evidence.establishes: World Cup half series use a two-week postponement window instead of the 48-hour window used by club half series.

rules_evidence.quote: If Tie is the result of the second half in the PSG vs Aston Villa professional UEFA Super Cup soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: A cup final's 2nd Half winner market is defined as the second 45 minutes plus stoppage, so extra time is outside the winner/Tie window even in a one-off final.

variants_and_edge_cases: Second-half contracts are conditional-in-state: the 2H goal rate depends on the half-time score (leader parks, trailing side chases), yet the contract ignores the half-time score itself; 1H and 2H are therefore correlated through state, not independent halves of a Poisson.

First-half exact-score ladder (KXMLS1HSCORE, KXLIGUE11HSCORE) is a custom strike set of mutually exclusive scores with mass concentrated on 0-0, 1-0, 0-1, 1-1; tail scores like 3-2 in a half are rare, so the ladder is dominated by Dixon-Coles low-cell structure.

Half spread 'wins by more than 1.5 goals' (KXBUNDESLIGA1HSPREAD, KXUCL1HSPREAD) needs a 2-0+ half lead, a rare event (about 5-8% for a strong favourite), so estimates are sensitive to the tail of the half goal distribution.

216 live series, 177 with rules text (half winner/Tie, half totals, half spreads, first-half exact score); 39 are TITLE_ONLY, including the 8 residual half-BTTS series still filed here (KXCOUPEDEFRANCE1HBTTS, KXCONCACAFCCUP1HBTTS, KXCLUBWC1HBTTS, KXAFCAC1HBTTS, KXITASUPERCUP1HBTTS, KXESPSUPERCUP1HBTTS, KXFACUP2HBTTS, KXCLUBWC2HBTTS); the other 56 half-BTTS series moved to btts_and_clean_sheet.

Cup half series (KXTACAPORT1H, KXUSOPENCUP1HTOTAL, KXFACUP2H, KXUEFASC2HTOTAL): the winner/Tie texts fix the 2nd Half at 45 minutes plus stoppage, but the 2H total and spread texts only say 'goals scored during the 2nd Half', so whether extra-time goals could count there is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.
First-half correct-score series (KXMLS1HSCORE, KXWC1HSCORE) have no secondary text: neither a postponement clause nor an 'any other score' rung is visible.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official match report goal events with minute (goal minute and period as recorded by the league/Kalshi data provider, with 45+N counted as first half and 90+N as second half); own-goal credit is not stated in any half text and is presumed to follow the beneficiary.

mechanism.summary: A half contract counts goals scored inside one 45-minute period (plus that period's stoppage), so the outcome is a low-count process derived from full-match team intensities scaled by the team's own first/second half profile. The first half is shaped by cautious starts and a shorter stoppage, so 0-0 and 1-1 dominate and draw probability for a half is high; the second half depends on the half-time score through the trailing team's chase and the leader's retreat, so the halves are correlated through state. Dependence among low cells, lineup quality and the added-time minutes of the referee complete the chain, and settlement counts only that half's goals with fair-price resolution if the match is moved.

stages.name: Full-match scoring rates
stages.description: The per-half rates are a fraction of the match's two team intensities, so the full-match opponent-adjusted lambdas, the confirmed lineup and any xG-based ratings come first. For a half-spread of 2+ goals the favourite's lambda dominates; for a half total of 0.5 the sum of both lambdas does.
stages.distribution: Poisson-like team counts over the match; half contributions are thinned sub-samples with overdispersion due to state.

stages.name: Time profile of scoring across halves
stages.description: About 44-46% of goals arrive in the first half and 54-56% in the second, driven by fatigue, substitutions, tactical commitment when trailing, and longer second-half stoppage. A cautious opening raises P(0-0 at half-time), and team style (pressing intensity early, deep block) changes the split; the first-half share also varies by competition (heat, schedule) and kickoff time. Kickoff heat, humidity and altitude (soc.weather) can lower second-half intensity relative to the first, shifting the 2H share of lambda downward in hot afternoon or high-altitude venues (Liga MX at Toluca/Mexico City, summer Brasileiro, the 2026 World Cup afternoon slots); the sign is expected but the size is unestablished.
stages.distribution: Time-inhomogeneous intensity, roughly increasing across the match; team-level share varies with a heavy shrinkage to the league (sd about 4 percentage points).

stages.name: Within-half low-count dependence
stages.description: Half totals are small numbers (mean about 1.2), so joint outcomes concentrate on 0-0, 1-0, 0-1 and 1-1; draw probability for a half is far larger than a Poisson implies because early cagey play and equalising dynamics couple the sides. The relevant dependence parameter is half-level, not the full-match Dixon-Coles rho.
stages.distribution: Bivariate low-count distribution with draw inflation; half draw rate about 40-45%; tail beyond 2 goals each is thin.

stages.name: Second-half state and conditional rates
stages.description: For second-half markets the half-time score matters: the trailing side's attack rate rises, the leading side's falls, substitutions arrive around minute 60, and a first-half red card alters everything. The 2H total is therefore a function of the 1H result, which plausibly creates dependence between halves whose sign by match type is a hypothesis to be tested, not an established fact.
stages.distribution: Conditional intensity multipliers by half-time margin (sizes such as +25% trailing or -15% for a two-goal leader are unsourced hypotheses to estimate), plus discrete red-card shocks.

stages.name: Stoppage, officials and settlement
stages.description: Added time (in minutes) and VAR delays extend each half's exposure and differ by half and referee; second-half stoppage is typically longer than first-half stoppage (lengths to be measured). Settlement uses the half's regulation 45+ stoppage and ignores the other half, with fair-price resolution for postponements in the winner, total and spread texts (48 hours, two weeks for World Cup series); first-half correct-score texts have no such clause.
stages.distribution: Added time per half is a small discrete variable (1-3 min in the first half, 4-8 in the second); goal rate per minute times added minutes shifts expected goals by about 0.03 to 0.15.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted full-match strengths with luck regressed supply the base rates for both halves; raw soc.xg is audited DUPLICATE_OF soc.xg_adjusted_ratings and is not cited.

opponent_matchup.note: Teams that start fast against high-line sides versus those that finish strong create a half-specific matchup.

role_personnel.note: Starting XI sets first-half quality; the substitute bench matters for second-half intensity.

availability_news.note: Lineup vintage at about 60 minutes pre-kickoff; late changes are decisive for first-half rate.

coaching_scheme.note: Managers' substitution timing and chase/park behaviour determine the half-specific rates.

environment.note: Heat, humidity and altitude at kickoff shifting the second-half share of the full-match lambda.

game_context_script.note: Score-state response and half-time score give the conditional 2H rate.

pace_volume.note: Tempo and territory determine volume of attempts per half; corners proxy early pressure.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing luck is regressed so that a hot-streak team is not priced as a high-scoring first half.

distribution_variance.note: Half-level draw inflation and low-cell dependence shape the exact score and Tie markets.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Stakes and congestion alter rotation and half-time effort; modelled through the state multiplier and the lineups.

officiating_rules.note: Referee added-time habits set exposure minutes in each half and the referee/VAR penalty and red-card propensity drives the discrete first-half shocks named in stage s4.

settlement_contract.note: Half-only goal counting, Tie rule and fair-price clause; the ladder across half-strikes must be monotone.

soc.half_specific_xg_ratings.label: Half-specific attack and defence ratings
soc.half_specific_xg_ratings.mechanism: Separate xG creation and concession rates for the first and second half.
soc.half_specific_xg_ratings.rationale: A single full-match rating hides that some teams are strong starters (high press early, fresh legs) and weak finishers, and vice versa; first-half markets need first-half strengths, which differ from full-match by up to 20% for extreme styles. It overlaps soc.period_split and soc.first_goal_hazard (all three describe how scoring is spread over the match); the team-level deviation from the league 1H share is small, so this input is a shrunk correction, not a standalone primary.
soc.half_specific_xg_ratings.measurement: For each team: xG for/against in minutes 1-45+ and 46-90+ per 45 minutes, opponent-adjusted with a ridge regression log(xG_half) ~ attack_i + defence_j + home + half, 30-match window half-life 15, shrink half-effect to the league 1H/2H ratio with k=20 matches; output a 1H multiplier m_1H_team in [0.7,1.3].
raw_data: shot-level xG with minute and team
soc.half_specific_xg_ratings.why: Gives the first-half and second-half lambdas their own team-level scaling rather than a fixed league 45/55 split.

soc.second_half_state_multiplier.label: Second-half scoring multipliers conditional on half-time score and cards
soc.second_half_state_multiplier.mechanism: Multipliers on each side's second-half goal rate given the half-time margin and numerical parity.
soc.second_half_state_multiplier.rationale: Second-half markets are state-conditional: teams trailing by one raise output by 20-30% and leaders drop 10-20%, and a red card swings rates by roughly 30%; the 2H total depends on how the first half unfolded.
soc.second_half_state_multiplier.measurement: From league event data: for margin m in {-2,-1,0,+1,+2}, estimate goals per 45 for each side in the second half relative to expectation from pre-match lambda (Poisson regression with offset log(lambda_match*share_2H)), by favourite/underdog; shrink to league effect with k=200 half-minutes; include 10-man indicator at halftime.
soc.second_half_state_multiplier.why: Provides the conditional structure for 2H markets and for combining first-half simulations with second-half rates.

soc.half_level_dependence_rho.label: Half-level Dixon-Coles dependence and draw inflation
soc.half_level_dependence_rho.mechanism: Dependence parameters fitted on half-time scores rather than full-time scores.
soc.half_level_dependence_rho.rationale: Full-match rho does not carry over to half scores, where 0-0 and 1-1 cells are heavy; using the full-time rho misprices the half draw and half exact-score ladder.
soc.half_level_dependence_rho.measurement: Fit a bivariate Poisson/Dixon-Coles with draw-inflation parameter (and separate rho_1H, rho_2H) to half scores per league on 5 seasons (weights exp(-0.002 per day)); report profile-likelihood intervals; as-of = prior matches only.
raw_data: half-time and full-time scores per match
soc.half_level_dependence_rho.why: The Tie and exact-score ladders for halves are controlled by these parameters.

soc.period_split.reason: Share of goals per half is the scaling factor, but team-level sd around the league share is only a few percentage points with heavy shrinkage; it overlaps soc.half_specific_xg_ratings (its team/opponent-conditioned form) and soc.first_goal_hazard, so it is demoted from primary to secondary.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.reason: Provides base lambdas; half-specific ratings are needed on top.

soc.dixon_coles_low_score.reason: Full-match rho is misleading for half scores; use half-level fit (new input) instead.

soc.draw_propensity.reason: Team draw effects carry some persistence, but the half draw is largely structural (low counts), so the weight is small.

soc.first_goal_hazard.reason: Opening-period hazard measures the same time profile as soc.period_split and the half-specific ratings; it is kept only as a context check and to build the HT-margin distribution, not as an independent driver.

soc.pace_press.reason: Style indicator for early pressing and territory; overlaps partially with half-specific xG.

soc.xi_strength_delta.reason: Starting XI drives first-half quality; less weight in 2H where substitutes matter.

soc.score_state.reason: Not pregame; used to estimate the 2H multiplier input.

soc.added_time.reason: Adds a few percent of exposure per half; small but systematic difference between halves.

m.rules_text.reason: Needed to know half-only counting and fair-price clause; not predictive.

m.ladder_structure.reason: The cross-rung monotonicity check is computed on quoted strike prices, so it is market-derived and used only to validate model output across rungs, not as an input to any stage or coverage claim; the nested-event structure itself is taken from m.rules_text.

soc.xg.reason: Raw xG for/against feeds the adjusted ratings; keeping both double counts team chance creation.

soc.lineups_pit.reason: Confirmed XI matters but is less decisive for halves than for full match; still the key late update.

soc.corners.reason: Corners are a downstream count of pressure; correlation with half goals is weak once xG is in and it is not a causal driver.

soc.finishing_regression.reason: Shrinkage of lucky finishing stops overreaction in small half samples.

soc.weather.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on soc.weather x soc.period_split: Above a heat-index or altitude threshold the second half loses intensity (fewer high-intensity runs, more drin; stage s2) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

soc.penalty_rate.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s4) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: The second-half rate depends on the half-time margin and on who was favoured: a favourite trailing at the break lifts output strongly, while an underdog leading drops it, so the effect has opposite signs by role.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress 2H goals on HT margin interacted with pre-match favourite status; compare residuals.

interactions.mechanism: High-press teams front-load their chances; pairing a high-press side with a deep-block opponent (proxied by the opponent's PPDA and territory, since line height itself is not in free data) raises first-half expected goals more than the sum of the parts.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit 1H goals on pressing intensity interacted with the opponent PPDA/deep-block proxy; line height needs a tracking-data provider and is not available free.

interactions.mechanism: An early first-half goal produces the half-time margin that then selects the second-half multiplier: the opening-period hazard determines which state regime the 2H starts in, so P(2H total over 1.5) differs by who scored first and when (direction: a favourite conceding first lifts 2H output, an underdog scoring first lowers it).
interactions.how_to_test: Condition 2H goal counts on first-goal minute bucket and scorer favouredness, and compare with a model that uses only the HT margin.

interactions.mechanism: A long first-half delay (VAR checks, injuries) adds exposure minutes: the extra time scales the half's expected goals proportionally (roughly one minute per 1/45 of the half rate; the size of a typical delay is to be measured) and matters most for close 0.5 total strikes.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast 1H goals per minute vs added time buckets.

interactions.mechanism: Late lineup news (a missing first-choice striker) affects the opening-period rate more than the match average, because replacements need time and bench players are used later; the effect is conditional on the half.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare 1H vs 2H goals by lineup-change indicator.

interactions.mechanism: Above a heat-index or altitude threshold the second half loses intensity (fewer high-intensity runs, more drinks-break pauses), so the first-half share of goals rises and 1H totals/1H BTTS gain probability relative to the full-match lambda; in temperate sea-level matches the split is unchanged.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress the second-half share of goals on kickoff heat index and venue altitude with league and kickoff-hour fixed effects, pooled over multiple seasons.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating: 1H share bounded about 0.35-0.55
nonlinearities.why: Team shares shrink heavily to the league mean; the response of half lambda to the raw observed share is strongly sublinear because of small samples.

nonlinearities.shape: Asymmetric and piecewise in HT margin
nonlinearities.why: A one-goal margin changes rates by about 20% but a three-goal margin does not change them further (garbage time), so the multiplier saturates beyond 2.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear in added minutes with small slope
nonlinearities.why: Each extra minute of exposure adds about 1/45 of the half's expected goals, but late-minute urgency makes second-half minutes denser.

Where extra time exists it lowers P(no goal) relative to a regulation-only window.

mechanism.summary: A First-Team-To-Score contract is a competing-risk race between two time-varying scoring intensities with a no-goal outcome. The relative intensity (opponent-adjusted attack versus defence, home or neutral venue, confirmed XI) sets who is favoured; the early-minute hazard shape and the route mix (set pieces and penalties are over-represented among early goals) move the race beyond the simple lambda share; and the window length decides the no-goal mass: 90 minutes plus stoppage in league fixtures, up to 120 minutes where the competition plays extra time, which competitions do so is an unverified rule table here. Settlement (entire-game window, own-goal credit, listed No Goal outcome) is verified from 23 texts; abandonment and postponement handling is unstated.

stages.name: Relative scoring intensities of the two sides
stages.description: Each side's goal intensity for the match comes from opponent-adjusted xG attack and defence ratings, the venue (full home multiplier at a club ground, near zero at neutral finals such as the World Cup final or super cups abroad) and the confirmed XI. The ratio lambda_A/(lambda_A+lambda_B) is the first-order probability of scoring first given at least one goal, and the sum sets how fast the race ends. Kickoff heat, humidity and altitude (Liga MX, AFC and some qualifier venues) can lower both intensities and the early-goal hazard, so soc.weather enters as a context multiplier.
stages.distribution: Two positive rates per match; their ratio drives the race share and their sum the no-goal mass via exp(-total x exposure).

stages.name: First-goal timing hazard and route
stages.description: The relevant process is the competing-risk race between the two sides' scoring intensities in minutes: P(team A first) = integral of lambda_A(t) exp(-(lambda_A+lambda_B) t) dt over the exposure window, so the stronger attacker wins with about lambda_A/(lambda_A+lambda_B) at first order, adjusted by timing hazards and each side's opening-period caution. Early goals come disproportionately from set pieces and penalties. The no-goal leg is the joint 0-0 cell, taken from the same joint goal-count model soc.goal_dist (with the Dixon-Coles correction) that the sibling match-result, totals and BTTS prices use, so the FTTS no-goal price and those prices cannot disagree; both team markets resolve No on 0-0. The length of the window is set in stage s3.
stages.distribution: Competing hazards with time-varying intensity; first-goal minute is right-skewed (early-minute peak to be fitted, not assumed); P(no goal) is the 0-0 cell of the joint model over the exposure window and is larger in cup ties with a shorter-scoring posture (unsourced prior, to be measured).

stages.name: Race window: regulation only or with extra time
stages.description: The FTTS window is the entire game, so its length depends on the competition-season rule. League fixtures stop at 90 plus stoppage. For cups, super cups, playoffs and tournaments the extra-time rule per competition-season is UNVERIFIED in this record (no regulation text fetched): exposure is a mixture of 90 and 120 minutes weighted by the unknown rule, never an assumed zero (this applies to KXUEFASCFTTS and KXGERSCFTTS in particular). P(no goal) = P(0-0 at 90) x P(no ET goal | ET played) where extra time exists; the ET hazard is the reduced tired-play rate, and in second legs the aggregate state changes how both sides attack from the first minute. soc.knockout_cagey_factor only scales both hazards in cup ties and is context here, not a primary FTTS driver.
stages.distribution: Mixture over exposure 90 or 120 minutes weighted by P(level at 90) and the competition rule (rule unverified for cups and super cups); knockout caution scales both hazards down.

stages.name: Settlement mapping
stages.description: The contract maps the official goal log to one outcome: the team credited with the first goal (an own goal is credited to the team awarded it, so the opponent's defensive errors are part of each side's hazard), or the listed No Goal outcome if nothing is scored before the shootout. Whether a VAR-disallowed goal counts is an UNVERIFIED assumption (none of the 23 FTTS rules texts mentions VAR; the official goal log is assumed to exclude disallowed goals); a goal scored in extra time counts only where extra time is played. Abandonment after a first goal is not covered by any sampled FTTS text.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the official match record; outcome set of three exclusive legs.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted strengths and venue effects determine regulation result and the first-scorer race.

opponent_matchup.note: Matchup between set-piece attack and defence matters for early goals.

role_personnel.note: Starting forwards and keepers; deep benches for extra time.

availability_news.note: Lineup news before a knockout game; suspensions after yellow-card accumulation.

coaching_scheme.note: Cup-knockout risk posture and aggregate-aware tactics lower or raise both early hazards.

environment.note: Kickoff heat, humidity and altitude shift both scoring intensities and the early-goal hazard in hot or high venues (Liga MX, AFC, qualifiers); the size of the effect is not measured here.

game_context_script.note: Early-goal timing and the extra-time extension of the race window in cup ties.

pace_volume.note: Shot volume and tempo enter only through the opponent-adjusted xG attack/defence ratings and the first-goal hazard; stand-alone soc.pace_press and soc.shots are audited WEAK for scoring-order races and are no longer cited as cover.

efficiency_conversion.note: Penalty awards and set-piece conversion as early first-goal routes.

distribution_variance.note: Low-score dependence for the no-goal leg and the right-skewed first-goal minute.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Aggregate leads and the incentive structure of two-leg ties.

officiating_rules.note: Referee and VAR penalty propensity changes the early-goal route.

settlement_contract.note: Entire-game window, own-goal credit and the listed No Goal leg verified from 23 FTTS texts; abandonment unstated.

soc.knockout_cagey_factor.label: Knockout-stage goal-rate and draw-rate multiplier
soc.knockout_cagey_factor.mechanism: Competition-and-stage multiplier on goals and draws relative to league baselines.
soc.knockout_cagey_factor.rationale: Cup knockouts reduce goals and favourite win rates, and the effect varies by round, tie format and leg; a league-fitted goal and draw rate misprices the goalless leg and the race window of first-scorer contracts in cup ties and the regulation/extra-time/shootout split of method-of-finish or method-of-victory contracts.
soc.knockout_cagey_factor.measurement: For each competition (domestic cup, Champions League knockouts, supercups, tournaments) and stage: ratio R_goals = observed goals/90 divided by model-expected goals from ratings, and draw uplift = observed draw rate minus model draw rate; estimate over 10 seasons, shrink to pooled knockout mean with k=40 matches; separate single-leg, first-leg, second-leg; as-of = previous seasons only.
raw_data: cup match results with stage, leg, ET/pens flags
soc.knockout_cagey_factor.why: In FTTS it only scales both teams' hazards in cup knockouts and second legs, which moves the goalless leg and the race window; irrelevant for the league and neutral-final series, so secondary context rather than a primary driver.

soc.first_goal_route_mix.label: Route mix of first goals: open play, set piece, penalty, own goal
soc.first_goal_route_mix.mechanism: Share of a team's first goals by route and the opponent's concession share.
soc.first_goal_route_mix.rationale: The first goal is disproportionately a set piece or penalty (about 30-35% of first goals combined), so a team that scores first through dead balls differs from one that does so in open play, and referees who give early penalties matter.
soc.first_goal_route_mix.measurement: For each team over last 40 matches: share of first goals scored/conceded via open play, set pieces, penalties, own goals; shrink to league shares with k=10; combine with expected numbers of corner/free kick/penalty events in this fixture to give each side's first-goal intensity decomposed by route.
raw_data: goal log with situation tag, minute and scorer team
soc.first_goal_route_mix.why: Turns a lump first-goal hazard into route-specific intensities that respond to referee and set-piece news.

soc.first_goal_hazard.reason: Minute-level hazards are the object of the race; the realised first-goal minute is unknown pre-match but the fitted team hazard parameters are knowable, so pregame_knowable is partial, not no.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.reason: Supplies the two relative scoring intensities that decide who wins the first-goal race.

soc.dixon_coles_low_score.reason: Affects 0-0 and the P(no goal) outcome but little else for first-scorer race.

soc.set_pieces.reason: Dead balls account for a large share of first goals; attack-vs-defence matchup matters.

soc.pace_press.reason: Style descriptors have little incremental power over xG ratings for who scores first; mostly through shot volume.

soc.xi_strength_delta.reason: Missing striker/keeper changes lambda; partial pregame knowability.

soc.penalty_rate.reason: Early penalty awards are a source of first goals; referee-level shrinkage is necessary.

soc.home_advantage.reason: Scoring intensity ratio depends on home advantage; for neutral finals it must be set to zero.

m.rules_text.reason: Required for the entire-game window, own-goal credit and the No Goal leg; abandonment handling is still unstated in FTTS texts.

soc.xg.reason: Raw xG is the unadjusted version of the same quantity.

soc.lineups_pit.reason: Timing and vintage of lineups matter; a late striker absence changes the first-goal race.

soc.shots.reason: Shot counts add little over xG for scoring-order races; kept only as raw data.

soc.extra_time_phase_scoring_rate.reason: Sets P(no goal in 91-120) and the second-half of the race window in competitions that play extra time (stage s3); factor is exactly one in leagues and straight-to-penalties cups.

soc.second_leg_aggregate_state.reason: Changes which side must attack from kickoff in second legs (stage s3 and interaction with soc.knockout_cagey_factor); absent for league and single-leg FTTS series.

soc.weather.reason: Heat, humidity and altitude change both intensities and the early-goal hazard at some venues; context multiplier only, with no measured effect size in this record.

soc.goal_dist.reason: The no-goal leg is the joint 0-0 cell of the goal-count model; carrying it ties the FTTS price to the same model as the sibling result, total and BTTS prices instead of leaving consistency to the Dixon-Coles term alone.

interactions.mechanism: In a second leg the aggregate decides who must attack: a side leading by two sits deep and the trailing side presses from kickoff, so the first-goal hazard is shifted toward the trailing team and the no-goal mass rises when the leader is strong enough to defend; the cagey factor is a function of the aggregate state, not a constant.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin second-leg FTTS outcomes by aggregate margin and compare first-scorer shares and goalless rates to first-leg baselines.

interactions.mechanism: The first-goal minute and route are jointly distributed: set pieces concentrate after minute 30 while penalties are timed by referee decisions, so the intensity decomposition changes the win-the-race probability and the minute distribution together.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the first-goal CDF by route and compare with a pooled hazard in held-out matches.

interactions.mechanism: Home advantage multiplies the intensity ratio, so in a neutral-venue final it disappears and the favourite's first-scorer odds fall by an amount to be estimated from neutral-venue finals relative to the same pairing at home.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit first-scorer indicator with home and neutral flags.

interactions.mechanism: Only in competitions that play extra time: the no-goal leg needs 0-0 at 90 and no extra-time goal, so its price is the product of the 0-0 cell and the tired-play survival over 30 minutes; in leagues and straight-to-penalties cups the extra-time factor is exactly one.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare goalless-after-120 frequencies in cup ties with ET against the 0-0-at-90 cell times modelled ET survival.

interactions.mechanism: A referee with a high penalty-award rate raises the penalty share of first goals for the side that wins more box entries, so the route mix and the referee propensity multiply; the effect is largest when open-play xG is close and a single penalty decides the race.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit first-scorer probability with a referee penalty-rate x box-entry-share term on held-out matches.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave first-goal CDF with right-skewed minute
nonlinearities.why: The probability a goal arrives by minute t is 1-exp(-integral hazard), so equal differences in hazard matter more early.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise by stage and leg
nonlinearities.why: The goal-rate multiplier differs sharply between first legs, second legs and single-leg finals, and P(no goal) responds exponentially to it, so a linear multiplier misprices the goalless leg in cup ties.

contract.settlement_definition: Spread series: YES when the named team 'wins by more than' the x.5 strike 'after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)', so 'more than 2.5' needs a margin of 3+ and there is no push. Correct-score series: each market is one scoreline for a named winner ('Manchester United wins 6-2') on the same 90-minute window, except KXWCSCOREET, whose text counts the score 'during the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)', so a knockout game level after 90 settles on the 120-minute score (a shootout does not change it). Spread texts carry only the trademark disclaimer and correct-score texts no secondary at all: no postponement, abandonment, draw-rung or 'other score' clause is visible. Own goals count in the score.

rules_evidence.quote: after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)

rules_evidence.establishes: Spread strikes extend to 5.5 in a women's league fixture (the quote shows the 5.5 strike); that a margin beyond five goals is a mismatch event rather than Poisson noise is an inference from the strike, not rules text.

rules_evidence.establishes: Exact-score rungs are one specific scoreline for a named winner (a 5-2 rung needs the loser to score twice); the quote does not show the draw or 'other' rungs, so partition completeness is unresolved (exact_score_rung_set).

rules_evidence.quote: If UD Maracena wins 5-2 in the UD Maracena vs UE Tavernes professional Copa del Rey soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: The sampled Copa del Rey series lists a 5-2 scoreline for a named side (UD Maracena); the quote does not state that amateur sides are paired, which is background knowledge about early cup rounds.

rules_evidence.establishes: The extra-time correct-score series settles on the score including any extra time, so for knockout games the extra-time goal process enters the scoreline distribution.

rules_evidence.quote: If Manchester United wins 6-2 in the Manchester United vs Aston Villa professional EPL soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: League correct-score rungs extend to extreme scorelines (6-2), so the ladder covers deep tail cells, not only the common 1-0/2-1 scores.

variants_and_edge_cases: Spread strikes are x.5 'wins by more than' with strike_type greater (e.g. KXLALIGA2SPREAD 3.5): P(margin>=4) is a deep-tail event for most pairings, so the tail of goal difference and mismatch magnitude (cup ties across divisions) dominate rather than lambda differences.

Exact score requires a correct joint distribution of each team's count: a 'wins 5-2' rung needs the loser to score 2, which is very sensitive to the loser's conversion in a chasing game; the ladder across hundreds of rungs must be a proper joint distribution (monotone and summing to one).

Cup ties that need a winner go to ET and penalties but spreads and regular correct scores settle at 90 minutes; neither spread nor correct-score texts contain a postponement or abandonment clause (the 48-hour rule is visible only in sibling GAME texts).

180 live series, 156 with rules text (spreads: identical 'wins by more than N goals ... after 90 minutes plus stoppage time' wording, sampled strikes 2.5 to 7.5 being the top listed rung; correct scores: one scoreline per market, sampled up to 7-6); 24 are TITLE_ONLY; first-half spreads are in first_half_and_period.

KXWCSCOREET is the only extra-time-inclusive series: for a World Cup knockout game the scoreline is the 90-minute score if a side wins in regulation and the 120-minute score otherwise, so P(score) mixes the regulation joint pmf with the extra-time increment conditional on a draw at 90 (stage s6).
