mechanism.summary: A handicap or exact score settles on the regulation goal difference or scoreline, so the object is the joint distribution of two team goal counts. The mean gap comes from team strengths (with a bridge between divisions for cup mismatches) and from the confirmed lineup; the favourite's rotation in mismatch games is a major discrete driver. The tail of the margin differs from independent Poisson: leaders ease off after a large lead and underdogs can collapse, and the base rate of mismatches depends on the league's competitive balance. Exact-score rungs depend on cell-level dependence in low scores and on the trailing side's scoring while chasing. The ladders are nested (spreads) or a partition (scores), settled at 90 minutes.

stages.name: Strength gap between the two teams
stages.description: A handicap and a correct score first require the full distribution of the strength gap: league-adjusted attack/defence strengths for both teams, venue, and a bridge between divisions when cup sides come from different tiers. Rating error for the weaker side is large in cups (small samples, no common opponents), so the mismatch size is itself uncertain.
stages.distribution: Log-normal-ish posterior of attack and defence per team; the gap between divisions has sd of about 0.3-0.5 log-goals when linked only by sparse cup results.

stages.name: Lineup and rotation of the favourite
stages.description: In cups and congested weeks big clubs rotate heavily against small clubs, which reduces the favourite's lambda by 15-30% and changes who plays up front; the confirmed XI shifts the margin distribution far more than the opponent does. Depth of the favourite's bench determines how large the drop is.
stages.distribution: Discrete lineup states (full strength / rotated / reserves) with probabilities that depend on stakes; lambda scale shifts by regime.

stages.name: Goal-difference distribution and its tail
stages.description: Given the two lambdas the margin is a Skellam-like difference, but real blowouts have a different tail: after a 3-0 lead the favourite eases off (lowering its lambda), while a collapsing underdog (red card, tactical disorganisation) concedes in bunches. The league's competitive balance sets how often mismatches occur and how fat the tail of margins is.
stages.distribution: Difference of correlated overdispersed counts; the tail beyond margin 4 is thicker than Skellam in lopsided leagues, thinner after garbage time sets in.

stages.name: Low and mid scoreline structure for exact scores
stages.description: Exact-score rungs depend on the joint distribution cell by cell: the 0-0, 1-0, 1-1 cells use Dixon-Coles dependence, and cells like 3-1, 2-2 depend on the two teams' high-count behaviour; the loser's scoring chance when trailing (chasing) matters for 4-2 vs 4-0.
stages.distribution: Joint pmf over scorelines with heavy mass at 1-0, 1-1, 2-1; each cell probability below 15% so rung prices are small and noise-sensitive.

stages.name: Ladder consistency and settlement
stages.description: Spread strikes form a nested monotone ladder (P(margin>3.5) <= P(margin>2.5)) and correct-score rungs form a partition; regulation-only settlement and the 'winner' conditional in each rung determine mapping. No cancellation, abandonment or fair-price clause is visible in any spread or correct-score text, so postponement handling cannot be mapped from the contract.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping; constraint structure rather than randomness.

stages.name: Extra-time-inclusive scoreline (KXWCSCOREET)
stages.description: For the World Cup 'Correct Score after Extra Time' series the settled scoreline is the 90-minute score when regulation produces a winner, and otherwise the level 90-minute score plus the two teams' extra-time goals. The scoreline pmf is therefore the regulation pmf on non-draw cells plus a convolution of each drawn cell (0-0, 1-1, 2-2) with a low-rate tired extra-time process; drawn 120-minute scores stay possible because the shootout does not alter the score, and group-stage games (no extra time) collapse to the regulation pmf.
stages.distribution: Mixture: regulation joint pmf on decided cells, plus drawn cells convolved with extra-time counts of mean about 0.4-0.5 combined; P(level after 120 | level after 90) near one half (to be estimated).

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted strengths with a cross-division bridge and uncertainty for cup mismatches.

opponent_matchup.note: Style mismatches and the competitive balance of the league.

role_personnel.note: Which players play, and probability the favourite rotates in a mismatch.

availability_news.note: Confirmed XI vintage; rotation signals matter most for spread.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach rotation and substitution habits in cup mismatches.

environment.note: Home advantage and neutral venue shift the margin; weather is minor for large margins.

game_context_script.note: Garbage-time damping and collapse dynamics change margin tail.

pace_volume.note: Possession and tempo volume modulate both lambdas jointly and do not independently determine the margin beyond what the xG-based strengths already encode; adding a pace term separate from lambda double counts.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing distribution of a dominant attack with many chances; xG shows chance quality.

distribution_variance.note: Joint distribution and heavy tail beyond the Skellam.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Whether the favourite prioritises the match (cup rounds between league fixtures, European weeks) is only partially encoded in rotation and stakes inputs and has not been linked to margin tails; effect of priority on exact-score ladder is unmeasured.

officiating_rules.note: Referee card and penalty propensity (shrunk) drives early-red-card and penalty regimes that change the margin tail; soc.fouls_cards (audited WEAK) is no longer cited.

settlement_contract.note: Regulation-only margin and consistency across rungs.

soc.cross_tier_strength_link.label: Cross-division bridge rating for cup mismatches
soc.cross_tier_strength_link.mechanism: Estimated strength difference between divisions or leagues from cup ties and European fixtures.
soc.cross_tier_strength_link.rationale: In Coupe de France, Copa del Rey or FA Cup rounds there are no common opponents; ratings estimated within leagues are on different scales, and the bridge parameter drives the expected margin and so the spread ladder.
soc.cross_tier_strength_link.measurement: Fit a joint rating model across divisions/leagues using all inter-division matches (cups, European club competitions, friendlies): rating_i = league_effect(L_i) + team_effect_i with a random-walk-on-season; league effect posterior with sd; update weekly; shrink team effects to division mean with k=12 matches; as-of = prior to kickoff.
raw_data: inter-division match results with date and venue
soc.cross_tier_strength_link.why: Large cup mismatches are the main source of high spread and exact-score rungs and need explicit division bridging.

soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.label: Favourite's rotation intensity in mismatch fixtures
soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.mechanism: Predicted number and quality of changed starters for a big club facing a lower-ranked side.
soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.rationale: A rotated favourite loses 15-30% of attacking output but a full-strength one may win by five; the spread ladder swings between regimes, and the rotation is partly predictable from the cup, midweek schedule and manager history.
soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.measurement: Ordinal logit of starters changed (0, 1-3, 4-6, 7+) on: days since last match, days to next major match, competition type, rating gap, manager rotation propensity (past 30 matches); output expected lambda multiplier = sum_k P(k) * m_k, with m_k estimated by regressing xG on number of rotated starters (with player-quality weights); re-evaluate at lineup release. Backtests are restricted to point-in-time proxies that are verifiable historically (previous-match XI changes, days since last match, fixture density, competition type); press-conference and training signals are excluded because no timestamped history exists (rotation_ground_truth).
soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.why: Dominant spread driver in cup fixtures that no strength rating captures.

soc.blowout_tail_inflation.label: Empirical tail of goal difference relative to Skellam, by gap quantile
soc.blowout_tail_inflation.mechanism: Excess or deficit of large margins compared with the independent-Poisson prediction.
soc.blowout_tail_inflation.rationale: At strikes 3.5-5.5 the model's tail fraction is wrong by tens of percent when game-state (garbage time, collapse) is ignored; calibrating on history is the only way to price the deep tail.
soc.blowout_tail_inflation.measurement: Define model P as the production Dixon-Coles/NB goal model refit on an expanding window using only matches before each match date. Pool 10 seasons per league group; bin by pre-match expected goal difference (deciles); per bin compute observed P(margin>=m)/model P(margin>=m) for m in {2,3,4,5}; isotonic-smooth across bins, shrink to pooled-league ratio with k=100 matches per bin; output multiplicative factors. As-of kickoff using only prior-season-fitted factors.
raw_data: pre-match model expected goal difference per match
soc.blowout_tail_inflation.why: Mismatch-driven spreads depend more on tail calibration than on mean strength.

soc.league_strength_dispersion.label: League competitive balance: sd of team strengths
soc.league_strength_dispersion.mechanism: Dispersion of ratings within a league-season.
soc.league_strength_dispersion.rationale: A league with one dominant club (Scotland, Women's Première Ligue, Turkish and Greek top halves) generates many 4+ goal margins compared with a balanced league; the base rate of mismatches differs by league and the model should reflect it.
soc.league_strength_dispersion.measurement: Per league-season: sd of team rating (attack-defence) from the ratings model, plus P(expected margin > 1.5) share of fixtures; compute rolling 3-season values with shrinkage to a global value (k=2 seasons).
soc.league_strength_dispersion.why: Calibrates base rates of lopsided games by league, where sampled spreads reach 5.5 goals.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.reason: Opponent/venue-adjusted strengths give the two lambdas; needs division bridging for cups.

soc.dixon_coles_low_score.reason: Matters for the low-scoreline cells of the exact-score ladder but little for 2.5+ spreads.

soc.goal_dist.reason: Joint count distribution is the object of both contracts; require overdispersion and tail calibration.

soc.ratings_uncertainty.reason: Strength uncertainty fattens the margin tail, especially for cup sides with sparse data.

soc.home_advantage.reason: Shifts margin by 0.3-0.4 goals on average; zero on neutral grounds.

soc.xi_strength_delta.reason: Lineup and rotation changes move the margin more than most other pregame variables.

soc.score_state.reason: Not pregame; calibrates damping and collapse in the tail.

soc.implied_lambda_from_lines.reason: Implied lambdas are derived from de-vigged market prices, so they are a benchmark, not an independent input.

soc.favourite_longshot_bias.reason: Describes distortions in market prices; useful for evaluating edge but not an input to the goal mechanism.

m.ladder_structure.reason: The cross-rung monotonicity check is computed on quoted strike prices, so it is market-derived and used only to validate model output across rungs, not as an input to any stage or coverage claim; the nested-event structure itself is taken from m.rules_text.

m.rules_text.reason: Regulation-only settlement and winner conditioning flags.

soc.xg.reason: Raw xG is the unadjusted input to the adjusted ratings.

soc.lineups_pit.reason: Lineup vintage determines whether the rotation scenario materialised.

soc.set_piece_matchup.reason: Set-piece strength matters for mid-range scorelines, but is small for the margin.

soc.fouls_cards.reason: Card tendencies matter only via early red cards, which are rare and unpredictable; the referee effect on margin is small.

soc.referee.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s3) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

soc.extra_time_shootout_model.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s4; stage s6) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

soc.knockout_cagey_factor.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s6) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: Rotation scales the favourite's attack, and the cross-tier gap sets the baseline; their product determines whether a cup mismatch is a 5+ goal margin or a tight win, so the combined effect is much larger than either factor alone.
interactions.how_to_test: Interaction regression of margin on rotation intensity times rating gap in cup ties.

interactions.mechanism: Beyond a three-goal lead the match switches from a scoring regime into a damping regime for the leader, while a red-card collapse switches the opposite; the margin tail therefore has two regimes depending on which happens first.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate hazard of next goal by lead size and numerical advantage.

interactions.mechanism: Exact-score cells are determined jointly by marginal counts and the dependence correction; shifting rho changes 1-0/0-0/1-1 cells but leaves 3-1 unchanged, so the ladder must be fitted as a joint distribution, not rung by rung.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare log-loss of exact-score pmf with and without the dependence correction by cell.

interactions.mechanism: In lopsided leagues, rating uncertainty adds disproportionately to the probability of big margins because the convex tail of the margin distribution amplifies variation in the strength gap. (hypothesis: convexity of the margin tail in rating uncertainty is asserted, not measured)
interactions.how_to_test: Compute league balance from an external statistic (final-table points sd or Gini from standings, not from the ratings model) and compare P(margin>=4) calibration by balance tercile and posterior width.

interactions.mechanism: Home advantage in the margin depends on the home side being at full strength; a rotated home favourite loses much of its crowd-driven edge over an organised underdog, so the venue term is conditional on lineup quality. (hypothesis, size unmeasured)
interactions.how_to_test: Fit home effect separately for rotated vs full-strength lineups.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex mapping from rating gap to P(margin>=4)
nonlinearities.why: The probability of a large margin grows faster than linearly in the expected goal gap because the Skellam tail increases roughly exponentially.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at 4+ changed starters
nonlinearities.why: Changing one to three players barely affects output, but rotating most of the attack changes the favourite's lambda abruptly.

nonlinearities.shape: Isotonic non-parametric correction by margin
nonlinearities.why: The ratio of observed to model tail probabilities is not constant in margin; it needs a flexible monotone fit.

contract.settlement_definition: Each match has three mutually exclusive binaries (home wins, away wins, 'Tie is the result'), settled on the score after 90 minutes plus stoppage time; extra time and penalties are explicitly excluded, so in cup ties a team that wins on penalties still leaves 'Tie' as the YES outcome. Club matches cancelled or rescheduled more than 48 hours away resolve to a fair price; eight series use 'over two weeks away' instead (KXWCGAME, KXFIFAGAME, KXAFCACGAME, KXINTERCONCUPGAME, KXFINALISSIMAGAME, KXCONCACAFCCUPGAME, KXESPSUPERCUPGAME, KXITASUPERCUPGAME); KXCLUBWCGAME has a third clause: a postponed game keeps the market open until the rescheduled game is played (within two years), and a cancelled game not played resolves 33/33/33 across Tie and both team markets. All 156 live series are single-match GAME series (143 with rules text, 13 without: 12 TITLE_ONLY plus KXAFCCL2GAME, which is NO_LISTING and rests on Kalshi series-metadata evidence only, not rules text); the exception is KXBALLERLEAGUEGAME (Baller League small-sided format), whose text ('If Club 360 and Super Ninos tie in the ... Baller League soccer game') states no 90-minute window and no postponement clause.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game ends in a tie, the market called "Tie" resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Draw is its own contract; for the Premier League there is no extra time anyway, but a draw is a priced outcome, not a void or push.

rules_evidence.quote: after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)
rules_evidence.establishes: Even in a continental knockout, the result is judged at the end of regulation, so draw probability at 90 is the object, not who advances.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is cancelled or rescheduled to over 48 hours away, the market will resolve to a fair price in accordance with the rules.
rules_evidence.establishes: Postponement settlement is a fair-price void: a market holder is not hurt by weather postponements beyond 48 hours but a short delay under 48 hours leaves the contract live.

rules_evidence.quote: professional Club Friendlies soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: Friendlies are listed with the same settlement as competitive league games, which creates a different data-generating process (rotation, substitution waves) under the same contract text.

rules_evidence.quote: after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)
rules_evidence.establishes: Bolivian Premier Division at altitude settles identically to European games, so the altitude advantage enters through the goal process only.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is cancelled or rescheduled to over two weeks away, the market will resolve to a fair price in accordance with the rules.
rules_evidence.establishes: World Cup and other FIFA-tournament game series use a two-week postponement window, longer than the 48-hour club window.

rules_evidence.quote: tie in the Club 360 vs Super Ninos Baller League soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: The Baller League text defines the tie without any regulation window or postponement clause, so its settlement period is whatever the small-sided format's own rules define.

variants_and_edge_cases: Three binaries per match must be coherent: P(home)+P(draw)+P(away)=1; each is its own series entry (e.g. KXMLSGAME ticker suffix -TIE vs team codes), so mispricing can sit in the draw leg alone.

Some texts phrase the draw leg as 'If Tie wins the ...' (KXFIFAGAME, KXINTERCONCUPGAME) rather than 'Tie is the result'; both are the same 3-way partition. No two-way (no-draw) soccer winner text exists in the 143 texts read.

Cup ties, club friendlies and Libertadores/Sudamericana knockouts mix incentives (aggregate state, rotation, substitution waves up to 6 players) under the same 90-minute settlement; two-leg aggregate position changes the draw rate without changing the contract.
Stoppage time is part of the window: late goals in 90+ minutes count, and 90+N length depends on VAR and substitution; abandonment mid-match (weather, crowd) is not covered in the sampled text.

Exhibition and non-standard formats share the 3-way wording: MLS All-Star Game (KXMLSASTGAME, MLS vs Liga MX all-stars), NCAA men's soccer (KXNCAAMSOCCERGAME), club friendlies; Baller League is a small-sided format with its own match length and tie rules (stage s7).

Postponement clauses differ: 48 hours (most club texts), two weeks (eight tournament and super-cup texts), and KXCLUBWCGAME's stay-open-then-1/3-each rule for a cancelled game; Baller League has none.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official match report score at full time of regulation (90 minutes plus stoppage time) from the competition's governing body, which Kalshi's data provider mirrors; extra time and shootouts not used.

series_mapping_issues.issue: Baller League is a six-a-side short-format competition with its own rules; the Tie text gives no 90-minute window, so neither the 11-a-side goal model nor the regulation window applies.

TITLE_ONLY 'Italy Serie A (W) Game' with the KXBB prefix of KXBBSERIEAGAME and KXBBSERIEA2GAME, both re-filed OUT_OF_SCOPE:other_sport_basketball; it was never reviewed (origin ledger, NO_LISTING) and is most likely women's basketball, not soccer (women's Serie A soccer is KXSERIEAWGAME).

mechanism.summary: The 3-way result is the sign of the regulation goal difference, with the draw as a separate priced leg. Expected goal difference comes from adjusted team strengths and team-specific home advantage, then moves with the actual lineup (the part that was not predicted), rotation and stakes, fatigue and travel, and for specific leagues altitude. The draw probability depends on the total goal environment and on low-cell dependence, peaking when teams are balanced and totals are low; referee shocks and red cards add rare large effects. The contract settles on 90 minutes plus stoppage time with extra time and penalties excluded and a fair-price void for postponements, and friendlies and cups share the same settlement but different incentives.

stages.name: Team strength differential
stages.description: The expected goal difference comes from opponent-adjusted attack and defence strengths with decay and shrinkage, plus home advantage by team and league, and a preseason or promotion prior when evidence is thin. The rating gap, scaled by the competition's goal environment, sets the shape of win/draw/loss probabilities.
stages.distribution: Latent strengths are Bayesian posteriors with sd about 0.1-0.15 in log goal-rate; three-way outcome follows from a bivariate goal model.

stages.name: Who plays: lineup, rotation and surprise
stages.description: The outcome depends on the quality of the XI that actually plays; the deviation of the actual lineup from the predicted one is only a timing construct for when information arrives, together with suspensions, injuries to key players and manager rotation in congested weeks. A missing goalkeeper or playmaker is worth roughly 0.1-0.25 goals of expected goal difference.
stages.distribution: Discrete lineup scenarios; effect on goal difference is heavy-tailed and sparse (most matches change little, some change a lot).

stages.name: Fatigue, travel and situational context
stages.description: Rest days, minutes load, travel and time-zone change, international-break returns and the stakes of the match (title or relegation leverage, dead rubbers, rivalry) shift effort and rotation; altitude and heat in parts of South America and CONCACAF alter the physiological advantage of the home side far beyond ordinary home advantage. The size of the altitude penalty (a few tenths of a goal in extreme cases) is unsourced and to be estimated. In cup second legs the aggregate score, not the match score, sets each side's required risk, which shifts the regulation draw probability (soc.second_leg_aggregate_state); it is absent for league and single-leg games.
stages.distribution: Smaller effects (0.05-0.15 goals) except altitude which can be 0.3-0.5 goals; many correlated small shocks.

stages.name: Draw mass and low-scoring structure
stages.description: The draw is the most mispriced outcome: its probability depends on the total goal environment (lower totals raise draws), on the dependence between teams in low cells (Dixon-Coles) and on team-specific draw tendencies from style (low-block, cagey sides). Draw probability is about 26% on average, peaking when expected goal difference is near zero.
stages.distribution: Discrete 0-0/1-1 cell masses; draw rate is bounded in the 20-33% range for league games with a peak at balanced matches.

stages.name: Officiating and shocks
stages.description: Referee choices (penalties about 0.3 per match, red cards about 0.1) and VAR create sudden shifts in the match; a first-half red card changes the expected goal difference by about 0.5 goals. These are mostly unpredictable but have referee-level baselines.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete shocks with large effects; right skewed on goal difference.

stages.name: Settlement and market-type bookkeeping
stages.description: Settlement is the 90-minute score; the contract boundary must be correctly implemented for cup ties, and the three outcome markets must be consistent. Friendlies and cups use different incentive structure but the same settlement; the market-derived odds are only a benchmark for validation.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the final regulation score; no randomness beyond the match.

stages.name: Non-standard formats: all-star, college and small-sided games
stages.description: A minority of GAME series are not ordinary 11-a-side competitive fixtures: the MLS All-Star Game pits selected squads with mass substitutions and low defensive effort, NCAA games use unlimited re-entry substitutions and different squad depth, and Baller League games are short small-sided matches with their own clock and scoring rules. For these the goal rate, home advantage and draw mass cannot be borrowed from league models; the format profile (match length, players per side, substitution rule, how a level game is decided) sets the scoring environment and the tie probability, and team strength must come from the competition's own results.
stages.distribution: Format-specific: all-star and small-sided games have high goal rates and thin draw mass; college games resemble lower-tier league games with larger rating uncertainty.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted attack/defence and team-specific home advantage supply the expected goal difference.

opponent_matchup.note: Style interaction (pressing versus low block) and derby effects on draw rate.

role_personnel.note: XI quality relative to average and relative to prediction; rotation probability.

availability_news.note: Lineup vintage about 60 minutes before kickoff; the surprise is the informative component.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager rotation habits and tactical system.

environment.note: Altitude, travel and time zones plus heat, humidity and pitch conditions from soc.weather (added) cover the environment channel.

game_context_script.note: Aggregate state (cup second legs) and stakes dictate risk taking and the regulation draw rate; soc.second_leg_aggregate_state is attached to this archetype as context and audited here.

pace_volume.note: Chance volume from xG-based strength; tempo effects on result are second order for a 3-way outcome.

efficiency_conversion.note: Goalkeeper shot-stopping and finishing; both shrunk.

distribution_variance.note: Draw mass shaped by low-cell dependence and team tendency.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Congestion, stakes and the special case of friendlies.

officiating_rules.note: Referee/VAR-shrunk penalty award rate (soc.penalty_rate, added) is the main officiating input; soc.referee is audited WEAK and is secondary cover only.

settlement_contract.note: Regulation-only counting, Tie as a separate outcome and the 48-hour fair-price clause are parsed from the rules text; soc.market_odds is a BENCHMARK_ONLY audit item and is not an input to any stage or category.

soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted.label: Deviation of the actual XI from the predicted XI
soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted.mechanism: Value difference between the lineup announced at about T-60 and the lineup forecast from the previous day.
soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted.rationale: For outcome prediction what matters is the quality of the XI that plays (soc.xi_strength_delta); the surprise relative to a predicted XI is a timing and edge-detection construct that says when the information is new, and it cannot be backtested without archived predicted lineups (rotation_timing).
soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted.measurement: Predict starters via a logistic model on last-5 starts, minutes, injury flags, rest, press-conference status (calibrated start probability p_i); expected lineup value E[V]=sum p_i * v_i; surprise = V_actual - E[V] in expected goals (v_i from ridge on team xG-diff). Compute at lineup release; as-of strictly the announced lineup timestamp.
soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted.why: Marks when lineup information is new relative to an expectation formed hours earlier; the outcome effect itself is carried by soc.xi_strength_delta.

soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.label: Altitude difference between home venue and visitor's habitual altitude
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.mechanism: Home altitude minus the visitor's mean altitude over recent matches, with recency of exposure.
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.rationale: Bolivia, Ecuador, Colombia and Mexico City host matches above 2,000-3,600 m; visiting teams from sea level lose 0.3-0.6 goals of expected margin, the effect is nonlinear in altitude and decays with acclimatisation days, and is outside the usual home-advantage parameter.
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.measurement: gap_m = alt(venue) - A_vis, where A_vis = sum_k w_k*alt(venue_k)/sum_k w_k over the visitor's matches in the 60 days before kickoff (w_k=0.5^(days_ago/20)); if no match in window use altitude of the visitor's home venue. x = max(0, gap_m-500)/1000 (km above 500 m). Fit goal-difference ~ ... + beta*x (plus separate beta for 2H if minute data exist) on all matches since 2000 with team home-advantage and rating terms, ridge-shrink beta to 0 with k=50 matches above 500 m. As-of kickoff-1h; altitude values are static venue constants.
raw_data: team match history with venue and date for last 60 days
team base altitude (home venue) for clubs
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.why: A first-order home advantage driver in the Bolivian, Ecuadorian and Colombian leagues in this ledger bucket.

soc.friendly_match_intensity.label: Friendly-match rotation and effort index
soc.friendly_match_intensity.mechanism: Competitive-intent indicator for friendlies and pre-season matches.
soc.friendly_match_intensity.rationale: Club friendlies settle like league games but are played with rotated squads, 60-minute starters and mass substitutions, so ratings fitted to competitive matches overstate team quality and understate randomness.
soc.friendly_match_intensity.measurement: For international and club friendlies (martj42 dataset; club friendlies from worldfootball), regress |goal difference| and draw indicator on match-type dummy (friendly vs competitive), pre-match rating gap and team fixed effects over 8 seasons; the type coefficient is shrunk to 0 with k=30 friendly matches. Output variance multiplier v = observed Var(goal diff | friendly)/model variance and compressed gap g' = g*(1 - c) with c = fitted rating-gap slope ratio friendly/competitive (bounded 0.3-1). As-of prior matches only.
soc.friendly_match_intensity.why: Friendlies appear in the ledger bucket (KXCLUBFGAME) with settlement identical to competitive matches but a distinct data-generating process.

soc.match_format_rules_profile.label: Match format rules profile for non-standard game series
soc.match_format_rules_profile.mechanism: Match length, players per side and substitution rules change the goal rate and the draw probability of a 3-way market.
soc.match_format_rules_profile.rationale: All-star, college and small-sided (Baller League) GAME series share the 3-way text with league games but not the 11-a-side, 90-minute process; applying league draw rates to them misprices the Tie leg. The subtle part is that the Baller League text states no window, so the format's own rules define what 'tie' means.
soc.match_format_rules_profile.measurement: Per competition, a static record updated each season: regulation minutes, players per side, maximum substitutions and re-entry flag, level-game procedure (draw stands / shootout / golden goal), plus the competition's empirical goals per match and draw rate over the last 2 seasons (or all available games if fewer than 100), shrunk toward a format-class prior with k=50 games; as-of the market listing.
free_sources: competition regulations pages (Baller League, MLS All-Star, NCAA rulebook)
raw_data: rulebook fields: minutes, players_per_side, subs_rule, tie_procedure
soc.match_format_rules_profile.why: Sets the scoring environment and draw mass for GAME series that are not standard 11-a-side fixtures.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.reason: Core strength estimates feeding the 3-way probabilities.

soc.ratings.reason: Both fit attack/defence strengths from goals (Dixon-Coles) or xG; running both as separate inputs duplicates strength; keep one as the prior and the other as a robustness check.

soc.home_advantage.reason: Home advantage is team- and competition-specific and sizable (about 0.3-0.4 goals), with a need to zero it on neutral grounds.

soc.dixon_coles_low_score.reason: Shifts draw cells; league-level rho is small but matters for the draw leg.

soc.draw_propensity.reason: Team-pair draw tendencies persist weakly; the structural draw rate is mostly from goal environment.

soc.xi_strength_delta.reason: Lineup quality relative to season average; needs surprise vs predicted version.

soc.rotation_index.reason: Predicts lineup changes before release; useful with a forecasting horizon of 24 hours.

soc.stakes_leverage.reason: Stakes explain effort differences in dead rubbers, but magnitude is modest outside relegation and title fights.

soc.congestion_load.reason: Cumulative minutes explain rotation more than performance; small incremental power.

soc.gk.reason: Keeper effect is small and mostly absorbed in defensive ratings.

soc.referee.reason: Referee baselines have little predictive value for the result direction beyond penalty rates; high noise.

soc.market_odds.reason: Closing odds are a market-derived benchmark for calibration, not an independent input.

m.rules_text.reason: Needed to ensure regulation-only labels for cups and friendlies.

soc.lineups_pit.reason: Lineup vintage is the main late information; timestamp discipline crucial.

soc.motivation.reason: Motivation is defined from the same season-simulation leverage as stakes_leverage.

soc.rest_travel.reason: Rest and travel add small signals, separately modelled from congestion.

soc.xg.reason: Raw xG is the unadjusted data for the adjusted ratings.

soc.formation.reason: Tactical system matchups are hard to measure pregame and have weak evidence.

soc.rivalry_intensity.reason: Derby flag has only small effects on goals/cards and is partly collinear with draw propensity.

soc.favourite_longshot_bias.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on soc.market_odds x soc.favourite_longshot_bias: Price comparison needs favourite-longshot and draw-bias correction to avoid false edges on the draw rung.) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

soc.weather.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s3) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

soc.penalty_rate.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s5) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

soc.ratings_uncertainty.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s7) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

soc.second_leg_aggregate_state.reason: Only cup second legs among the GAME series have an aggregate that changes risk posture and the 90-minute draw rate; context for those series, irrelevant to league games.

interactions.mechanism: The result impact of a missing player scales with team dependence on him and with opponent strength; a surprise absence of a star in a close match moves P(win) by an unmeasured amount (a few points is a hypothesis) while the same absence in a mismatch barely matters.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress outcome on surprise times rating gap; compare to additive.

interactions.mechanism: Altitude adds to the home advantage once the visitor altitude gap exceeds about 500 m (the single breakpoint used throughout this record), rises roughly linearly above it and saturates for well-acclimatised sides near 3,000 m; the 500 m and 3,000 m values are hypotheses to be fitted, not established thresholds.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit home effect by altitude bins in Bolivian/Ecuadorian leagues.

interactions.mechanism: Rotation is most likely precisely when stakes are low and the next match is bigger, so rotation times (1 - leverage) predicts strength cuts; stakes alone does not.
interactions.how_to_test: Interaction regression of lineup strength on rotation index and leverage.

interactions.mechanism: Draw probability is determined jointly by the expected goal difference (peaks at 0), the total goals (lower totals raise draws) and rho; a rating-only model gets the ordering right but misprices the draw because it ignores total-goal environment.
interactions.how_to_test: Calibrate P(draw) against total expected goals and gap; check by decile.

interactions.mechanism: In friendlies the effective rating gap is compressed (rotation, substitutions) and the variance is higher, so P(favourite win) is a flattened function of the rating gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate slope of win probability on rating gap separately for friendlies.

interactions.mechanism: League-estimated draw propensity applies only under the 11-a-side 90-minute regime; in all-star and small-sided formats the higher goal rate collapses the draw mass, so the draw input must be replaced, not adjusted, when the format profile changes.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised draw rates in All-Star/Baller League games with the league-model prediction for equal-strength pairings.

nonlinearities.shape: Ordered-logit style S-curve in rating gap for win probability; draw peaks at zero
nonlinearities.why: P(home win) and P(away win) are logistic in the gap, while P(draw) is hump-shaped; a linear gap feature cannot represent the draw leg.

nonlinearities.shape: Zero below a 500 m gap, roughly linear above it, saturating near 3000 m (breakpoints are hypotheses to be fitted)
nonlinearities.why: The physiological penalty to acclimatised visitors saturates at extreme altitude and is minimal below the threshold.

nonlinearities.shape: Possibly asymmetric: bad surprises may count more than good ones (hypothesis, unsupported)
nonlinearities.why: A key absence may reduce output more than a returning starter raises it because replacement quality is below the starter by more than depth adds; the asymmetry is an unsupported hypothesis and is not tied to market expectations.

contract.settlement_definition: One binary per candidate. Winner series (KXBALLONDOR men's 2027, KXBALLONDORAWARD women's 2026, KXPFAPOY): YES when the named player wins the named award for the stated season. KXBALLONDORAWARD and KXPFAPOY add that co-winners split $1 by the number of tied recipients unless a separate Tie/Co-Winners market is listed, and that if no award is given every candidate resolves No; the sampled KXBALLONDOR (men's 2027) text has only the one-sentence primary rule, with no tie or no-award clause. Rank series (KXBALLONDORRANK): YES when the player is in the stated top N of the official final ranking, ties resolved by the publisher's method, otherwise all tied share the highest rank and tied contracts pay $1/(number tied) rounded down. Resolution is the awarding body's official announcement. World Cup awards: KXWCAWARD pays the named Golden/Silver/Bronze Ball (or similar) recipient as recognised by FIFA, and if co-winners are announced a separate 'Tie/Co-Winners' market resolves Yes and every individual market No; KXWCAWARDCOMBO pays if the named player wins both the Golden Boot and the Golden Ball; its text states neither the Golden Boot criterion nor any shared-award rule. KXEPLPOY is TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple recipients are announced and no separate Tie/Co-Winners market is listed, Yes contracts on each recipient resolve to $1 divided by the number of tied recipients
rules_evidence.establishes: Ties pay fractional (1/n), so a joint-winner scenario carries probability weight with a payoff below one.

rules_evidence.quote: If no award is given, all participant markets resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: If the award is not given, all candidates settle No, so candidate probabilities need not sum to one.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple candidates are tied for a given rank, then their Contracts will resolve to $1/(the number of candidates tied), rounded down.
rules_evidence.establishes: Top-N rank contracts need the whole ranked vote-share distribution (rank 10 vs 11), not only the winner; tied ranks split the payout and are rounded down.

rules_evidence.quote: wins the men's Ballon d'Or in 2027
rules_evidence.establishes: The men's 2027 award trades in November 2026, months before the 2026-27 eligibility window closes, so remaining minutes, injuries and trophy paths are live inputs.

rules_evidence.quote: Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Men's Players' Player of the Year (Premier League) for 2026-2027 season
rules_evidence.establishes: The PFA award is a players' vote restricted to Premier League performance in one season, a different voter pool and eligibility scope from the Ballon d'Or.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple participants are announced as co-winners, then Tie/Co-Winners resolves to Yes and all other markets resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Unlike the Ballon d'Or text (1/n split), World Cup award co-winners resolve a dedicated Tie market and zero every individual market.

rules_evidence.quote: wins the Golden Boot and the Golden Ball in the 2026 Men's FIFA World Cup
rules_evidence.establishes: The combo needs one player to win a count-based award and a selected award together, so the dependence between top scoring and Golden Ball selection is the object.

variants_and_edge_cases: Seven live series: men's and women's Ballon d'Or winner, Ballon d'Or top-N ranking, PFA and EPL player of the year, World Cup awards (single and Golden Boot + Golden Ball combo); six have rules text, KXEPLPOY is TITLE_ONLY.

Rank series settle on the official final ranking: 'Tied rankings shall be resolved using the publisher's official tie-breaking methodology', otherwise tied entities share the highest rank and tied contracts pay $1/(number tied) rounded down, so a candidate near the 10th place cut carries tie risk.

The voting body, number of voters, scoring scale (journalist points scale of believed 15-12-10-8-7-6-5-4-3-1 for the top ten, unverified) and the eligibility window are not in the market text; they determine the joint distribution of vote shares and the tie probability.
Awards revealed by leak before the ceremony change the information state; the contract settles on the official announcement, creating timing risk if different sources publish contradictory winners.

Horizon: KXBALLONDOR (2027 men's award) is listed in November 2026, before the eligibility season ends, so availability and remaining production matter; the finalized KXBALLONDORAWARD market is the post-window case.

Scope: women's award inputs need women's-league data, which is much thinner; PFA is voted by players and restricted to the Premier League season; World Cup Balls follow FIFA's selection (technical study group plus public/media input, composition unverified) and the Golden Boot is a goal count with tiebreaks (stage s6).

Tie handling differs by series: KXBALLONDORAWARD and KXPFAPOY split $1/n among co-winners unless a Tie market exists; KXBALLONDOR states no tie rule; KXBALLONDORRANK splits tied ranks $1/n rounded down; KXWCAWARD resolves a Tie/Co-Winners market and zeros individuals; KXWCAWARDCOMBO has no clause for a shared Golden Boot or Golden Ball.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official announcement and published final ranking of the awarding body (France Football/Ballon d'Or organisers, PFA, Premier League, FIFA) as published on its website and at the ceremony.

mechanism.summary: A voted award is decided by ballots, not by on-pitch counting, so the mechanism is a vote-share model. The candidate pool is narrowed to a few players by team trophies in the eligibility window (the Champions League and tournament results carry the highest weight, with weights varying by year); within a team-success tier, individual output and media narrative separate candidates. Ballots from a finite panel aggregate with noise and possible national bias, so close races are near coin flips and ties can occur and pay 1/n. Credible leaks before the ceremony are the dominant late information, and the contract settles on the official announcement with a no-award clause.

stages.name: Eligibility, season window and candidate pool
stages.description: The award covers a defined season window and the shortlist (30 nominees for the Ballon d'Or) removes most players; the realistic contenders are 3-6 players whose teams won the main trophies in the window. A player's candidacy is determined by season-level team success and visible individual output, not by statistics accumulated before the window opens.
stages.distribution: Small discrete candidate set; probability mass heavily concentrated (top 3 hold 80-90% of the price) with a long tail of outsiders.

stages.name: Team success coupling and tournament weighting
stages.description: Voters are strongly influenced by trophies: a Champions League winner with a decisive final performance or a World Cup/Euros winner takes the lead, and the weight of each trophy varies with the year (international tournament year versus none). The player's share of team success (goals, assists and decisive moments in knockout rounds) converts team outcomes into candidate vote share.
stages.distribution: Conditional-logit style: vote share is a softmax of a utility that is dominated by team trophies; heavy-tailed shifts when a final is won or lost.

stages.name: Individual production and narrative
stages.description: Within a team-success tier, goals and assists, big-match output and the media narrative separate candidates: a 'story' (injury comeback, record-breaking season) adds votes beyond counting stats. Production is measured over the season window, but only part of it is in voters' memory, with more weight on the final months.
stages.distribution: Smooth, right-skewed utility differences; narrative factors are unobserved and partially proxied by media share and previous awards (PFA/UEFA awards).

stages.name: Voter panel aggregation and bias
stages.description: Each voter ranks a top-N list and the points sum determines the winner; with a few dozen to a hundred voters, the margin between top candidates, voter nationality and regional bias (home-country voting), and the scoring scale determine the final ordering and the chance of a tie. Close races (within 5-10 points) are essentially noisy draws.
stages.distribution: Sum of discrete voter ballots; vote-total noise sd of about 3-6 points for 100 voters; ties rare but nonzero.

stages.name: Announcement information and leaks
stages.description: The winner is determined before the ceremony and can leak; pre-ceremony reporting (credible outlets, club statements, attendance of players) updates the probability sharply, and the contract settles on the official announcement. Injuries, minutes and remaining production are live inputs only while the eligibility window is open and become inert once it closes; the pricing horizon of the sibling award series is unknown (pricing_horizon_unknown).
stages.distribution: Jump process: probability moves to near 0/1 on credible news; otherwise slow drift.

stages.name: World Cup awards: selected Balls and the counted Golden Boot
stages.description: World Cup Balls are chosen by FIFA after the final, with heavy weight on players from the finalists and on knockout-round performances, while the Golden Boot is mechanical (by FIFA practice most goals, then assists, then fewest minutes; the combo text itself states no criterion). The combo series needs both to land on one player, which happens mainly when a finalist's forward also tops the scoring, so the joint probability is far above the product of marginals for elite forwards on strong teams and near zero for others. Team progress through the bracket drives both legs.
stages.distribution: Selection: softmax over a handful of finalists' players; Golden Boot: maximum of tournament goal counts with tiebreak; combo is a strongly positively dependent joint event.

talent_strength.note: Candidate quality and team trophy outcomes drive the vote utility.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent matchup in a voted award: candidates are compared by voters across the whole season and not head to head in a match, so matchup variables of the game archetypes have no role here beyond the finals that feed team success.

role_personnel.note: Role (forward/midfielder) shapes how production converts to votes; minutes matter for the season window.

availability_news.note: Before the window closes injuries and expected minutes change remaining contribution chances; after it, leaked announcements matter.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching and tactical scheme enter only through team trophies and a forward's volume, which the team-success input already captures; no voter looks at tactics, so no separate coaching input is warranted for a voted award.

environment.note: Venue, weather and travel have no bearing on a ballot cast by journalists after the season; their effect is already inside the underlying season outcomes the voters see, so there is no environmental input for this contract.

game_context_script.note: Final and knockout events weigh more heavily in voters' memory.

pace_volume.note: Volume statistics such as shots or touches are not the voters' criterion beyond the goals and assists they produce; keeping them would give a false sense of precision in a subjective vote.

efficiency_conversion.note: Goal conversion is only a partial signal because voters respond to totals regardless of luck.

distribution_variance.note: Vote-share distribution and aggregation noise determine the tail and ties.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Tournament year, stakes of trophies, and narrative.

officiating_rules.note: Match officials do not affect a vote; rules and eligibility windows of the award are contract matters and are handled under settlement, not as an officiating input.

settlement_contract.note: Co-winner split, no-award clause, season eligibility window.

soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.label: Trophy weighting by year and competition for voters
soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.mechanism: Estimated vote weight for Champions League, World Cup, continental championships and league titles in each award year.
soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.rationale: A Women's Ballon d'Or in a tournament year behaves differently from a non-tournament year; the weight a Champions League final carries versus a World Cup depends on the year, which a pooled model would blur.
soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.measurement: From historical winners and top-5 results (2018-2025 Ballon d'Or male and female, plus Super Ballon d'Or), fit a conditional-logit with features: team won UCL, won World Cup/Euros/Copa/AFCON, won league, reached final, interaction with tournament-year dummy; regularised with ridge and cross-validated by leave-one-year-out; output feature weights with sd. Identifiability limit: with about 7 women's ceremonies (pooled with men's and Super Ballon d'Or via shared coefficients) a year-interaction model is under-identified; fit main effects plus a single tournament-year dummy, shrink strongly (ridge), and report intervals; points-scale and panel changes by year are covariates, not ignored.
raw_data: historical vote tables with ranks and points
soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.why: Isolates the dominant coefficient of the voting model and lets the model switch regimes by year.

soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.label: Voter panel aggregation and tie simulation
soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.mechanism: Monte Carlo of ballots with a points scale, voter nationality bias and noise, giving winner and tie probabilities.
soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.rationale: Close races among two or three candidates are decided by ballots drawn from a distribution; the probability of a tie and the payoff split depends on the scale, voter count and variance.
soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.measurement: Utilities u_i = log-scores from soc.award_vote_distribution (conditional logit, market-free features: production, trophies, tournament result) fitted on prior ceremonies only. Each of N voters draws a top-10 ordering from Plackett-Luce with utility u_i + b*home_nation(voter,candidate) + e (e~Gumbel); points 15,12,10,8,7,6,5,4,3,1; N as published for the award. b and the voter noise scale are fitted by maximum likelihood to historical vote totals (2019-2025 Ballon d'Or men's and women's) with ridge toward b=0. 20000 draws; report P(win) and P(tie).
raw_data: vote totals by candidate and voter lists
soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.why: Provides winner and tie probabilities and the 1/n split payoff that the contract specifies.

soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.label: Pre-announcement leak and credible-report signal
soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.mechanism: Reliability-weighted indicator that the winner has been leaked ahead of the ceremony.
soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.rationale: Previous awards have been leaked days ahead by outlets and club staff; a credible leak moves probability to near certainty and is the most informative late input, but a false leak is also possible.
soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.measurement: Event log of each report (timestamp, source tier, named winner). Per tier t estimate hit rate h_t = P(report names the eventual winner) with Beta(2,1) prior updated on past leaks, and false-report rate f_t = 1-h_t over the same sample; LR_t = h_t/(f_t/(K-1)) with K candidates. Posterior log-odds for candidate c = prior log-odds + sum of log LR_t over independent reports (reports from the same upstream source counted once, total LR capped at 20). As-of strictly the report timestamp.
raw_data: timestamped news reports with source tier
soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.why: The decisive late-moving information for voted awards; absent from the existing list.

soc.prior_award_momentum.label: Momentum from precursor awards and shortlists
soc.prior_award_momentum.mechanism: Results of precursor awards (UEFA Player of the Year, PFA, national awards) and shortlists as predictors.
soc.prior_award_momentum.rationale: Precursor awards share voters or taste with the target award and are announced earlier, so they are cheap pre-ceremony information.
soc.prior_award_momentum.measurement: Binary and rank features: won/placed in UEFA Women's Player of the Year, FIFA Best, PFA/WSL awards, league MVP; fit to historical winners with leave-one-out CV; weight by correlation of voter bodies.
soc.prior_award_momentum.why: Adds the predictability of taste before the target award.

soc.wc_award_selection_profile.label: World Cup Ball selection profile and its link to team progress and scoring
soc.wc_award_selection_profile.mechanism: FIFA Ball selections favour players of the finalists and knockout performers, coupling them to bracket outcomes and to the Golden Boot race.
soc.wc_award_selection_profile.rationale: Golden/Silver/Bronze Ball and combo markets cannot use journalist-ballot models: the selector is FIFA, the winner usually comes from a finalist, and the Golden Boot leg is count-based; the dependence between legs makes the combo far from independent.
soc.wc_award_selection_profile.measurement: Conditional logit fitted on World Cups 1982-2022 (about 11 editions, 3 Balls each): candidate features = team final placing (1-4, QF, earlier), goals+assists in knockout rounds, total goals, position, captaincy; Golden Boot from simulated tournament goal counts with FIFA tiebreaks; joint simulation inside the tournament Monte Carlo (N>=100,000) to price combos; ridge penalty chosen by leave-one-edition-out.
raw_data: historical Ball winners with team placing and stats
soc.wc_award_selection_profile.why: Prices World Cup Ball awards and the Golden Boot + Golden Ball combo.

soc.award_voting_narrative.reason: Voters respond to team success and storylines, but the narrative component has no verified data until the media-attention dataset (GDELT, Wikipedia pageviews, Google Trends) is validated; demoted from primary until a signal is shown to predict ranks.

soc.player_awards.reason: Remaining-season Poisson production is defined for in-season scoring races; for a voted award decided after the season it is only a weak proxy for the narrative component.

soc.player_xg.reason: npxG/90 is not what voters weigh and the season window is closed by the time of the ceremony; keep only as a covariate for forward candidates.

soc.leader_race_state.reason: Goal tally state is mostly Golden-Boot logic; for a voted award it matters only before the window closes through remaining fixtures and is weak compared with trophy outcomes.

soc.comp_sim.reason: Competition simulation is the engine that supplies team-trophy probabilities before the final (not a raw input); it matters only while the key finals are undecided and is deterministic afterwards.

soc.player_minutes_expectation.reason: Live for KXBALLONDOR 2027, which trades months before the 2026-27 window closes: remaining minutes decide final and tournament contributions; inert only after the window closes.

soc.injuries.reason: Live while the eligibility window is open (KXBALLONDOR 2027 trades from November 2026): a long injury removes remaining contribution and trophy chances; no effect after the window closes.

soc.finishing_regression.reason: Voters judge realised totals, so regression matters only pre-close for expected remaining output; weak because the remaining production is a small share of the season record.

m.rules_text.reason: Needed for co-winner split and no-award clauses.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook outright prices are market-derived and are only a calibration benchmark.

soc.shots.reason: Shot counts do not matter to voters beyond the goals they produce.

soc.award_vote_distribution.reason: This is the fitted vote-share distribution (a model output of the conditional logit), not a raw input; it is retained as the modelled target distribution, secondary to the trophy and narrative features that drive it.

interactions.mechanism: A player's vote share multiplies trophy weight by individual narrative: a Champions League winner with the key goal gets disproportionately more votes than the winner's teammate, so team success and individual role multiply rather than add.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare an additive-utility softmax with and without a trophy x decisive-contribution product term by likelihood ratio and leave-one-year-out log score; if the product term adds nothing, the effect is additive.

interactions.mechanism: In tournament years a single international winner can concentrate first-place votes, so the vote-share spread among top candidates is wider and the aggregation noise matters less than in non-tournament years when several club-trophy winners split the vote (hypothesis).
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the margin between first and second by tournament-year status and test whether the fitted softmax temperature differs by regime.

interactions.mechanism: Before a credible leak the market is in a model-driven regime; after it, probability jumps to near certainty regardless of the model, so the model prior is replaced by the reliability of the source. This is a reliability-weighted Bayesian update, listed as an interaction only in the sense that the update weight depends on the source tier; it is not a separate structural channel.
interactions.how_to_test: Event study of price/probability around leak timestamps.

interactions.mechanism: Precursor award results matter more when the Champions League final has been played and is undecided for the leader, because the leaders are already narrowed; before the final they are weaker evidence.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast predictiveness of precursor awards by timing relative to major final.

interactions.mechanism: The Golden Ball and the Golden Boot both load on a forward whose team reaches the final, so they co-occur far more often than independence implies; a combo priced as the product of marginals is too low for the favourite and too high for scorers on teams likely to exit early.
interactions.how_to_test: Count historical editions where the Golden Ball winner also topped scoring and compare with the product of marginal frequencies.

nonlinearities.shape: Softmax saturation: vote share concentrated in top two candidates
nonlinearities.why: Utility differences translate to win probability through a softmax, so a gap of one utility unit moves the leader from 50% to 73% while the tail candidates stay near zero.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function at tournament-final result
nonlinearities.why: Winning the Champions League or the World Cup produces a discrete jump in utility rather than a gradual change.
