contract.settlement_definition: Twenty player-tally series, all with rules text. League leaders: YES when the player has the highest regular-season total of goals (Bundesliga, La Liga, Serie A, Ligue 1, Liga MX Apertura, MLS) or assists (KXEPLLEADER, and KXUCLLEADER for the UCL tournament) per official league statistics; goals for several clubs in the league combine, a player who plays no games resolves No, and a tie with no official tiebreak is a dead heat (KXLEADERUCLGOALS: $1/N rounded down). KXEPLSEASONSTAT: N+ goals across all games of the EPL season. World Cup series: the anytime-goal, goal-count, trio, country-top-scorer and streak texts include regulation, stoppage and extra time; those and the Golden Boot total and record texts exclude shootout goals; the career, goal-leader and Mbappe-record texts state no window. Series cover scoring at all (no entry = No), N+ goals including the third-place match, Golden Boot leader with FIFA tiebreaks (most assists, then fewest minutes), country top scorer ($1/N dead heat, 'No Goalscorer' leg), Golden Boot winner's total 15+, a named trio's combined 22+, a 9+ match scoring streak across 2022 and 2026 in matches entered, any player beating 13 goals, Mbappe becoming sole all-time leader in a named round, and career 40+ World Cup goals. Own goals are excluded explicitly in the career, Golden Boot total, streak and record texts (and are not credited to the scorer elsewhere).

rules_evidence.quote: If Yoane Wissa records 14+ goals across all games during the 2026-27 EPL season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Season-total threshold N+ for a named player across the EPL season; floor 13.5 means the rung is 14 goals; whether cup games count is a wording question.

rules_evidence.quote: must have the highest total goals across the entire regular season as documented by the official league statistics
rules_evidence.establishes: Leader races settle on official league statistics for the regular season only, so playoff or cup goals do not count and the provider is the league.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple players finish tied for the most goals and the league does not officially declare a single leader through a tiebreaker, the market will resolve as a dead heat.
rules_evidence.establishes: A shared lead pays a dead-heat share unless the league names a single leader, so the tie probability enters the price of every close candidate.

rules_evidence.quote: Own goals scored by Kylian Mbappe do not count for purposes of this market. 3rd place game goals are included in total goals scored.
rules_evidence.establishes: World Cup career totals count only tournament (not qualifier) goals, include the third-place match and exclude own goals.

rules_evidence.quote: settlement will follow FIFA’s official Golden Boot tiebreaker rules: first, most assists; if still tied, fewest minutes played
rules_evidence.establishes: The World Cup goal-leader race has no dead heat: ties are broken by assists then minutes, so assists and playing time enter the price of close candidates.

rules_evidence.quote: If no goals are scored, the No Goalscorer market will resolve to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Country top-scorer markets include a no-scorer leg and (per the text) split tied leaders 1/N, so the joint distribution of a squad's tournament goals is required.

rules_evidence.quote: If Lionel Messi does not enter a game, that game does not count towards the streak.
rules_evidence.establishes: The streak is defined over matches entered across two tournaments, so history from 2022 is part of the state and non-appearances do not break it.

rules_evidence.quote: must have the highest total assists across the entire tournament as documented by the official league statistics
rules_evidence.establishes: Assist-leader races exist (UCL and EPL), so assist attribution and chance-creation share, not only goals, drive part of this key.

variants_and_edge_cases: Leader markets: dead heat if tied and the league declares no single leader ($1/N in KXLEADERUCLGOALS), goals for several clubs within the league combined, a candidate who plays no games resolves No; Liga MX and MLS use the Apertura/regular season only.
Assist leaders (KXEPLLEADER, KXUCLLEADER) depend on the provider's assist attribution, a noisier and more definition-sensitive count than goals.

World Cup series run over three to eight matches per team: the number of matches a player can play depends on his team's progress, the third-place match counts for goal counts and career totals, extra time counts and shootouts do not.

Path-dependent World Cup series: KXWCGOALSTREAK (consecutive matches entered with a goal across 2022 and 2026), KXWCMBAPPEGOALLEADER (the round in which he first becomes sole record holder, with a 'does not break record' leg), KXWCRECORD (any player above 13), KXWCGOALCOMBO (sum of a named trio).

KXEPLSEASONSTAT 'across all games during the 2026-27 EPL season' leaves the counting scope (league only vs all competitions) to interpretation; KXWCPLAYERGOALS resolves No (not void) if the player never enters.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league statistics (goals/assists, regular season or tournament) as documented by the league or UEFA; FIFA official tournament records and Golden Boot tiebreaks for World Cup series; own goals and shootout goals excluded.

mechanism.summary: For a season total or a leader market the outcome is the realised tally at the deadline: expected goals equals matches times minutes survival times team chance volume times the player's share times finishing, with penalty duty adding a discrete block. Minutes are a survival process with a zero-inflated left tail; finishing luck must be shrunk; teammates and managers change the share mid-season. A leader market is the maximum of many correlated tallies, so variance and tie rules matter as much as means. World Cup goal series run over at most about eight tournament matches, so they are short count processes; leader rules settle on official regular-season statistics with a dead heat when no tiebreak is declared and No for a player who never plays, while the EPL stat ladder counting scope is not visible. For World Cup series the number of matches played is itself random through the team's bracket path, and streak, record and combined series need match-by-match joint simulation.

stages.name: Availability and minutes over the remaining season
stages.description: A player's tally can only grow while he plays; the remaining-season minutes distribution is determined by the injury hazard (with history of recurrence), suspensions, rotation and the risk of leaving the competition (winter transfer, loan), so expected minutes is a survival-type quantity. A starter with 85% of minutes in the first 12 games can lose a quarter of the remaining season to a single injury.
stages.distribution: Survival and recurrence process; minutes are zero-inflated with a mass at 0 (injury) and a bulk near 80-90 per start; heavy left tail.

stages.name: Per-match goal or assist intensity
stages.description: Per 90 the player scores according to shot volume, shot quality and finishing, plus penalty duty; role in the team (focal striker vs shared) determines the share of team xG, and teammate arrivals or departures change that share. Per-match intensity is combined with the opponent's defence and the team's expected goals for that fixture. Assist races (EPL, UCL) replace shot share by chance-creation share, set-piece delivery duty and teammates' finishing, which add noise beyond the passer's own skill.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial-like per-match counts; strong dependence on set pieces and penalties; season totals are overdispersed relative to a Poisson with the mean xG.

stages.name: Luck versus skill in current tally
stages.description: The running total includes finishing over- or under-performance relative to xG which should be regressed toward the player's multi-season baseline; a striker at 12 goals from 7 xG is a regression candidate while another at 7 from 12 xG is not. The shrinkage fraction is large over a half season.
stages.distribution: Poisson noise plus persistent skill; finishing skill persists weakly (persistence share to be estimated; 20-30% is a placeholder).

stages.name: Race dynamics across candidates
stages.description: Leader markets are decided by the maximum across many correlated candidates: teammates compete for the same chances, candidates share fixtures, and ties and tiebreaks matter; the probability a candidate is first depends on the gap to the leader and on how many rivals are within reach, not on his own mean alone.
stages.distribution: Order-statistic outcome from a vector of correlated overdispersed counts; the maximum rewards variance (high-volume strikers with injury risk).

stages.name: Tournament exposure set by the team's progress
stages.description: In World Cup series a player's tally is bounded by how many matches his nation plays: three group games, then up to five knockout games including the third-place match. The distribution of matches played comes from the team's group and bracket simulation, so a striker on a likely semi-finalist has roughly twice the exposure of an equal striker on a likely group exit; extra-time minutes add exposure in drawn knockouts. Per-match scoring intensity is multiplied by this random number of matches.
stages.distribution: Discrete number of matches (3-8) from the bracket simulation, mixed with per-match negative-binomial goals; the mixture is strongly right-skewed for elite teams.

stages.name: Settlement scope, dead heat and DNP
stages.description: The contract reads the official league total for the regular season (or all EPL games for the stat ladder, World Cup tournament games for career goals): goals for two clubs within the league are combined, a candidate with no appearances resolves No, and a tie with no official tiebreak pays a dead-heat share; parsing scope and dead-heat rules per series avoids label errors in training data.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from official statistics; scope ambiguity is the only randomness.

stages.name: Path-dependent and combined tournament tallies
stages.description: Some World Cup series depend on the order or combination of goals: a streak of consecutive matches entered with a goal (carried over from 2022), the round in which a career record is first broken outright, whether any player passes 13 goals, and the sum of three named strikers. These need match-by-match simulation of each player's goals jointly with his team's path, keeping correlation between teammates and the record state, rather than end-of-tournament marginal totals.
stages.distribution: Sequential Bernoulli/negative-binomial per match; streak and record events are rare tail events with probabilities often below 5%, and trio sums are overdispersed through shared team paths.

talent_strength.note: Per-90 scoring rates with opponent context; leaders are the top of a talent distribution.

opponent_matchup.note: Fixture difficulty and set-piece opportunity for each candidate.

role_personnel.note: Role, penalty duty, share of team shots, minutes.

availability_news.note: Injury hazard and news flow; long horizon so status vintage matters less than hazard.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager changes alter a striker's role and service, and a tactical shift (system change, new playmaker) can change goals per 90 by 20-30% in the middle of a season; no input quantifies this and press-conference news does not capture it.

environment.note: Weather and pitch effects on a single player's goal count are small and average out over dozens of matches; their impact is already in the per-90 rate, so no separate environmental input is required for a season total.

game_context_script.note: Current tally, matches remaining and the position relative to the leader.

pace_volume.note: Team chance volume (team xG) and the player's share of it set the number of scoring opportunities; raw shots (WEAK) are not used as cover.

distribution_variance.note: Order-statistic race simulations and dispersion of totals.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Congestion and rotation across competitions act through expected minutes and the minutes-survival curve; the WEAK soc.lineups_pit is not used as cover.

officiating_rules.note: Referee identity affects penalties awarded to a given team only slightly over a season and averages out; it matters at the match level for first-event contracts, not for season-long leader totals, so no officiating input is attached here.

settlement_contract.note: Counting scope, tie rules, own-goal and disallowed-goal handling.

soc.team_goal_share_competition.label: Player's share of team npxG and competition for it
soc.team_goal_share_competition.mechanism: Share of team non-penalty xG taken by the player and how it changes with teammates.
soc.team_goal_share_competition.rationale: A player's goal rate equals team chance volume times his share; new signings, injuries to teammates and system changes redistribute shares in ways that per-90 averages miss, and a shared striker role halves volume in expectation.
soc.team_goal_share_competition.measurement: share_i = player npxG / team npxG over the last 20 matches (half-life 10) with shrinkage to position-role mean at k=8 matches; projected share = share adjusted by indicator of teammate arrivals/departures and rotation (regress change in share on competitor strength); expected goals = team npxG projection x share x P(playing).
raw_data: player-level shots and xG by match
soc.team_goal_share_competition.why: Separates team volume from role share, the quantity that changes when squads change.

soc.season_minutes_survival_curve.label: Remaining-season minutes survival curve
soc.season_minutes_survival_curve.mechanism: Survival function of availability over the remaining matches including recurrence.
soc.season_minutes_survival_curve.rationale: Minutes are the multiplier on every per-90 rate and are far from deterministic; injury recurrence, age and load create a left-skewed distribution; the cumulative effect over 25+ matches is what the season total needs.
soc.season_minutes_survival_curve.measurement: Cox / discrete-time hazard model for injury onset per match with covariates age, previous injuries in 24 months, minutes last 28 days, position; plus duration model for time-out; simulate remaining season for each candidate; expected minutes and its quantiles; shrink the baseline hazard to the position mean with k=30 player-seasons.
raw_data: injury episodes with dates and durations
soc.season_minutes_survival_curve.why: Gives tails (long-term injury) that a mean minutes input misses.

soc.leader_tiebreak_and_scope.label: Leader tie rule and counting scope flags
soc.leader_tiebreak_and_scope.mechanism: Contract-level flags for tie handling and which competitions count.
soc.leader_tiebreak_and_scope.rationale: Leader prices are sensitive to whether a tie pays 1/n, goes to assists or minutes, or resolves No for all; and 'all games' versus 'league games' changes the tally by cup goals.
soc.leader_tiebreak_and_scope.measurement: Parse and version rules_primary/secondary of each leader and season-stat series into flags: scope {league_only, all_competitions}, tie_rule {split, tiebreak_assists, tiebreak_minutes, official_source}, own_goal handling; resolution source; store with version hash and timestamp; for unsampled series mark UNKNOWN and require manual confirmation before use.
raw_data: rules text by series with timestamps
soc.leader_tiebreak_and_scope.why: Without it the same player goal tally is labelled differently across leader markets.

soc.player_tournament_match_exposure.label: Player's distribution of tournament matches and minutes from team progression
soc.player_tournament_match_exposure.mechanism: A player's tournament goal tally is bounded by the number of matches his team plays, which is random and set by the bracket.
soc.player_tournament_match_exposure.rationale: World Cup goal counts, leaders, top scorers, streaks and record series all scale with matches played; equal per-90 scorers on teams with different progression odds have very different tallies. The subtle part is that progression and scoring are positively correlated (a team goes further partly because its striker scores).
soc.player_tournament_match_exposure.measurement: From the tournament simulation (N>=100,000 draws) take per team the number of matches played (3-8, third-place match included) and extra-time periods; multiply by the player's start probability and expected minutes per start (last 12 international matches, shrunk to role prior with k=6) to get a minutes distribution; simulate per-match goals jointly with match outcomes so correlation is preserved; update after each match day.
soc.player_tournament_match_exposure.why: Sets the exposure that multiplies per-match scoring for every World Cup tally series.

soc.leader_race_state.reason: Current tally, matches remaining and expected minutes are the state variables for the race simulation.

soc.player_xg.reason: Non-penalty xG/90 is the rate input; should be combined with team share and minutes survival.

soc.player_minutes_expectation.reason: Minutes multiplies the rate; needs a survival distribution not a point estimate.

soc.penalty_taker_status.reason: Penalties are 10-20% of a top scorer's goals; designated taker status is a discrete share determinant.

soc.finishing_regression.reason: Needed to avoid extrapolating hot finishing, though shrinkage is already built into the xG-based rate.

soc.injuries.reason: Current status matters, but the longer horizon is better served by the survival curve.

soc.remaining_schedule_strength.reason: Opponent quality changes expected goals modestly for 20+ remaining matches.

soc.set_pieces.reason: Set-piece role is partly in xG; needed mainly for aerial forwards.

soc.award_voting_narrative.reason: No voted-award series remains in this key after the reconciliation (awards moved to player_award); leader and goal-count races do not depend on narrative or votes.

soc.player_awards.reason: Remaining-season Poisson race simulation is the same computation as the leader race-state input.

m.rules_text.reason: Tie rule and scope must be parsed per series; not a predictor.

soc.shots.reason: Raw shots add little over xG for finishing-driven goal counts.

soc.xg.reason: Team-level xG (team chance volume) is the first factor of the expected-goals product (team volume x player share x minutes); it is not a duplicate of player xG/90, and it is used through soc.team_goal_share_competition and the remaining-fixture chance volume.

soc.lineups_pit.reason: Timestamped match lineups matter for single matches, not for a season-long total; marginal once the survival curve exists.

soc.press_conference_news.reason: News flows matter only for injuries and transfers; weak, noisy signal for a season-long contract.

soc.assist_set_piece_role.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s2) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

soc.bracket_path_difficulty.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s5) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

soc.group_stage_scenarios.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s5) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: Expected goals is the factorisation team volume x share x minutes survival; the interaction of interest is that zero-inflated minutes make the exceedance probability of a rung lower than a mean-based Poisson suggests only when the mean is at or above the rung, and higher when the mean is well below it (the skewed minutes distribution widens both tails).
interactions.how_to_test: Compare probability of crossing the strike from simulation with mean-only prediction.

interactions.mechanism: The probability of finishing first depends on tie rules: if ties split payouts, a candidate level with the leader has half the value, and if ties resolve on assists the playmaker striker gains; the gap-to-leader effect is conditional on the tie rule.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate leader markets under each tie rule and compare to observed settlements.

interactions.mechanism: The expected future scoring rate is a shrunk mix of a hot finishing record and xG; the weight on realised goals decays with sample size, so equal over-performance is worth much less in a long remaining season.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest forward goals/90 on past npxG and past goals with an interaction in sample size.

interactions.mechanism: Penalty duty adds roughly the team penalty rate times conversion (for example 0.15 team penalties per match x about 0.78 = about 0.1 goals per match) for the designated taker only; the gain is a product of the taker flag and the team penalty rate, not a threshold, and varies with referee and VAR habits.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress goals on designated-taker flag and team penalty rate.

interactions.mechanism: Tournament tallies are per-match intensity times a random match count, and the two are positively correlated because a team advances partly through its striker's goals; ignoring this correlation under-prices high totals (record, 11+ goals) and over-prices middling ones.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated tally distributions with and without joint goal-and-progression simulation against past World Cup top-scorer totals.

nonlinearities.shape: Left-skewed, zero-inflated minutes distribution
nonlinearities.why: Minutes are bimodal at injury (0) and full-minutes outcomes; linear expectations misprice exceedance probabilities for round-number rungs.

nonlinearities.shape: Sigmoid in gap to leader scaled by sqrt(remaining expected goals)
nonlinearities.why: Probability of overtaking depends on gap relative to the sd of remaining goals; the 2-goal and 5-goal breakpoints are placeholders to be estimated from the race simulation.

nonlinearities.shape: Shrinkage weight rising with sample size
nonlinearities.why: Predictive weight on observed over-performance grows with shots taken, roughly n/(n+k) with k to be estimated (about 100 shots is a placeholder).

contract.settlement_definition: Table series settle on the final official table: last place (single bottom rank), relegation ('is relegated from'), promotion ('is promoted from the EFL Championship', play-off route included), and UCL league-phase bottom. Tie series settle YES when the named side 'advance[s] past' its opponent in the named tie and round (finals add 'and lift the cup'; KXMLSADVANCE and KXINTERCUPADVANCE state 'including extra time and penalties'); legs and away-goals treatment are inherited from the competition. Qualification and stage-reach series (KXUCLQUAL, KXWCQUAL, KXUCLRO16/RO8/RO4/FINALIST, KXUCL16xxx, KXWCROUND, KXWCGROUPQUAL) settle on qualifying for the named stage even if the team then does not compete. KXUCLMOV splits a final into Regular Time / Extra Time / Penalty Shootout advancement. World Cup aggregate series settle on stage reached by sets of teams (furthest advancing nation of a confederation with a $1/N dead heat, stage of elimination with a withdrawal rule, counts of debutants or hosts reaching the knockouts).

rules_evidence.quote: If Tottenham finishes in last place in the league table in the 2026-27 EPL season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Last-place market is a single bottom rank in the final table; it is not the same as relegation (bottom three), so the probability is an extreme-value event with its own tiebreak exposure.

rules_evidence.quote: If Palmeiras advance past Fluminense in the Palmeiras vs Fluminense soccer tie in the Semi-Finals of the CONMEBOL Libertadores, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Advancement resolves on who progresses from the named tie (both legs), not on a single match result, so first-leg state, away-goals rules and ET/penalties belong to the event.

rules_evidence.quote: If Latina advance past Grosseto in the Grosseto vs Latina soccer tie in the Round 2 of the Coppa Italia Lega Pro, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Same wording is used for single-leg cup ties, where advancement includes extra time and penalties, so the format (one leg vs two) is per competition and has to be looked up.

rules_evidence.quote: If Villarreal finishes in last place in the league table in the 2026-27 La Liga season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Confirms last-place wording is identical across leagues but tiebreak order (head-to-head in La Liga) differs by competition.

rules_evidence.quote: if they qualify but do not end up competing, the market will still resolve to Yes
rules_evidence.establishes: Nations League qualification settles on qualifying, not on taking part in the next round.

rules_evidence.quote: Extra Time: Resolves to Yes if the specified team advances after extra time is played, but before any penalty shootout occurs.
rules_evidence.establishes: The method-of-advancing series partitions a final into regulation, extra-time and shootout wins, so the regulation/ET/penalty path tree is required for this key.

rules_evidence.quote: Yes payout: $1/N, rounded down to the nearest cent (N = number of tied participants)
rules_evidence.establishes: Furthest-advancing-nation contracts dead-heat when several nations reach the same stage, so P(tie at the furthest stage) enters the price.

rules_evidence.quote: Advancing to a later stage of qualification without securing a place in the main tournament does not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: Champions League qualification series settle on a main-tournament place, so qualifying rounds and slot allocation (including spillover slots) define the event.

rules_evidence.quote: Teams can qualify by either finishing in the top 8 of the league phase table or by winning their respective knockout phase play-off.
rules_evidence.establishes: Reaching the round of 16 is a union of a league-phase rank event and a play-off tie event, needing both the league-phase simulation and the tie tree.

rules_evidence.quote: If all host nations qualify for the knockout stage in the 2026 Men's FIFA World Cup
rules_evidence.establishes: An all-hosts intersection settled on knockout qualification; modelled from the joint stage-reached vector with host advantage on home matches.

variants_and_edge_cases: Last-place and relegation have different cut lines: 'last place' needs the single lowest points total and its tiebreak (La Liga/Serie A head-to-head first, Premier League goal difference first), while relegation is bottom-N and also affected by relegation play-offs in some leagues (Bundesliga 16th-place play-off, Ligue 1).

Qualification series settle on qualifying, not competing (KXUCLROUND, KXUCLRO16, KXWCROUND: 'if they qualify but do not end up competing, the market will still resolve to Yes'); KXUCLQUAL requires a main-tournament place, so slot spillover and qualifying rounds are part of the event.

Advancement series pool single-leg cups, two-leg Libertadores/Sudamericana ties, play-offs and World Cup group qualification (best-third-place rule); the number of legs, ET/penalties and away-goals treatment are competition-specific and not in the sampled text.

176 live series, 91 with rules text; 85 TITLE_ONLY (mostly league and cup 'Advance' series, KXBRASILEIRORELEGATION, KXWCHOSTSTAGE). Final-tie series add 'and lift the cup'; a sanction-driven table change after the last match is not addressed.

World Cup aggregate series: KXWCSTAGE (furthest stage by any team of a confederation pathway), KXWCSTAGEOFELIM (stage of elimination; a withdrawing team is assigned the next stage), KXWCFURTHESTADVANCING ($1/N dead heat), KXWCREGIONKO ('exactly N' debutants reach the knockouts), KXWCHOSTKO (all hosts), KXWC3RDPLACEQUAL, KXWCFIFATOP10 (any non-top-10 nation reaches the semi-finals).

Single-match items filed here: KXWCADVANCE text is 'wins the 3rd Place ... game' (window not stated), KXMLSADVANCE and KXINTERCUPADVANCE include extra time and penalties with a two-week postponement clause.

mechanism.summary: Placement and advancement events are threshold events on random objects. For tables, each team's final points come from simulated remaining fixtures with uncertain strengths; last place is the minimum of closely spaced totals, relegation or top-N is a rank threshold whose cut line itself depends on cup winners, play-offs and sanctions. For ties, advancement is a sequential tree: first-leg state, second-leg goals shaped by aggregate lead, extra time with fatigue, and a near-coin-flip shootout. Group qualification adds tiebreak order and best-third rankings. Injuries, manager changes and administrative rulings are the shocks, and settlement depends on the competition's own regulations and tie rules.

stages.name: Team strength with uncertainty
stages.description: Both sides of a bubble race and both sides of a tie begin with opponent-adjusted strength and its posterior width; for bottom-of-table and last-place events the weakest teams are separated by small rating differences, so uncertainty width and short-memory form (new manager, injuries) dominate rankings among the bottom five.
stages.distribution: Posterior of latent strength with sd to be estimated (about 0.1 log goals is a placeholder); bottom-N membership is an order statistic of closely spaced values.

stages.name: Table state and the schedule left to play
stages.description: Remaining fixtures determine how points can still be earned: points gap to the cut line, number of matches remaining, strength and venue of the opposition (including direct clashes between rivals for survival or a slot), all of which determine a team's distribution of final points relative to the line. Bottom-six clubs dismiss managers often, so the remaining-fixture simulation draws in-season dismissals from soc.manager_dismissal_hazard (driven by simulated winless runs and points below expectation) and applies the re-blended post-change rating from soc.transfers; the new-manager bounce magnitude stays at zero until estimated, since much of it is mean reversion.
stages.distribution: Sum of remaining match lotteries (0/1/3); variance of gap relative to cut line scales with matches remaining.

stages.name: Where the cut line sits
stages.description: For relegation, promotion and qualification the line is not fixed: relegation can be shifted by play-offs (Bundesliga 16th place) or deductions, promotion runs partly through a play-off mini-tournament, and Champions League qualification depends on coefficient slots and on cup winners already holding a place. KXUCLQUAL settles on a main-tournament place, so spillover and qualifying rounds move its effective threshold; last-place and relegation series settle on rank only. Promotion and relegation play-offs are an explicit bracket (soc.promotion_relegation_playoff_bracket): P(promoted) = P(automatic rank) + sum over play-off ranks of P(rank) x P(win bracket | rank). KXEFLPROMO is for 2026-27, for which a secondary web search (no primary EFL text on disk) reports a six-team Championship play-off for 3rd-8th, with the final format reported as pending; round structure, legs, host rule and tie-break are therefore format parameters to be encoded once the rules are read, not assumptions. KXLALIGA2PROMO (sampled series text covers 2025-26 and states no play-off rule) is modelled on a Segunda play-off where secondary sources report that a level tie after extra time goes to the better-placed side; the pairings, number of legs and the absence of away goals or penalties are unverified.
stages.distribution: Discrete random threshold determined by cup winners and administrative rulings; effect is 0 or 1 place shifts with probabilities to be estimated (10-30% is a placeholder) in the cup-spillover case.

stages.name: Tie formats: legs, extra time and penalties
stages.description: An advancement market is the product of a first-leg state, a second-leg match, and then if needed extra time and penalties; the first-leg score, the venue of the second leg, and the team's priorities in the next league match drive risk-taking, and shootouts are close to coin flips. Away goals no longer decide UEFA ties but may in some national cups. KXUCLMOV maps the same tree onto three outcomes (advance in regular time, after extra time, via shootout), so the branch probabilities themselves are traded.
stages.distribution: Sequential probability tree; aggregate lead changes the match goal rate and draw probability; shootout win near 50% with small skill edge.

stages.name: Group-stage qualification and cross-group ranking
stages.description: Group qualification (World Cup, Nations League, Champions League league phase) depends on points, goal difference, head-to-head and in expanded formats on ranking third-placed teams across groups; the order of tiebreaks and the final-day simultaneous matches create strong dependencies between teams. KXUCLRO16 (top 8 or win the knockout play-off) and KXUCLBOTTOM (36th place) need the 36-team league-phase simulation over eight unbalanced fixtures rather than a group table.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution across teams and groups; tie-breaks create discrete jumps in qualification.

stages.name: Squad shocks and administrative events
stages.description: Injuries, international absences and suspensions shift strength during the run-in; sanctions (points deductions, licensing, administration) move teams across the line administratively, with probability mass concentrated at lower-profile leagues.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed strength shocks and rare discrete administrative events.

stages.name: Stage reached by sets of teams in a bracket tournament
stages.description: World Cup and UCL stage-reach series ask how far one team or a set of teams goes: the furthest stage by any nation of a qualification pathway, which host or which confederation nation goes furthest (dead heat if several share the stage), exactly N debutants reaching the knockouts, all hosts qualifying, or a non-top-10 nation reaching the semi-finals. These are functions of the joint stage-reached vector: bracket placement makes teams of the same group or half negatively dependent, so counts and maxima over a set cannot be built from independent marginals, and tie probabilities at a stage must be kept for the $1/N payouts. Host series (KXWCHOSTKO: all three hosts reach the knockout stage; KXWCHOSTSTAGE) apply soc.home_advantage to each host's group matches in its own country; KXWCHOSTKO is an intersection over hosts in different groups, so it is the product of near-independent group-qualification probabilities, each lifted by the host edge.
stages.distribution: Joint categorical vector of stages reached per team; counts over a set are dependent-Bernoulli sums, maxima have heavy mass at the round of 32 and round of 16.

talent_strength.note: Strength distribution with posterior width, needed particularly for tightly spaced bottom teams.

opponent_matchup.note: Direct clashes between rivals and group opponents.

availability_news.note: Availability news; matters for ties more than for season-long placement.

coaching_scheme.note: In-season dismissal hazard for relegation-threatened clubs and the post-change rating re-blend; bounce size empirical.

environment.note: Weather, altitude and pitch affect single matches and their influence on season placement averages out; for ties, neutral-site venues are encoded in the aggregate-state and home-advantage logic rather than as a separate environmental input.

game_context_script.note: Aggregate and table state set risk posture and win probabilities.

pace_volume.note: Volume stats such as possession or shots matter only via the goal-model strengths feeding the simulation; no independent volume variable determines a table position or tie advancement, so no pace input is attached.

distribution_variance.note: Order-statistic and tail structure of the table, especially at the bottom.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Dead-rubber and priority rotation effects come from soc.rotation_index (predicted rotation) and break effects; soc.stakes_leverage and soc.motivation are simulation outputs (WEAK/duplicate) and are not cited as cover.

officiating_rules.note: Administrative sanctions, abandonment and voided matches.

settlement_contract.note: Tiebreaks, slot allocation and the contract wording.

soc.european_slot_spillover.label: European slot spillover and variable cut line
soc.european_slot_spillover.mechanism: Probability distribution of the number of European places a league gets and how many reach the table.
soc.european_slot_spillover.rationale: A top-4 or qualification contract refers to a cut line that moves: the UEFA coefficient determines league allocation, and a domestic cup winner already qualified through the league moves the places down the table; so a 'top 4' price for fifth place is a function of cup results. Applicable only if a series settles on European qualification; the live titles (KXEPLTOP4, KXLIGUE1TOP4, KXEPLTOP2, KXEPLTOP6, KXUCLTOP8) read as table-rank cut lines and are TITLE_ONLY, so this input is context until a qualification-based series is confirmed.
soc.european_slot_spillover.measurement: Stochastic spillover only: the static allocation rules (base UEFA places by coefficient, cup-winner replacement, title-holder entry) are read from soc.tiebreaker_rules and not re-encoded here; this input adds the simulated probability E that a domestic cup winner already holds a higher European slot, from the cup simulation, giving the effective cut line L = base - E for top-N and qualification series; recompute after each cup round with the as-of date stamped.
soc.european_slot_spillover.why: Makes the qualification threshold a random variable rather than a constant, which the table simulation alone omits.

soc.last_place_extreme_value.label: Bottom-of-table extreme-value distribution
soc.last_place_extreme_value.mechanism: Probability each team ends with the lowest points total, and the gap structure at the bottom.
soc.last_place_extreme_value.rationale: Last place is the minimum of correlated points totals; the favourite for last place often has only 25-40% because others are within a few points, and the shape is not a simple function of a team's own rating.
soc.last_place_extreme_value.measurement: From the posterior-sampled season simulation: for each team compute P(rank=N), P(rank in bottom 3), gap to 3rd bottom and to 4th bottom at each as-of date; calibrate with historical bottom-team final points (shrunk league mean with k=5 seasons); correct tie rules in the minimum.
soc.last_place_extreme_value.why: Last-place contracts are minimum order statistics and are not equal to relegation odds.

soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.label: Advancement tree for single-leg and two-leg ties
soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.mechanism: Round-by-round conditional probabilities given the legs, the first-leg score and the tie rules.
soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.rationale: Advancement is a state-dependent tree: after a first-leg win by 1-0, the second leg's draw/win probabilities differ from a pre-leg symmetrical model; format rules (ET, penalties, away goals) then determine the remaining branch.
soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.measurement: Tie-rule composition layer, not a second copy of the aggregate state: the state multipliers (trailing/leader risk posture, aggregate deficit) are read from soc.second_leg_aggregate_state, which is the only place they are estimated; this input adds the competition-season rule table (single leg vs two legs, extra time played or straight to penalties, no away-goals rule) and composes P(advance) = P(aggregate win in 90) + P(aggregate level) * (P(ET win) + P(pens win)) from that table, with shrinkage k=40 ties per competition and as-of prior seasons only.
raw_data: tie results with leg scores, ET, penalties
soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.why: Provides the structured tree the existing inputs (aggregate state, ET model, shootout skill) only describe separately.

soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.label: Joint distribution of tournament placings from a full group-and-bracket simulation
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.mechanism: Union, exact-order and any-group-winner contracts are functions of the joint placings of many teams, which bracket structure makes dependent.
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.rationale: Summing marginal title odds is right only for disjoint unions; exact orders (KXWCFINISHINGORDER, KXWCGROUPORDER) and 'any nation of a set wins its group' need the joint draw, and group-mates are negatively correlated. Tiebreak rules and the best-third-place allocation make the dependence discrete and non-trivial.
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.measurement: Monte Carlo of the full competition (N>=200,000 draws) from current team ratings with posterior rating draws per simulation, official group composition, FIFA/UEFA tiebreak order, best-third allocation table and bracket; store per draw each team's placing (group rank, stage reached, final placing 1-4); contract probabilities are frequencies of the defining event; rerun at each as-of time after every match day.
soc.tournament_joint_finish_distribution.why: Prices stage-reach counts, maxima and $1/N dead heats over sets of teams (furthest-advancing confederation nation, debutant and host counts, non-top-10 semi-finalist) from the per-draw stage-reached vector; the same simulation already serves competition_winner_and_top_n.

soc.promotion_relegation_playoff_bracket.label: Promotion and relegation play-off bracket conversion
soc.promotion_relegation_playoff_bracket.mechanism: Maps the simulated regular-season rank to the probability of promotion (or survival) through the competition's post-season play-off bracket, tie by tie, under that season's format rules.
soc.promotion_relegation_playoff_bracket.rationale: Promotion series settle on being promoted by any route, so ranks 3-8 (EFL Championship from 2026-27) or 3-6 (Segunda) carry probability through a short knockout: the format decides how much rank matters. For 2026-27 a secondary web search reports a six-team EFL Championship play-off for 3rd-8th (round structure, hosts and tie-break not verified from primary text; final format reported as pending); if there is an early round that 3rd and 4th skip, 5th-8th face an extra gate of roughly 50% (an estimate, not sourced). In Segunda a level tie after extra time is reported by secondary sources to go to the better-placed side, which would tilt every tie toward the higher seed with no shootout coin-flip; whether away goals or penalties play any role is unverified. Subtle: the Segunda reserve-team eligibility rule (filial sides) is unverified here and, if real, shifts which ranks qualify; formats change between seasons.
soc.promotion_relegation_playoff_bracket.measurement: Per competition-season, encode the format: entrant ranks, round structure, legs, host rule, away-goals (none in either), extra time and tie-break (EFL: ET then penalties assumed as default, unverified for the 2026-27 format; Segunda: ET then higher regular-season rank per secondary sources, remaining rules unverified). For each simulated final table, simulate each tie with team goal rates from the as-of ratings: single legs via soc.extra_time_shootout_model at the higher seed's venue, two-leg ties via soc.tie_advancement_state_tree (second leg at the higher seed), Segunda ties replacing the shootout branch with P=1 for the higher seed if the better-placed-side rule is confirmed from the regulations. P(promoted_i) = sum over simulated tables of [rank_i automatic] + [rank_i in play-off] x P(win bracket | bracket draw). Calibrate P(win bracket | seed) against 20 seasons of EFL and Segunda play-off results (Wilson intervals, shrink to the simulation with k=10 seasons). As-of: format rules published before the season; ratings as of the pricing timestamp.
free_sources: EFL and LaLiga official competition regulations (free)
raw_data: play-off format rules per competition-season (entrant ranks, legs, host, tie-break)
historical play-off ties with seeds, leg scores, extra time and shootout outcomes
soc.promotion_relegation_playoff_bracket.why: Converts the table simulation into promotion probability for KXEFLPROMO and KXLALIGA2PROMO, whose YES includes the play-off route.

soc.comp_sim.reason: Season simulation produces the table distributions; needs dynamic cut line and tiebreaks.

soc.stakes_leverage.reason: Leverage is an output of the same season simulation; using it as an input is circular for a placement forecast.

soc.tiebreaker_rules.reason: Head-to-head vs goal difference order alters last-place and cut-line outcomes in tight races.

soc.points_deductions.reason: Rare but decisive for administrative events; coverage in lower leagues is thin.

soc.group_stage_scenarios.reason: Required for group qualification markets, but it is a derived simulation, not an independent measurement.

soc.second_leg_aggregate_state.reason: Aggregate state is the primary driver of second-leg risk posture and the draw probability.

soc.extra_time_shootout_model.reason: ET goal rate and shootout probabilities determine the tail of the advancement tree.

soc.ratings_uncertainty.reason: Posterior width matters for bottom-of-table clusters.

soc.remaining_schedule_strength.reason: Schedule asymmetry is a first-order driver for survival races in the run-in.

soc.injuries.reason: Key injuries shift strength but season-long evidence of effect size is weak.

soc.international_break_effect.reason: Evidence for a systematic effect on league points is small and mostly absorbed by lineup availability.

m.rules_text.reason: Needed to know single-leg vs two-leg and ET/penalty rules; not a predictor.

soc.motivation.reason: Defined from the same season Monte Carlo leverage as stakes_leverage.

soc.penalty_shootout_skill.reason: Persistent shootout skill is statistically weak in available samples and only matters in a small share of ties.

soc.abandonment_risk.reason: Voided matches and abandoned competitions are rare but contract relevant.

soc.press_conference_news.reason: Noisy signal for injuries and rotation that matters only for ties; long-run placement markets barely respond.

soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.reason: Stage s2 draws in-season dismissals for each simulated path from this hazard (winless runs, points per game below ratings-implied expectation, tenure; Cox model on top-5 league changes) for relegation-zone clubs, so P(relegated) becomes a mixture over change paths; it supplies only the timing/probability of a change, not the rating shift (that is soc.transfers).

soc.rotation_index.reason: Stage s2: late-season rotation (dead rubbers, congested cup schedules) lowers a side's expected strength in specific remaining fixtures of the run-in, which the remaining-schedule simulation must apply per match rather than as a season average; context because the sign of the effect for cut-line clubs is not established.

soc.method_path_tree_calibration.reason: Stage s4: KXUCLMOV trades the regular-time / extra-time / penalty-shootout split of an advancement, so the tie tree's branch probabilities are calibrated against realised method-of-victory frequencies; only used for the MOV series, not for plain advancement or table markets.

soc.uefa_league_phase_simulation.reason: Stage s5: KXUCLRO16 (top 8 or win the knockout play-off) and KXUCLBOTTOM (36th place) are settled on the 36-team league-phase table over eight unbalanced fixtures, which a group-table model cannot represent; not used for domestic table series.

soc.home_advantage.reason: Stage s7: the host series (KXWCHOSTKO, KXWCHOSTSTAGE) lift each host nation's group-match strength by the home edge in its own country, applied before the joint stage-reached simulation; not needed for neutral-site or domestic table markets.

soc.transfers.reason: Stage s2 and the interaction [soc.manager_dismissal_hazard, soc.transfers, soc.comp_sim]: once a simulated path draws a dismissal, remaining fixtures use the re-blended rating w(m) x (pre-change rating + d_mc) + (1 - w(m)) x rating estimated under the new manager, with w(m)=6/(6+m) and the bounce shift d_mc held at 0 until estimated (much of it is mean reversion); the same input carries window-move squad-value shifts for early-season and post-window futures. Secondary: it changes the rating of a few clubs on a subset of paths, whereas the hazard decides whether a path switches.

interactions.mechanism: For qualification-settled series (KXUCLQUAL requires a main-tournament place per its text): a club finishing just outside the domestic Champions League places has a qualification probability that is a step function of whether a cup winner or coefficient slot frees an extra place, moving the cut line by one rank; rank-only series (last place, relegation) are unaffected.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare qualification probabilities with and without the cup-spillover branch in past seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Second-leg goal and draw rates depend on the first-leg lead: a two-goal leader plays deep, lowering both teams' rates, while a one-goal trailing team pushes; the advancement probability conditional on first-leg margin is nonlinear.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin second legs by first-leg margin and compare draw rates and goals.

interactions.mechanism: Last-place probability is convex in rating uncertainty because the minimum of several tightly clustered totals is more sensitive to variance than the mean; widening the posterior increases odds for the second-worst team more than it reduces the worst team's.
interactions.how_to_test: Scale the posterior sd by 0.5-1.5 and track P(last) of the bottom 3.

interactions.mechanism: Direct clashes among survival rivals create paths where points tie; the tiebreak order then decides, so schedule effects interact with tiebreak only in narrow finishing scenarios.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute frequency of tie-resolved placements in simulations by league.

interactions.mechanism: A pending deduction or a final-day simultaneous kickoff changes the competitive regime: the deducted team goes from fighting for survival to a dead-rubber, shifting rotation and draw rates for its rivals. (speculative: for a deducted team still fighting relegation the effect may be the opposite; treated as a hypothesis to be tested only on observed deductions)
interactions.how_to_test: Event study on matches following deduction announcements.

interactions.mechanism: When two nations of the same set share a group, at most one can win it and their knockout paths diverge, which lowers the expected count reaching the knockouts and raises the chance that the set's furthest stage is decided by one team; independence over-prices 'all hosts qualify' or 'exactly N debutants' outcomes when set members are drawn together.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare count-over-set probabilities from the joint simulation with an independent-marginals product for past World Cups.

interactions.mechanism: Relegation-zone clubs on a winless run have the highest dismissal hazard; a dismissal switches their rating regime for the remaining fixtures, so P(relegated) is a mixture over change paths and survival odds of a struggling club are not simply its current rating projected forward.
interactions.how_to_test: Event study of bottom-six points per game after in-season changes versus matched non-changing clubs, then compare relegation calibration with and without the dismissal branch.

interactions.mechanism: Promotion probability is piecewise in final rank: near-certain in automatic places, then a drop to the bracket win probability for 3rd-4th (semi only), and a further drop for 5th-8th if the 2026-27 six-team EFL format has an extra early round that 3rd and 4th skip (structure unverified, details pending); in Segunda, if a level tie after extra time goes to the better-placed side (secondary sources, unverified beyond that), rank matters more than under a shootout tie-break.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare historical promotion rates by final rank to the bracket-composed prediction, separately for EFL (pre and post 2026-27) and Segunda.

nonlinearities.shape: Roughly linear in games remaining (variance), collapsing to tiebreak-only in the last two rounds (not a saturating shape)
nonlinearities.why: Schedule asymmetry adds variance proportional to the number of games left and nearly vanishes in the final two rounds when only points and tiebreak matter.

nonlinearities.shape: Right-skewed minimum order statistic
nonlinearities.why: The distribution of the lowest total has a skewed shape, and linear rating-gap predictors understate the probability of surprises.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise by aggregate margin: 0, 1, 2+
nonlinearities.why: Aggregate leads change rates sharply at one goal and saturate beyond two as leaders sit deep.

contract.settlement_definition: Off-field event contracts that resolve on an official or credibly confirmed fact inside a window: a named player transferring out of a club before a date (KXLAMINEYAMAL, KXCLUBCHANGEMBAPPE: permanent transfers, loans of any duration and contract termination/expiry all count), the player's next club (a multi-outcome set; in KXJOINCLUB/KXJOINLEAGUE/KXMLSJOIN a sign-and-loan counts for the signing club and staying, re-signing or extending resolves the current club's outcome Yes, while in KXJOINRONALDO/KXJOINDAVID still being under contract on the end date resolves a separate 'no change' outcome 'if it exists'), a manager leaving by effective date (KXPOCHETTINOOUT: resolves on the effective date of departure, not announcement), a host country being announced (KXCOPAAMERICAHOST: every announced co-host resolves Yes), including the two host-announcement series KXWCHOST (sampled text: 'If USA is announced as a host for the 2038 Men's FIFA World Cup and confirmed by any of the Source Agencies') and KXCLUBWCHOST (same wording for the 2029 Men's FIFA Club World Cup): once an official host is announced by a Source Agency every market for a named host country resolves Yes and all others No, and if several hosts are announced each named host resolves Yes, or a governing-body sanction stripping a count of titles (KXMANCITYTITLES: 'at least 8', as officially announced before 1 Jan 2028). Further verified families: next permanent manager (KXNEXTMANAGERMANU: interim or caretaker managers do not count unless later appointed permanently), office-holder exit (KXFIFALEAVE: temporary leave or suspension is not leaving; death resolves at the last fair price), team participation (KXWCIRAN 'competes in', KXWCCONGO 'competes in the Intercontinental Playoffs', No if disqualified), tournament format (KXWCTEAMS: a 64-team field confirmed by Source Agencies), match relocation (KXFIFAUSPULLGAME, whose sampled primary text still carries an unfilled '||date||' placeholder; the title says before Jun 11, 2026), and signings that stay Yes even if later voided (KXJOINMESSI).

rules_evidence.quote: This includes permanent transfers out (the player is sold or transferred to another club, whether for a fee or as a free transfer), loans out
rules_evidence.establishes: Loans of any duration count as leaving, so a loan-and-return still resolves YES; the event is broader than a permanent sale and the hazard of a loan must be included.

rules_evidence.quote: If Erling Haaland signs with a club and is immediately loaned out, the signing club resolves to Yes and all others resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: In the next-club set a 'sign-and-loan' credits the signing club, not the loan club, which affects multi-outcome probabilities for intermediaries.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple host countries are announced to host the 2028 Copa America
rules_evidence.establishes: Multiple co-hosts resolve Yes for each named; the host-country events are therefore not mutually exclusive and probabilities across countries can sum above one.

rules_evidence.quote: This market resolves solely based on the effective date of Mauricio Pochettino's departure from Manager of the US Men's National Team.
rules_evidence.establishes: Announcement or resignation timing is irrelevant; only the effective date counts, which can lag the announcement (notice periods) and matters near the deadline.

rules_evidence.quote: as officially announced before January 1, 2028
rules_evidence.establishes: Stripping of titles needs an official announcement by the deadline, so the timeline of a legal process (hearings, appeals) is the binding factor, not the merits alone.

rules_evidence.quote: If no award is given by the date the market will resolve No.
rules_evidence.establishes: The Super Ballon d'Or series settles on whether the organiser holds the award at all by the deadline, an event-occurrence hazard, not a candidate vote.

rules_evidence.quote: Interim, caretaker, or temporary managers do not satisfy the Payout Criterion unless they are subsequently appointed to the permanent position.
rules_evidence.establishes: Next-manager markets need a permanent appointment, so the interim period lengthens the time to resolution and the caretaker himself only counts if made permanent.

rules_evidence.quote: Temporary leaves of absence, suspensions, or recusals do not constitute leaving
rules_evidence.establishes: Office-holder exit markets count only a definitive departure; an ethics suspension of the FIFA president would not settle YES.

rules_evidence.quote: any subsequent nullification or reversal of that signing (e.g. voiding of the contract due to failed medical, withdrawn agreement, etc.) will not reverse the outcome
rules_evidence.establishes: A signing announcement is final for settlement, so the official announcement, not completion of registration, is the event.

variants_and_edge_cases: Sign-and-loan, contract-expiry release and loans of any duration are explicitly handled in the sampled transfer texts (KXJOINCLUB: 'signing club resolves to Yes'; KXLAMINEYAMAL: 'loans out ... for any duration', contract release incl. expiration); a free-agent signing counts like a fee, and a player still at his club on the end date resolves a separate 'no change' outcome (KXJOINRONALDO). Transfers within the same ownership group are not addressed in any sampled text and are CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

Governance events (host announcement, sanctions, bans) depend on committee calendars and appeal processes with fat-tailed timing; the stated window can end before a decision, which resolves No by default.

Manager markets resolve on effective dates (KXMANAGERSOUT, KXPOCHETTINOOUT, KXMANAGEROUTDATE with an 11:59:59 pm ET cutoff); next-permanent-manager markets exclude interim and caretaker appointments unless made permanent (KXNEXTMANAGERMANU).

36 of 47 series have rules text; TITLE_ONLY: KXNEXTMANAGERJUV, KXNEXTMANAGERMIL, KXMANCITYSANCTION, KXMANCITYBAN, KXMANAGEROUT, KXJOINMBAPPE, KXJOINSALAH, KXSOCCERINTLRETIRE, KXSOCCERLEAVE, KXUEFAISRAELBAN and KXMLSSKILLS; the Source Agencies list for host and format announcements is not shown.

Participation and format series: KXWCIRAN (competes in the 2026 World Cup), KXWCCONGO (competes in the Intercontinental Playoffs; No on FIFA disqualification), KXWCTEAMS (64-team 2030 field confirmed), KXFIFAUSPULL/KXFIFAUSPULLGAME (US involvement suspended / at least one match relocated); KXSUPERBALLONDOR settles on whether any Super Ballon d'Or is awarded before 2030; KXMLSSKILLS (skills challenge winner) is TITLE_ONLY.

KXMANCITYTITLES reads 'If the English Premier League imposes a sanction stripping at least 8 title(s) across Premier League, FA Cup, or League Cup'; whether a stripping imposed by the FA, EFL, UEFA or CAS rather than the Premier League itself counts is not stated.

KXFIFALEAVE: death in office resolves at the last fair price at the Exchange's discretion; KXSOCCERRETIRE must be retirement from all professional play effective immediately or before the next season; KXJOINMESSI stays Yes if the signing is later voided.

KXWCHOST (2038 World Cup) and KXCLUBWCHOST (2029 Club World Cup) are filed here: the sampled primary texts state no date by which the announcement must occur, the Source Agencies list is not shown, and whether a provisional or conditional selection counts as 'announced and confirmed' is not stated; a multi-nation co-hosting resolves each named host Yes (the 2038 text gives an 'Australia or New Zealand' combined-outcome example, whose handling when only one is announced is not stated).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official club, federation or governing-body announcement (club websites, FIFA/UEFA/CONMEBOL communications), with credible news agencies as source agencies where named; effective dates as stated in the announcement.

mechanism.summary: An off-field soccer contract is a rare-event hazard resolved by an official announcement inside a window. The prior comes from a reference class (club state, player or manager profile, body and process type); the actor's fundamentals (contract end and release clause, results versus expectation, legal stage) tilt the hazard; the calendar (window deadlines, committee dates, effective dates) decides whether the event can occur before the contract's end; and information arrives as tiered reports whose reliability sets how far probability should jump. Multi-outcome sets (next club, co-hosts) need 'no change' and non-exclusive handling, and loans, sign-and-loan and effective-date wording must be read per series. Scope: transfers, managers, office-holders, governance, participation and host/format announcements; the only sporting-skill series is the MLS skills challenge (stage s7).

stages.name: Reference-class base rate in the window
stages.description: Each event type has a base rate that depends on its reference class: a top-club star leaving in a given calendar year, a manager at a given league position being dismissed within a season, a host selection by a given body; the window length, the starting state of the actor (tenure, contract, league position) and the structural calendar anchor the prior before any news.
stages.distribution: Rare-event hazard with prior from event counts per class; a few percent per month for a star player's departure, much higher for a bottom-table manager.

stages.name: Actor fundamentals and incentives
stages.description: A transfer requires a willing player, a willing seller and a buyer that can afford the fee and wages: contract expiry date, release clause, club finances, squad needs and the player's stated intentions determine feasibility; managers face board tolerance linked to results, owners and succession options; sanctions depend on evidence and legal process.
stages.distribution: Discrete-time hazard conditional on contract and club state; strongly nonlinear in months to contract end.

stages.name: Calendar and timing structure
stages.description: Transfers cluster at window deadlines (a large share of window deals complete in the final days; the exact share is unsourced here), managerial dismissals follow poor-result runs and international breaks, and governance decisions follow committee dates and appeal periods. A contract whose window ends before a calendar decision date will resolve No whatever the merits.
stages.distribution: Event times clustered at deadlines; heavy-tailed delay distributions for regulatory processes.

stages.name: Information flow and credibility
stages.description: News arrives in tiers: club/federation statements, established journalists' 'here we go' confirmations, rumours from aggregators; the likelihood ratio of each tier and the lag from leak to official confirmation determine how fast a probability should move, and a false report is common at lower tiers.
stages.distribution: Jump process in log odds with reliability-dependent jump sizes; confirmation lag of hours to weeks.

stages.name: Governance and legal process
stages.description: Host selections and sanction decisions are decided by named bodies with procedural stages (bid evaluation, hearings, ruling, appeal) and politics; the events are lumpy, with long periods of nothing and sudden announcements; the stripping of a specific count of titles is a multi-valued legal outcome. Team-participation and format series (Iran competing, DR Congo in the playoffs, a 64-team 2030 field, relocation of US matches) are the same kind of governance outcome: a body's decision, a withdrawal or a disqualification inside the window.
stages.distribution: Staged process with random stage durations and lumpy outcomes; multi-valued legal outcome (0, 1, 2, ... titles).

stages.name: Settlement mapping and multi-outcome bookkeeping
stages.description: Settlement uses effective dates and official announcements; the 'next club' and host sets must include 'no change' and multiple co-host cases; loans count in some contracts and not in others, so label construction requires reading each series' wording.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from announcement records; ambiguity is in definitions.

stages.name: All-Star skills challenge winner (KXMLSSKILLS)
stages.description: The MLS All-Star Skills Challenge is a short exhibition of shooting, passing and crossing drills scored per round; the winner is determined by drill scores among a handful of selected players or teams, not by match play. Outcomes depend on the event format, which players are entered, and specific technical skills (long passing accuracy, shooting under time), with high noise from few attempts per drill.
stages.distribution: Multinomial over a small field with near-uniform priors adjusted by drill-specific skill; few attempts make outcomes highly random.

talent_strength.note: Club and player profile determine how likely a move is; no on-pitch strength but a reference-class prior.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent or matchup in an off-field event; a suitor club's fit with a player is covered by the transfer feasibility inputs, so a separate matchup variable would have no distinct meaning.

role_personnel.note: Roles of player, manager and board; contract status.

availability_news.note: News vintage and source credibility determine updates.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager tenure, performance and board patience.

environment.note: Weather, venue and pitch have no bearing on a transfer, appointment or governance decision; the only environment is the institutional context handled under the calendar and governance inputs.

game_context_script.note: Timing structure of windows and procedures.

pace_volume.note: There is no volume or opportunity count in an announcement event; the analogue (number of news items) is information flow, covered by the announcement-signals input, so a pace input is meaningless.

efficiency_conversion.note: No conversion rate or efficiency process exists for a one-off announcement; the nearest analogue, the conversion of leaks to confirmations, is part of the source-credibility measurement rather than a separate efficiency input.

distribution_variance.note: Rare-event distribution and jump-process news updates.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Window deadlines, results runs and international breaks.

officiating_rules.note: Rules and procedures of governing bodies; sanctions framework.

settlement_contract.note: Effective date vs announcement, loan handling, co-hosts and deadlines.

soc.contract_expiry_release_state.label: Contract expiry, release clause and renewal-talk state
soc.contract_expiry_release_state.mechanism: Months to contract end, release clause and wage structure, and reported renewal status.
soc.contract_expiry_release_state.rationale: A transfer or release hazard is steeply nonlinear in months to contract end: under 12 months the selling club sells or the player leaves free; above 36 months only a release clause or a rebellion moves the player.
soc.contract_expiry_release_state.measurement: For each player: months_to_expiry at as-of; indicator and amount of a release clause (if public) relative to market value; wage as % of club wage bill; renewal status {talks, agreed, stalled}; build hazard model h(months, status) fitted to 15 years of top-league transfers (discrete-time logit) with club-type effects; shrink to league rates with k=20 cases.
soc.contract_expiry_release_state.why: Directly drives KXLAMINEYAMAL-style leave-club contracts and next-club sets.

soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.label: Window calendar and deadline-clustering hazard
soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.mechanism: Timing of open and closed windows and the daily hazard within them.
soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.rationale: Contracts ending before the window opens (e.g. 'before Jan 1, 2027' with a winter window opening only on 1 January) give a different probability than the same question in summer; deals cluster in the last days of a window.
soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.measurement: Build calendar of windows by league and country (summer, winter, extended Saudi/Turkish windows); estimate daily hazard share = fraction of deals by days-to-deadline from 10 years of data; probability a deal occurs before date D = integral of window-open days times hazard; adjust for emergency loans and free-agent signings outside windows.
soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.why: Prevents time-window errors that dominate short-dated transfer contracts.

soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.label: Manager dismissal and appointment hazard
soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.mechanism: Hazard of leaving a role given results, expectations and board context.
soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.rationale: Managers are dismissed after results fall below expectation, with a spike after 4-6 game winless runs, and the 'next manager' contracts depend on the shortlist; national-team coaches depend on tournament cycle.
soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.measurement: Cox model: hazard of leaving per matchweek on points-per-game minus expected points-per-game from ratings, league position relative to preseason rank, run of winless games, tenure, owner change; fit to 20 seasons of top-5 league managerial changes; shrink team-specific frailty with k=3 seasons; for national teams use cycle stage and tournament result.
raw_data: manager appointments and exits with dates
soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.why: Needed for KXPOCHETTINOOUT and Next Manager series with no existing input.

soc.governance_procedure_stage.label: Stage and expected timeline of governance procedures
soc.governance_procedure_stage.mechanism: Procedural stage of a sanction or bid process with historical stage durations.
soc.governance_procedure_stage.rationale: A sanction or host decision resolves only after a sequence of steps; the stated deadline can lapse during a hearing, so timeline and stage durations determine the probability more than the merits.
soc.governance_procedure_stage.measurement: Record procedure stage (allegation, hearing scheduled, hearing concluded, ruling, appeal) with dates; fit stage-duration distributions (log-normal) from comparable cases (financial fair play, UEFA sanctions, FIFA bids) and compute P(final decision before deadline) and the distribution of outcomes (e.g. number of titles stripped) by case type; as-of date stamped.
soc.governance_procedure_stage.why: Provides the timing probability that dominates Man City-type and host-selection contracts.

soc.destination_club_feasibility.label: Buyer-side destination feasibility for next-club and join-league markets
soc.destination_club_feasibility.mechanism: For each candidate destination club or league, whether it can afford the fee and wages, needs the position, offers the sporting project and is a stated or reported preference of the player; normalised across candidates and the no-change outcome.
soc.destination_club_feasibility.rationale: KXJOINCLUB, KXJOINRONALDO, KXJOINSALAH, KXJOINMBAPPE, KXJOINSANE, KXJOINDAVID, KXMLSJOIN and KXJOINLEAGUE are multi-outcome which-club sets; seller-side hazard (contract expiry, window) says when a player moves but not where, and the where is decided by the buyer's financial room, positional need and the player's preference, none of which the seller-side inputs measure.
soc.destination_club_feasibility.measurement: Per candidate club c: wage_room = max(0, 0.70*latest revenue - wage bill - player wage - fee/contract_years) in EUR (0.70 = UEFA squad-cost ratio; league cap headroom for MLS/Saudi); need = 1 if club's best player at the position has rating below the player's by >0.5 SD of the club's squad rating, else 0; pref = 1 if a tier-1 outlet reported the club's interest in the previous 30 days (timestamped). Fit a multinomial logit of historical destinations of comparable players (top-5-league, age band, 15 seasons) on (wage_room/wage, need, pref, same-league flag) with ridge penalty set by CV; softmax over candidates plus a no-move outcome weighted by the seller-side hazard. As-of report timestamp.
free_sources: Transfermarkt squad values and rumour tables (free_scrape)
raw_data: transfer reports by source tier with timestamps
soc.destination_club_feasibility.why: Supplies the destination model that the seller-side inputs lack for the which-club series and ensures the outcome set is normalised including no change.

soc.skills_challenge_format_and_field.label: Skills-challenge format and entrant drill skill
soc.skills_challenge_format_and_field.mechanism: The skills-challenge winner is set by drill scores under the event's format among the announced entrants.
soc.skills_challenge_format_and_field.rationale: KXMLSSKILLS is a novelty exhibition whose outcome is driven by the format (which drills, team vs individual) and entrants; match statistics only weakly proxy drill skill (e.g. long-pass completion for passing drills), and the event is TITLE_ONLY so even the outcome set is unconfirmed.
soc.skills_challenge_format_and_field.measurement: From the event announcement: list of entrants and drills; per entrant a drill-skill score = z-scored season long-pass completion, shot accuracy and cross accuracy (last 2 MLS seasons, shrunk to league mean with k=200 attempts), mapped to win probability by softmax with temperature fitted to past skills-challenge results (2019 onward); fixed as of the announcement time.
soc.skills_challenge_format_and_field.why: Only input for the MLS skills-challenge winner series.

soc.official_announcement_signals.reason: Source-tier likelihood ratios and the leak-to-confirmation lag are the right updating mechanism for off-field events.

soc.transfers.reason: Net squad changes and manager flags give context, but the contract-level hazard inputs are more specific.

soc.points_deductions.reason: Relevant only as a context variable for league points-deduction sanctions; it does not measure titles-stripped outcomes (KXMANCITYTITLES), where the procedural-stage input is binding.

soc.tiebreaker_rules.reason: Tiebreak rules of competitions have no bearing on transfers, appointments or host selection.

m.rules_text.reason: Loan handling, effective date and co-host rules are decisive wording but not predictors.

m.quote_history.reason: Market price history is market-derived and is a benchmark, not an input to the mechanism.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trades reflect the market's view of news; useful for event studies, not as an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest describe market attention, not the probability of the event.

m.lifecycle.reason: Market open/close times matter for deadline handling and effective dates.

soc.press_conference_news.reason: Managers' statements on player futures are informative but noisy; needs credibility classification.

soc.offfield_base_rate.reason: Reference-class base rates are the prior for all rare off-field events; needs club-state conditioning.

interactions.mechanism: Inside the last 12 months of a contract and with a window open before the deadline, the hazard jumps; with no window before the contract's date, the probability of a transfer is only from emergency/free-agent routes, so the window availability gates the contract-state effect.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the hazard model with an interaction between months to expiry and a window-open indicator.

interactions.mechanism: Without credible news the prior drifts slowly; after a top-tier confirmation the probability jumps near certainty irrespective of the base rate, so the information regime replaces the base-rate regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Event study of resolved outcomes after each source tier's reports.

interactions.mechanism: A dismissal changes the transfer outlook for the club's stars (new manager's priorities) and vice versa; manager exits often precede window activity, so one hazard is conditional on the other state. (speculative cross-lag, not supported by the sampled contract texts; treat as a hypothesis for event-study testing)
interactions.how_to_test: Cross-lagged analysis of manager change and star departures within 60 days.

interactions.mechanism: The probability of a final decision before the deadline is piecewise in stage: near zero before hearing, rises after ruling, and appeal windows add a second step; the number of titles stripped depends on appeal outcomes. Note that soc.points_deductions measures league points deductions only; a titles-stripped legal outcome (KXMANCITYTITLES) is a different procedural result and is driven by soc.governance_procedure_stage, not by this input.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute conditional probabilities per stage from past cases.

interactions.mechanism: A star with a short contract at a club that has just lost its manager and sold others has a hazard far above the product of separate effects, because the club's bargaining position and the player's incentive both shift.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress departure on interactions of contract months and club transition indicators.

nonlinearities.shape: Steeply convex in months to expiry below 12
nonlinearities.why: Hazard of leaving rises sharply as expiry approaches because the club must sell or lose the player for free, so the function is not linear in months.

nonlinearities.shape: Heavy right tail in time-to-event
nonlinearities.why: Governance and transfer timings have fat tails; the survival function is not exponential and a constant hazard overstates short-window probabilities.

nonlinearities.shape: Spike in daily hazard at the deadline
nonlinearities.why: Daily hazard is highly non-uniform: a disproportionate share of window deals complete in the final days, so cumulative probability by date is convex until the deadline.
