contract.settlement_definition: Eleven live series, all with rules text. Team Points (EPL, La Liga, Serie A, Ligue 1, Bundesliga): YES when the club 'reaches at least N points' (floor N-0.5), resolved on the points awarded in the official season standings, so deductions count. Champion Winning Margin (same five leagues): YES when the champion finishes 15 or more points (greater_or_equal) above second in the final official table; level points give margin 0 regardless of tiebreaker, and in Serie A a title play-off after level points also gives 0. KXWCGSUNDEFEATED, despite its 'Undefeated' title, settles YES only if the named team 'wins 3 matches in the group stage' of the 2026 World Cup (a draw fails it). No postponement or abandonment clause appears in any text.

rules_evidence.quote: If Tottenham reaches at least 75 points in the 2026-27 EPL season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Team Points is an N+ threshold on the final season points total, a sum of 3W+D over the remaining league fixtures plus points already banked.

rules_evidence.quote: This market resolves based on the points awarded to Stuttgart in the 2026-27 Bundesliga season standings.
rules_evidence.establishes: Settlement reads the points in the official standings, so administrative deductions or awarded results change the total; a 34-match league has fewer remaining fixtures than a 38-match league.

rules_evidence.quote: If the top two teams are level on points, the winning margin is 0, regardless of the tiebreaker used to determine the champion.
rules_evidence.establishes: The margin series is the points gap between first and second, an order statistic of the two highest totals; ties give 0 whoever wins the title.

rules_evidence.quote: If the top two teams are level on points, and a single-match playoff is used to determine the winner, the margin is 0.
rules_evidence.establishes: Serie A's wording ties the zero margin to a title play-off, a league-specific variant of the level-points rule.

rules_evidence.quote: If Uzbekistan wins 3 matches in the group stage of the 2026 Men's FIFA World Cup
rules_evidence.establishes: The 'Group Stage Undefeated' series actually requires three group wins, so a draw resolves No; the object is the product of three match win probabilities, not avoiding defeat.

variants_and_edge_cases: Team Points thresholds are N+ on banked points plus 3W+D over the remaining 24-28 league fixtures (as of November 2026; 34-match Bundesliga), read from the official standings so an administrative deduction shifts the whole distribution.

Margin series use one strike of 15+ points per league: the event needs a dominant champion and a weak runner-up, so it is a right-tail event of the first-minus-second order statistic; Serie A's zero-margin rule refers to a play-off after level points.
KXWCGSUNDEFEATED title says 'Undefeated' but the rules text requires 3 wins; the third group game may be a dead rubber for a team already through, lowering its win probability through rotation.
No text covers postponed matches that are never played or voided seasons; Team Points relies on the standings 'points awarded', which would include awarded (forfeit) results.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final season standings of the named league (points awarded after deductions) for Team Points and Winning Margin; official FIFA group-stage results for KXWCGSUNDEFEATED.

mechanism.summary: Three contract types share this key. Team Points thresholds are the final season points total of one club: banked points plus a sum of remaining 0/1/3 outcomes whose probabilities come from ratings, venue and draw propensity, widened by shared rating uncertainty and shifted by deductions. Champion Winning Margin is the first-minus-second order statistic over all clubs' totals, a right-tail event at the 15-point strike that depends on the leader's dominance and the weakness of the best rival. The World Cup series requires three group wins, a product of match win probabilities with a third-game incentive effect. Rotation and injuries create regime shifts, and settlement reads official standings with explicit zero-margin and deduction rules.

stages.name: Per-match win and draw probabilities
stages.description: Every series is built from match-level outcome probabilities: each remaining league fixture (and each of the three World Cup group games) gets P(win), P(draw) and P(loss) from opponent-adjusted strengths and venue. Points thresholds weight a draw as one point, the three-group-wins series counts only wins, and the margin series needs these probabilities for every contender, so the draw split matters differently in each variant.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per match with p between 0.25 (away at a top side) and 0.85 (home against a weak side); sequence-dependent through shared strength uncertainty.

stages.name: Remaining schedule and its order
stages.description: The remaining league schedule fixes how many points are still available and against whom: a mid-table club with a soft run-in has a higher points ceiling than one facing the top six, and the champion-margin series depends on both the leader's and the runner-up's remaining schedules, including their direct meeting. For World Cup group series the three fixtures and their order (opening game vs dead rubber) are known at listing.
stages.distribution: Deterministic fixture list; random only through postponements and cup-induced rescheduling.

stages.name: First-minus-second order statistic for the champion margin
stages.description: For the Winning Margin series the outcome is the gap between the highest and second-highest final totals among all clubs, not the gap between two named clubs: a 15+ margin requires the champion's total to be high and the best rival's to be low at the same time. The relevant inputs are the joint distribution of the top few totals, their correlation through direct meetings and common opponents, and current banked points; a single dominant club makes the margin right-skewed.
stages.distribution: Order statistic of correlated points totals; margin sd about 6-8 points over a full season with strong right skew when one club is dominant; P(margin>=15) is a tail probability.

stages.name: Rotation, injuries and fatigue across the stretch
stages.description: Congestion from European and cup fixtures causes league rotation and lowers expected points per match, and a long injury to a key player lowers the whole remaining points path; for World Cup groups a team already qualified after two wins may rotate in the third game. These regimes move the season totals of contenders unevenly, which matters for both thresholds and the margin.
stages.distribution: Regime shifts in p_t by rotation and injury states; effect size 0.03-0.10 per-match p.

stages.name: Settlement and contract scope
stages.description: Points thresholds read the official standings (points awarded, deductions included); the margin series reads the final table with level points giving 0 (Serie A: 0 after a title play-off); the World Cup series counts three group-stage wins only. Abandoned or voided matches change totals through awarded results, which no text addresses explicitly.
stages.distribution: Deterministic from official records; ambiguity in scope definitions.

stages.name: Season points total for the Team Points thresholds
stages.description: For the Team Points series the final total is points already banked plus 3 per win and 1 per draw over the remaining league fixtures; each fixture's win and draw probabilities come from opponent-adjusted ratings, venue and draw propensity, and the sum is wider than a binomial because rating uncertainty is shared across all remaining fixtures. Points in the official standings also absorb any administrative deduction, which shifts the whole distribution. In-season managerial change is drawn inside the points simulation from soc.manager_dismissal_hazard and, when it occurs, the remaining matches use the soc.transfers re-blended rating, which widens the points distribution of under-performing clubs and, for contenders, the champion margin; the shift size is set to zero until the event study.
stages.distribution: Sum of about 24-28 categorical outcomes (0/1/3) with shared rating error; sd of the remaining-points total roughly 6-8 for a mid-table club; a deduction is a discrete left shift.

stages.name: Three group wins in a World Cup group (KXWCGSUNDEFEATED)
stages.description: The World Cup group series pays only if the team wins all three group games, so P(YES) is roughly the product of three match win probabilities, adjusted for dependence through shared rating error and for the third-game incentive: a team that has already won twice is usually through and may rotate, while one needing a win plays at full strength. Draw-prone low-scoring tournament football makes this a low-probability event for all but the strongest sides against weak groups.
stages.distribution: Product of three dependent Bernoullis; P(3 wins) from about 0.02 for weak teams to about 0.35-0.45 for a heavy favourite in a weak group.

talent_strength.note: Team strength and posterior width determine every p_t and their correlation.

opponent_matchup.note: Remaining opponents per club and direct meetings between the top two.

availability_news.note: Availability news for the matches in the next weeks; vintage matters less over a multi-month window.

coaching_scheme.note: In-season dismissal hazard and the post-change re-blended rating inside the points simulation; shift size empirical.

environment.note: Venue and weather act through each match's win/draw probabilities (home advantage is in the match model); season totals and the margin add no separate environmental mechanism.

game_context_script.note: Banked points and gaps at the as-of date, and World Cup group state before the third game.

pace_volume.note: Volume statistics matter only through team ratings; points totals, margins and group wins are functions of match outcomes, not of possession or shot counts.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing and saving luck in banked results is regressed through xG-based ratings, so the remaining-fixture probabilities are not inflated by an over-performing start.

distribution_variance.note: Order-statistic tail of the margin and the width of the season points distribution.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Predicted rotation and cumulative minutes load across the December and spring fixture pile (soc.rotation_index, soc.congestion_load, both catalog inputs) plus the schedule list; soc.motivation (audited WEAK) is no longer cited.

officiating_rules.note: Officiating tendencies affect single matches (penalties, cards) and average out over a season or a three-game group; no systematic officiating mechanism changes points totals or margins.

settlement_contract.note: Standings points with deductions, zero-margin rule, three-wins definition.

soc.latent_form_persistence.label: Latent form persistence (serial correlation of match residuals)
soc.latent_form_persistence.mechanism: Autocorrelation of match outcome residuals beyond ratings and strength drift.
soc.latent_form_persistence.rationale: If outcomes carry positive serial correlation after controlling for strength, runs are more likely than the independent calculation; if it is zero, ratings with drift suffice. Estimating it matters because the streak is a run statistic.
soc.latent_form_persistence.measurement: Residual e_t = (points won - expected points) where expected points come from pre-match club Elo (clubelo.com, value as of the day before kickoff) with home advantage; for each club-season, regress e_t on e_(t-1) controlling for expected points; estimate pooled AR(1) coefficient phi by mixed model with club random intercepts over top-5 leagues for 10 seasons, report cluster-bootstrap interval. Elo is already a form tracker, so phi is residual persistence only. Use phi in the copula only if its 95% interval excludes 0. As-of prior matches only.
raw_data: match results for top leagues over 10 seasons
soc.latent_form_persistence.why: Positive serial correlation of match residuals beyond rating drift would widen the season points distribution and fatten the 15+ margin tail; if it is zero, ratings with drift suffice.

soc.points_total_distribution.reason: Five of the six live series are Team Points thresholds on the final season total, so the season points distribution (banked points plus simulated W/D/L over remaining fixtures) is the core engine.

soc.remaining_schedule_strength.reason: Remaining opponents and venues set the points still available for each club and for the leader and runner-up in the margin series.

soc.ratings_uncertainty.reason: Shared strength uncertainty widens the season points distribution and correlates the remaining fixtures, which matters for both thresholds and the margin tail.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.reason: Per-match win probabilities require opponent-adjusted strengths.

soc.draw_propensity.reason: Draw tendency lowers P(win) only through the rating model (win/draw/loss split from soc.xg_adjusted_ratings); it is not independent evidence beyond the ratings, so it is context.

soc.points_deductions.reason: Team Points read 'points awarded' in the standings and the margin reads the final table, so a deduction moves both settlement quantities directly.

soc.injuries.reason: Long-term injuries to key players lower match probabilities across many remaining fixtures; for the World Cup three-wins series the squad news before each group game matters.

soc.paired_team_correlation.reason: The champion-margin series depends on the joint distribution of the top two totals, whose correlation via direct meetings sets the margin variance.

m.rules_text.reason: Fixes the settlement objects (standings points awarded, level-points margin 0, three group wins); not a predictor.

soc.abandonment_risk.reason: An abandoned or never-replayed match feeds the standings as an awarded result or not at all, changing season points and the margin; no text addresses it.

soc.fixture_sequence_win_vector.reason: Run-length (P(run>=5)) dynamic programme over an ordered win vector built for the win-streak series, which moved to unreg:team_win_streak; season points and the champion margin are order-free sums of W/D/L, already produced by soc.points_total_distribution with soc.remaining_schedule_strength.

soc.competition_scope_and_win_definition.reason: Scope flags (friendlies, shootout wins, competitions counted) were written for the moved streak series; every remaining text here counts league standings points or three group-stage wins, so there is no competition-scope choice to parse.

interactions.mechanism: A pending deduction on the leader or the runner-up shifts the first-minus-second gap by the deduction size, so a margin near 15 can cross the strike in either direction without any match being played; the effect is zero for clubs outside the top two.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate margins with and without announced deductions and compare against realised margins in seasons with sanctions.

interactions.mechanism: The margin depends on whether the leader and runner-up still have to meet: a remaining direct meeting is a six-point swing that raises margin variance, while once both meetings are played the two totals evolve more independently through different schedules.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare margin distribution width in simulations before and after the last direct meeting.

interactions.mechanism: Points thresholds far above a club's expected total are convex in rating uncertainty: wider posterior strength fattens the upper tail, so 75+ for a club expected at 65 rises sharply with uncertainty while near-median thresholds barely move.
interactions.how_to_test: Calibrate threshold probabilities by distance from expected total with and without posterior-draw simulation.

interactions.mechanism: For three group wins the third game switches regime: a team already qualified after two wins may rotate, lowering its win probability, while a team needing a win plays full strength; this conditional dependence lowers P(3 wins) below the naive product.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare third-game win rates of World Cup and Euro teams already qualified vs not, controlling for rating gap.

interactions.mechanism: A key injury during a congested stretch lowers expected points over many fixtures at once; below a squad-depth threshold the loss compounds with rotation, shifting the season total and, for contenders, the margin.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress points-per-game residuals on key-player absence interacted with congestion.

interactions.mechanism: A club below its expected points has a raised dismissal hazard; a dismissal switches the rating regime for all remaining matches, so the season-points distribution is a mixture that is wider and left-skewed for struggling clubs, and a contender's change moves both its points threshold and the first-minus-second margin.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare season-points calibration (PIT histograms) for clubs that changed manager in-season, with and without the simulated dismissal branch.

nonlinearities.shape: Right-skewed survival function in the strike
nonlinearities.why: P(margin>=m) decays slowly for a dominant champion and fast otherwise, so a single 15-point strike sits on very different parts of the curve by league and season.

nonlinearities.shape: Sigmoid in threshold minus expected total
nonlinearities.why: Threshold probabilities follow a CDF of an approximately normal total with sd 6-8 points, so they are near 0/1 beyond about two sd and steep near the mean.

contract.settlement_definition: Match totals: YES when 'over N goals are scored' in the named match 'after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)', N a half-goal strike so there is no push; the strikes form a nested monotone ladder. Team totals ('records above N goals', same window) count one side and state that own goals count towards the team awarded the goal. The World Cup series KXWCTOTAL and KXWCTEAMTOTAL use exactly this per-match wording (e.g. a France vs England game), so no tournament-aggregate series remains here. No totals text contains a cancellation, postponement or abandonment clause (the game-total secondary text is only the trademark disclaimer).

rules_evidence.quote: If over 5.5 goals are scored in the Algeria vs Togo professional AFCON Qualifiers soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: The 5.5 strike on a mismatched qualifier shows tail strikes are listed; the probability of 6+ goals is not given by the text and must be estimated, so tail calibration matters.

rules_evidence.quote: If over 5.5 goals are scored in the Besiktas vs Genclerbirligi professional Super Lig soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: Same wording across leagues; the 5.5 line on a league match with a strong home side is a mismatch tail contract.

rules_evidence.quote: after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)
rules_evidence.establishes: Extra time goals are excluded; in cup totals a 2-2 after 90 that finishes 4-3 in ET is still 4 goals, and ET must not be included in training labels.

rules_evidence.quote: If over 7.5 goals are scored in the Kabilio Jaffa vs Ironi Modiin professional State Cup soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: The ladder extends to 7.5 in a cup tie between mismatched Israeli clubs, i.e. the tail of the count distribution beyond seven goals is a live contract.

rules_evidence.quote: Own goals count towards the team awarded the goal.
rules_evidence.establishes: Team-total settlement credits own goals to the beneficiary, so the opponent defence error rate feeds a team total.

rules_evidence.quote: over 7.5 goals are scored in the Nottingham Forest vs Manchester City professional EPL soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: KXEPLTOTAL is a single-match total, not a league-season aggregate, so it belongs with the per-match inputs here.

rules_evidence.quote: If over 11.5 goals are scored in the France vs England professional FIFA World Cup soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: The World Cup total is a single-match total with the same regulation-only window, not a tournament aggregate; the 11.5 rung shows the sample captures the top listed rung.

rules_evidence.quote: If England records above 7.5 goals in the France vs England professional FIFA World Cup soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: World Cup team total is a per-match single-team count; it belongs with the per-match inputs here.

variants_and_edge_cases: Strike ladder: each rung is P(total >= k+1), monotone decreasing. The sampled strikes are the top listed rungs (3.5 to 11.5, mostly 5.5-7.5, e.g. 11.5 for KXWCTOTAL, KXUCLTOTAL, 10.5 for KXEFLCHAMPIONSHIPTOTAL), consistent with the sampler picking the highest strike of each event; the central rungs (1.5-3.5), where the mean and low-score structure dominate, are not visible in the text but almost certainly listed.
Team-total series (KXUECLTEAMTOTAL, KXEPLTEAMTOTAL-style) require a single side's count; an own goal credited to the side counts, so the opponent's attack feeds a team's count at about 3-5% of goals.

Totals for halves (1H/2H) are in first_half_and_period, and the same 'Point Total' ledger title is used for goals totals; league and cup versions differ in incentives (aggregate scores, ET) while settlement is regulation-only.

198 live series, 155 with rules text, all with the regulation-only wording; 43 are TITLE_ONLY (mostly cup and team-total series, plus the generic KXSOCCERTOTAL); abandonment mid-match with goals already scored and postponement are not addressed.

Scope: all live series are per-match totals or team totals, including KXEPLTOTAL, KXUCLTOTAL, KXWCTOTAL and KXWCTEAMTOTAL (verified per-match wording); the Team Points series moved to team_points_and_margin and KXWCTOTALGOAL/KXWCTEAMGOALS to unreg:tournament_aggregate_event_props.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official match report final regulation score (home plus away goals) from the competition's governing body; team totals credit own goals to the team awarded the goal, as their texts state; extra time and penalties excluded.

mechanism.summary: Total goals is the sum of two correlated overdispersed counts settled at 90 minutes plus stoppage. The mean comes from opponent-adjusted attack and defence strengths and the league's goal environment; the lineup's attack and defence composition moves the two sides in opposite directions, so it needs a split rather than a scalar. A shared latent openness factor correlates the team counts and thickens both tails; game-state damping and mismatch collapses shape the right tail, which is what the high rungs (5.5 to 7.5 in the sampled series) price. Finishing and keeper luck, set-piece and penalty events, weather and referee tendencies add noise, and the ladder is a nested monotone set with regulation-only settlement.

stages.name: Two scoring intensities and their sum
stages.description: The total's mean is the sum of both teams' opponent-adjusted lambdas; the lineup's attack/defence composition (which attackers and which defenders play) determines each side's contribution separately, and the sum rewards openness on both sides. League goal environment, home goal share and season trend set the baseline, with strong cross-league differences (2.3 to 3.3 goals per match). Stakes and rotation shift both lambdas: the direction of soc.rotation_index on the total is an unverified hypothesis with no source on disk (a rotating side's attack and defence may both weaken, so the net sign is not established and is to be estimated from lineup-change data), and soc.stakes_leverage flags dead rubbers and six-pointers whose effect on the total has no established sign (more open in dead rubbers, cagier in high-leverage relegation games are both plausible).
stages.distribution: Sum of two overdispersed counts; mean around 2.7 with variance excess over Poisson to be estimated (10-15% is a placeholder).

stages.name: Shared openness and style factor
stages.description: Some matches are open for both sides (high lines, weak defences, derbies without stakes) and some closed (cautious, low blocks); this match-level latent factor correlates the two teams' scoring and thickens both tails of the total beyond independent Poisson, which is why 0-0 and 5-3 are both more common than the independent model predicts.
stages.distribution: Mixture over a latent openness variable; positive correlation between team counts at the match level, negative conditional correlation within game-state.

stages.name: Game-state and tail dynamics
stages.description: Once a lead builds the leader eases off, so tails are shaped by two competing forces: collapse of a weaker team (red card, mismatch) pushes the total upward in bursts, while garbage-time damping caps it; the net is a heavy right tail only in strongly mismatched fixtures and in leagues with poor defending. High strikes depend on the tail, not the mean.
stages.distribution: Heavy right tail from mismatch mixture; P(total>=7) well above Poisson tail in cups with divisional gaps.

stages.name: Finishing, keeper and set-piece luck
stages.description: Realised totals include finishing and goalkeeper variance: a keeper in hot form or a team that has overperformed xG for months is a regression candidate, and set-piece and penalty events add lumpy goals; weather (wind, rain) modifies shot quality and keeper handling modestly.
stages.distribution: Overdispersion from persistent skill plus transient luck; penalty events add about 0.25-0.3 goals per match in expectation with high variance.

stages.name: Ladder and settlement
stages.description: Rungs form a monotone ladder in P(total>k); the contract uses regulation goals including stoppage, and team totals use one side's count; extra time and shootouts are excluded; cross-rung consistency is a constraint, not an input.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping; ladder is an implied distribution.

game_context_script.note: Score-state damping and collapse shape the tail.

pace_volume.note: Shot and possession volume per side.

soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.label: Calibrated tail dispersion of match totals by league and mismatch bucket
soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.mechanism: Excess probability of 5+ and 6+ goal matches relative to independent Poisson, by league and expected-total bucket.
soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.rationale: High strikes (5.5-7.5) are tail contracts: Poisson with league-average mean misses by factors of two, and the tail multiplier depends on mismatch size and league defending quality.
soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.measurement: Pool 10 seasons per league; bin matches by model expected total (deciles) and expected absolute goal difference; compute observed P(total>=k)/model P for k=4,5,6,7; isotonic smoothing; hierarchical shrinkage across leagues with k=150 matches per bin; output tail multiplier function m(league,bucket,k); as-of prior matches only.
raw_data: final scores and pre-match expected totals
soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.why: The sampled strikes of 5.5 to 7.5 make tail multipliers the first-order calibration term.

soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.label: Match-level shared openness factor
soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.mechanism: Latent factor that moves both teams' scoring rates together, estimated from residual correlation.
soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.rationale: Totals are controlled by how open the match is for both sides, which is more than the sum of two independent rates; ignoring it understates both 0-0 and 5-goal frequencies.
soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.measurement: Fit a bivariate model with a shared log-normal factor: log lambda_home = a_h - d_a + gamma*z, log lambda_away = a_a - d_h + gamma*z, z~N(0,1); estimate gamma per league by marginal likelihood over 5 seasons; also the team-pair covariates: both teams' PPDA and line height difference; shrink gamma toward the league value with k=30 matches per team-pair class.
soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.why: Directly models correlation between the team counts that drives the tails of totals.

soc.xi_attack_defence_split.label: Lineup attack and defence value split
soc.xi_attack_defence_split.mechanism: Separate expected-goals deltas for the attacking and defending halves of the confirmed XI.
soc.xi_attack_defence_split.rationale: A scalar lineup-strength delta cannot say whether goals will rise or fall: a missing centre-back raises the total while a missing striker lowers it, and these may cancel in a scalar.
soc.xi_attack_defence_split.measurement: From a ridge regression on team xG for and against per match on minutes-weighted player indicators (separate models for xG_for and xG_against), compute attack_delta = sum over starters of player_attack_value minus season-average XI value, and defence_delta likewise (including the keeper); expected total change = attack_delta_h + attack_delta_a + defence_delta_h + defence_delta_a (signs per convention); evaluate at lineup release.
soc.xi_attack_defence_split.why: Totals respond to the sum of attack and defence changes with different signs for each side.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.reason: Provides both lambdas and the base of the total; opponent adjustment is necessary.

soc.pace_press.reason: Tempo and pressing affect openness, but partly overlaps with team xG ratings.

soc.goal_dist.reason: Count distribution with overdispersion is the object of totals contracts; soc.dixon_coles_low_score is the low-cell correction layer within it, so the two overlap and only goal_dist is primary.

soc.dixon_coles_low_score.reason: Matters for the central and low rungs (1.5-3.5), where draw and low-score structure move the total; irrelevant only for 5.5+ strikes; kept alongside soc.goal_dist rather than demoted on the strength of four sampled tail strikes.

soc.xi_strength_delta.reason: Scalar lineup value mixes attack and defence with opposing effects on totals; the new split is needed.

soc.gk.reason: Goalkeeper effect on totals is small compared with defence quality.

soc.set_pieces.reason: Set-piece goals add a lumpy component, but incremental over xG is small.

soc.weather.reason: Wind/rain effects of a few percent on totals; fits league baseline.

soc.referee.reason: Referee goal effects come through penalties; weak predictor with large noise.

soc.league_baseline_environment.reason: League-season goal rate and home share are the baseline for each rung and drive cross-league differences.

soc.implied_lambda_from_lines.reason: Derived from de-vigged market lines; not an independent input.

m.ladder_structure.reason: The cross-rung monotonicity check is computed on quoted strike prices, so it is market-derived and used only to validate model output across rungs, not as an input to any stage or coverage claim; the nested-event structure itself is taken from m.rules_text.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Realised YES rate by strike is a calibration benchmark of the market, not a mechanism input.

soc.shots.reason: Shots for/against add little over xG for totals and are noisy.

soc.corners.reason: Corner counts are a downstream correlate of attacking pressure with negligible incremental effect on goals.

soc.fouls_cards.reason: Card tendencies matter only via red cards which are rare and unpredictable; small effect on totals.

soc.lineups_pit.reason: Timestamped lineup (keeper and defenders) is the largest pregame update for totals.

soc.score_effects_adjusted_xg.reason: Removes garbage-time distortion from xG ratings; improves rating quality.

interactions.mechanism: A shared latent openness factor multiplies both lambdas, so Var(total) exceeds the sum of lambdas by a term growing with (lambda_H + lambda_A) squared: mismatches with a high summed lambda amplify the tail more than balanced low-lambda games.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit gamma by league and check calibration of P(total>=5) in high-lambda games.

interactions.mechanism: A missing centre-back raises the total only if the opponent has strong attack ratings, and a missing striker lowers it only if the side's chances are concentrated in him; the lineup split effect is conditional on opponent attack quality from the ratings.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress totals on the defence delta times opponent adjusted attack rating.

interactions.mechanism: Tails switch regime with lead size: up to a three-goal gap totals grow, beyond it damping or collapse dominates, so tail multipliers must condition on the expected gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate tail multipliers within bins of expected absolute goal difference.

interactions.mechanism: Heavy rain or wind lowers the effectiveness of high-tempo passing teams more than direct teams, so the weather effect on totals is scaled by the style of the teams playing. (speculative style interaction with no supporting evidence cited; hypothesis only)
interactions.how_to_test: Interact weather indicators with team passing-directness index.

interactions.mechanism: Totals depend on both teams' finishing and both keepers; hot finishing against a hot keeper nets out; the joint distribution of finishing and keeper residuals sets the variance, not each separately.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare totals variance with joint shrinkage of finishing and keeper residuals vs separate.

interactions.mechanism: Only for low-leverage or very high-leverage league fixtures: rotation is likelier in dead rubbers and changes both sides' attack/defence ratings, while leverage itself may open or close the game; the total-goals shift is conditional on the leverage regime and of unknown sign.
interactions.how_to_test: Pooled regression of totals residuals on leverage percentile buckets and realised starters changed, league fixed effects, 5 seasons.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear in league mean but convex in rung probability at 5.5+
nonlinearities.why: A 0.2 shift in league average goals changes P(total>=6) by more than 20% relative because the tail is exponential in the mean.

nonlinearities.shape: Monotone isotonic multiplier increasing with k
nonlinearities.why: Tail multiplier relative to Poisson is not constant across rungs: the multiplier is near 1 at central rungs and larger in the tail, with the size to be estimated (1.5-2.5 at 6.5+ is a placeholder).

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in wind speed (a value near 30 km/h is a placeholder to be fitted)
nonlinearities.why: Weather affects scoring materially only beyond thresholds (strong wind, heavy rain), with near-zero effect otherwise.

contract.settlement_definition: All ten live series are corner counts: combined ('France and England combined record at least 9+ corners') or single-team ('France records at least 8+ corners') N+ thresholds (floor_strike N, greater_or_equal) over the entire game including regulation, stoppage and any extra time. The EPL and La Liga texts count only corner kicks actually taken; the UCL, World Cup and UEFA Super Cup texts do not mention it. World Cup corner series resolve to a fair price if the game is cancelled or rescheduled more than two weeks away; the club texts carry no postponement clause. No card or foul series is listed.

rules_evidence.quote: Only corner kicks that are actually taken will count toward this market. Corner kicks that are awarded but not taken will not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: The count is of taken corners; awarded corners that become goal kicks, are cancelled by VAR or not taken before a whistle do not count, so the data source must report taken rather than awarded.

rules_evidence.quote: combined record at least 9+ corners during the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)
rules_evidence.establishes: Extra-time corners count: in cup ties the exposure is up to 120 minutes, so knockout ties have a mean about 1.5-2.5 corners higher than the 90-minute version, whereas the 'taken' clause is absent from this series' sampled secondary text.

rules_evidence.quote: Barcelona records at least 6+ corners taken during the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)
rules_evidence.establishes: Team-corner thresholds are N+ for a single side, so the favourite's corner count depends on its territory and on whether it trails or leads, not on the match total alone.

rules_evidence.quote: Ipswich Town records at least 5+ corners taken during the entire game
rules_evidence.establishes: Underdog team thresholds (5+) are lower-mean events (about 4 corners) whose probability is driven by game state and set-piece pressure from the opponent's lead.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is cancelled or rescheduled to over two weeks away, the market will resolve to a fair price in accordance with the rules.
rules_evidence.establishes: World Cup corner series have a two-week postponement window, the only corner texts with any postponement clause.

rules_evidence.quote: France records at least 8+ corners during the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)
rules_evidence.establishes: World Cup team corners include extra time, and World Cup knockout games can reach 120 minutes, so exposure varies with the chance of a draw at 90.

variants_and_edge_cases: Threshold construction: 'N+' with floor_strike N (greater_or_equal, e.g. 9+ total, 6+ team), a nested ladder of integer rungs; counts are discrete with mean about 10 total (sd 3-3.5) so adjacent rungs differ by 6-9 percentage points.

Extra time is included in every corner text. World Cup knockout games (KXWCCORNERS, KXWCTCORNERS) and UCL knockout second legs can go to 30 minutes of extra time after a draw, adding corner exposure; the UEFA Super Cup (KXUEFASCCORNERS, KXUEFASCTCORNERS) has, under UEFA regulations since 2023, gone straight to penalties after a 90-minute draw, so the text's extra-time inclusion is normally inert there (to be confirmed against the current regulations).
'Actually taken' language appears in the EPL and La Liga texts but not in the UCL, World Cup or UEFA Super Cup texts, so awarded-but-not-taken corners may be treated differently by series.
Cards and fouls have no live series here (the catalog's cards inputs have no contract to be verified against); referee-dependent card contracts, if listed, would need their own rules.

EPL and La Liga series (four) can never reach extra time; UCL series cover league-phase games (no extra time) and later knockout second legs (extra time possible); World Cup knockout games can reach extra time; the Super Cup normally cannot. Exposure must be conditioned on the game's format and P(draw at 90) where extra time exists.
contract.settlement_data_source: Match data provider's corner-kick events (Opta-style events as used by Kalshi's sports data feed), counting corners taken in the entire game; the exact provider is not stated in the sampled text.

mechanism.summary: A corner-count contract counts corner kicks taken over the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time). Corners are a by-product of attacks that end blocked, deflected or parried: team expected corners scale with attacking volume and the share of attacks ending in blocked shots and crosses, and the opponent's defensive style (low block, clearance direction) multiplies it. Game state redistributes corners between the teams: the trailing side gains late, the leader concedes, so the favourite's team count depends on whether it scores early. Exposure (added time, VAR, extra time) and the 'taken versus awarded' definition adjust the count. Cards and fouls have no live contract in the ledger.

stages.name: Attacking pressure and territory
stages.description: Corners are generated when the attacking team's shots, crosses and passes are blocked or deflected over the byline, so each team's expected corners scale with its volume of attacks in the final third and the share of attacks that end in blocked shots; territorially dominant teams against deep blocks generate the highest counts, while transitional teams generate few.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count (negative binomial) with mean about 5 per team; dispersion from variation in how attacks end.

stages.name: Opponent defending style
stages.description: A low block that blocks shots and crosses concedes many corners, a high line concedes few corners but more shots; the relevant measure is corners conceded per attack (block rate and clearance direction), not shots conceded; defenders' clearing habits and goalkeeper behaviour (tipping over the bar) are part of this.
stages.distribution: Team-level rate multiplier with sd across teams to be estimated (15% is a placeholder); interacts multiplicatively with the attacker's volume.

stages.name: Game state redistributes corners
stages.description: The trailing team pushes forward in the second half and wins more corners, while the leader defends deep and concedes them; late-game state raises the trailer's corners after the 60th minute by an amount to be estimated (30-40% is an unsourced placeholder). So the favourite's team corners are high only if it dominates without scoring early; an early lead lowers the favourite's count.
stages.distribution: Time-inhomogeneous intensity with score-state multipliers; negative association between early goals and the leader's subsequent corners.

stages.name: Match exposure: stoppage, VAR and extra time
stages.description: Exposure minutes (45+ each half, VAR delays, 30 minutes of ET in cups) scale the count; referees' added-time habits differ; a red card changes both teams' corner rates; and taken versus awarded definition removes a few percent of awarded corners. For World Cup knockout games and UCL knockout second legs the extra-time branch (probability of a draw at 90 times about 30 extra minutes of corner rate, often elevated by fatigue and chasing) is part of the count.
stages.distribution: Exposure is a small discrete variable; extra time adds corners when played (2-3 and 30% of knockout ties are unsourced placeholders).

stages.name: Rivalry, stakes and settlement
stages.description: High-stakes or derby matches increase tempo and aggression; settlement requires the count taken in the entire game from the match feed and mapping of N+ rungs; ladder consistency across rungs is a constraint.
stages.distribution: Mild shifts in mean (derby shift of unmeasured size); deterministic settlement.

game_context_script.note: Trailing/leading effect is the largest source of variation in team corners.

soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.label: Corners generated per attack by shot outcome (blocked, saved, deflected)
soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.mechanism: Expected corners from the counts of blocked, saved-and-parried, and deflected attempts and crosses.
soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.rationale: Corners are a by-product of how attacks end; two teams with equal shots differ in corners according to the share of blocked shots and crosses; shot-based expected corners provide a more accurate estimate than past corner counts.
soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.measurement: Poisson regression of team corners per match on its saved-shot count and blocked-shot count (Understat result field) with opponent defence and home terms, trained on the last 3 seasons (match weights half-life 25 matches), coefficients ridge-shrunk toward league values with k=40 matches. Expected corners for the fixture = coefficients times expected saved/blocked shots from the soc.shots model (blocked share from the opponent's block rate). Crosses are included only if a paid feed is available. As-of kickoff-1h using prior matches.
raw_data: corners taken per team per match
soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.why: Moves from historic corner counts to a causal expectation based on how attacks end.

soc.corner_state_multiplier.label: Score-state multipliers on corner rate by team role
soc.corner_state_multiplier.mechanism: Corner rate multiplier for the trailing and leading team by minute bucket and goal margin.
soc.corner_state_multiplier.rationale: Totals and team counts depend on when goals happen: an early goal by the favourite reduces its corners, a late equaliser chase increases the trailer's, so unconditional averages mis-state the favourite's team threshold.
soc.corner_state_multiplier.measurement: From event data with minute and score: corners per 10 minutes for trailing, level and leading states by pre-match favourite/underdog; estimate multiplier m_state relative to level state with Poisson regression, 8 seasons; shrink per team with k=300 minutes; combine with simulation of goal timing to get distribution of corners.
soc.corner_state_multiplier.why: Provides the dynamic structure behind team-corner thresholds that static team averages cannot.

soc.cross_and_wide_play_share.label: Share of attacks through wide areas and crosses
soc.cross_and_wide_play_share.mechanism: Crosses and wide-zone entries per 90 for the team and the opponent's concession of them.
soc.cross_and_wide_play_share.rationale: Crossing teams generate blocked crosses and corners at much higher rates than central combination teams; the opponent's wide defending determines conversion.
soc.cross_and_wide_play_share.measurement: Per team: crosses attempted per 90 and share of final-third entries via wide zones (last 25 matches, opponent-adjusted by regression with defence effects, shrink k=8 matches) and opponent's crosses conceded; the product (attack share × opponent concession relative to league mean) gives a matchup multiplier on expected corners.
raw_data: crosses and final-third entries by zone per match
soc.cross_and_wide_play_share.why: Captures matchup in how teams attack, which total corner counts depend on.

soc.corner_taken_definition_flag.label: Taken-versus-awarded and extra-time inclusion flags
soc.corner_taken_definition_flag.mechanism: Per-series contract flags describing counting definition and the data provider's corner event type.
soc.corner_taken_definition_flag.rationale: Provider event definitions differ (awarded vs taken) and the sampled rules contain the 'actually taken' clause in some series only; wrong definition adds a systematic count error of a few percent.
soc.corner_taken_definition_flag.measurement: Parse rules into flags: taken_only, includes_ET, team vs combined; map provider field (e.g. corner taken event); measure the ratio taken/awarded in a historical sample from a provider with both (an unsourced guess of 0.97-1.0, to be measured) per league; store with version hash and timestamp.
soc.corner_taken_definition_flag.why: Settlement-definition input needed to label training data consistently.

soc.corners.reason: Opponent-adjusted corners for/against is the core rate; should be built from shot outcomes and state, not raw averages.

soc.fouls_cards.reason: UNVERIFIED (no live cards or fouls contract exists in the ledger): fouls and cards are not corner determinants; the verdict is a domain judgement, not tested against any cards contract.

soc.referee.reason: Referee influence on corner counts is minor (via stoppages); card tendencies are irrelevant here.

soc.pace_press.reason: Possession and territory proxy volume; partially overlapping with corner rates.

soc.formation.reason: Formation determines width and crossing volume; hard to measure pregame.

soc.rivalry_intensity.reason: UNVERIFIED (derby effect on corners is not established and no cards contract exists): kept as a weak flag, a domain judgement not tested against data.

soc.stakes_leverage.reason: Stakes shift corner counts only marginally; mostly redundant with tempo.

soc.score_state.reason: Score-state response is the largest variation source but is not pregame; used to estimate state multipliers.

soc.set_piece_matchup.reason: Set-piece strength concerns conversion of corners into goals, not counts of corners; some link via aerial approach.

soc.var_intervention_rate.reason: VAR reviews lengthen stoppage and cancel some awarded corners; a small exposure effect.

soc.added_time.reason: Added minutes scale exposure; ET inclusion for cup matches matters more.

soc.extra_time_shootout_model.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s4) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: A favourite's team corners depend on whether it scores early: an early goal drops its expected count while the underdog's rises, so the favourite's team-corner threshold has a negative interaction with goal timing; the match total changes less.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare favourite corner counts split by whether it scored before minute 30.

interactions.mechanism: A wide-attacking team facing a low block that clears crosses over the byline yields a multiplicative boost to corners: width volume times opponent concession rate, not their sum.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit corners on product of attack width and opponent concession index.

interactions.mechanism: Corners per attack saturate at very high possession against deep blocks because shot quality, not volume, becomes the limit, but total corners still rise with territorial dominance as s1 states; the saturation concerns the marginal corner per extra attack and is a hypothesis, not a decline in counts.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot corners vs shots volume by possession decile.

interactions.mechanism: Late stoppage minutes are played in a score state that is already imbalanced, so added time multiplies the trailing side's elevated corner rate: a long second-half added time in a one-goal game adds more expected corners than the same minutes in a level game.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare corners per minute in the 90+ period by score margin and fit an added-minutes x margin term.

nonlinearities.shape: Negative-binomial overdispersion; variance excess over Poisson to be estimated (1.2-1.4 times the mean is a placeholder)
nonlinearities.why: Counts are overdispersed by game-state heterogeneity, so Poisson-based rung probabilities are too narrow at both tails.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise by margin: +1 goal raises trailer, saturates beyond 2
nonlinearities.why: Corner multipliers grow when trailing by one and saturate at two goals as the trailing team gives up or the leader parks.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in cross volume
nonlinearities.why: More crosses add corners at a decreasing rate as defensive clearances become less likely to go over the byline.

contract.settlement_definition: Per-player binaries over the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods): 'Goalscorer' = records at least 1 goal (floor 0.5, greater), 'Assists' = at least 1 assist, 'Score or Assist' = a goal or an assist, 'First Goalscorer' = the player records the first goal (plus a 'No Goal' outcome), and the 'First Goal Win' combo = the named player scores the first non-own goal AND his team wins (including any officially recognized tiebreaking procedure). If a player is active but never enters the game (the wording says only 'active'; the outcome for a player who is injured, rested or not in the matchday squad is not stated) the market settles to the (last) fair market price before game start rather than to No; once a player enters, settlement is on his goals/assists. For the club and Nations League first-goalscorer texts, a first goal scored before the player enters as a substitute also settles to fair price; KXWCFIRSTGOAL and KXWCTEAMFIRSTGOAL have no such clause ('Once a player enters the game, the market settles based on the player's goals scored'), so a substitute entering after the opener resolves on his goals. World Cup and Super Cup variants add: N+ goal rungs (KXUEFASCGOAL 'at least 2 goals'); first goalscorer where an own-goal opener passes to 'the next non-own-goal scored' (KXWCFIRSTGOAL); the first goal for a named team in the match (KXWCTEAMFIRSTGOAL, own goals skipped likewise); and the first goalscorer for a country over the whole 2026 World Cup (KXWCTEAM1STGOAL), which spans several matches, excludes own goals and shootouts and has a 'No Goalscorer' leg; its text is cut at 'All players who do not score the first qualifying goal will r', so the non-scorer outcome (presumably No) is not fully visible.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player is active but never enters the game, the market settles to the fair market price before game start.
rules_evidence.establishes: A player who is 'active' but never enters is refunded at the pre-game fair price, which removes benching risk for unused substitutes; the quote does not say what happens to a player who is injured, rested or outside the matchday squad (not active), so squad inclusion cannot be assumed to be refunded.

rules_evidence.quote: If the first qualifying goal is scored before the player enters the match as a substitute, the market will also settle to the fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: A substitute's first-goalscorer contract is voided at fair price if the first goal arrives before he enters, so the relevant probability is conditional on being on the pitch at the time of the first goal.

rules_evidence.quote: records at least 1 assist during the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)
rules_evidence.establishes: Assists count in extra time; for knockout games the exposure exceeds 90 minutes, and assist attribution follows the official data provider's definition (not shown).

rules_evidence.quote: The first qualifying goal is the first non-own goal scored by either team, including regulation, stoppage time and any extra time.
rules_evidence.establishes: In the combo contract own goals are skipped when finding the first goal, a different definition from sibling team-level first-goal markets that credit own goals to the beneficiary.

rules_evidence.quote: records a goal or assist during the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)
rules_evidence.establishes: Score-or-assist is a union event: P(goal or assist) = P(goal) + P(assist) - P(both), where both is a within-player correlation, and a player cannot assist his own goal.

rules_evidence.quote: The winning team is determined by the official match result, including any officially recognized tiebreaking procedure.
rules_evidence.establishes: In the First Goal Win combo a penalty-shootout win counts as the team winning, so the second leg is the official result including tiebreakers, not the regulation score; the player must also score the first non-own goal.

rules_evidence.quote: If the first goal of the match is an own goal, the market will resolve based on the next non-own-goal scored.
rules_evidence.establishes: First-goalscorer markets skip own goals and settle on the next credited non-own goal, so the race is among players only.

rules_evidence.quote: If no player from the Country scores a goal, the No Goalscorer market will resolve Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The country-first-goalscorer series runs over the whole tournament with a no-scorer leg, so it depends on the country's matches played and its scoring share across games.

rules_evidence.quote: records the first goal for Argentina during the entire game
rules_evidence.establishes: Team-first-goal markets condition on the named team scoring and ask which of its players scores first, a within-team share race.

variants_and_edge_cases: DNP/bench rule: unlike many sports props, a player who never enters settles to fair price (stated 'before game start' vs 'last fair market price before game start' in different series), so the market contains an embedded refund and pre-game liquidity matters; once a player enters for one minute the contract resolves on his actual output.

First goalscorer: the 'No Goal' outcome resolves YES when no player scores; KXWCFIRSTGOAL and KXWCTEAMFIRSTGOAL skip own goals to the next non-own goal, while the EPL first-goal text is cut before its own-goal clause; KXINTLFRIENDLYFGW also uses the first non-own goal.

Assist attribution depends on the data provider (Opta-style definitions: the final pass leading directly to a goal, counting deflected passes in some cases; set-piece assists and penalty-won are not assists); own goals have no assist; this determines assists and score-or-assist labels.

Strikes are N+ for count thresholds (floor 0.5 means at least one) with also 2+ goals/hat-trick style rungs possible; extra time is included, so cup matches add exposure; abandonment mid-match with goals scored is not described.

33 live series, all with rules text; 8 World Cup and UEFA Super Cup series were re-filed here, including the tournament-span KXWCTEAM1STGOAL, which is not a single-match prop (its non-scorer clause is cut off in the sampled text). The World Cup first-goal texts lack the club texts' substitute-after-opener fair-price clause.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official match data feed event log (goals with scorer, assists, substitutions) from the provider used by Kalshi (not named in the texts); own goals are skipped to the next non-own goal in KXINTLFRIENDLYFGW, KXWCFIRSTGOAL, KXWCTEAMFIRSTGOAL and KXWCTEAM1STGOAL, while the club first-goal texts are cut before any own-goal clause.

mechanism.summary: A player goal or assist prop is a thinned, allocated team event. The player must be on the pitch (starter, substitute, or unused, where an unused player settles at fair price); given minutes, his probability is one minus exp(-lambda) with lambda equal to the team's expected goals in this fixture times his share of team chances times conversion, plus penalty duty; assists are the same logic through creation share and the set-piece taker role, bounded by team goals and the teammates' finishing; score-or-assist is a union with within-player dependence. First goalscorer is a competing-risk race for the first goal with a categorical allocation and substitution timing, and the combo adds the dependence between scoring first and winning. Extra time counts, and own-goal and fair-price rules vary by series.

stages.name: Availability and entry into the game
stages.description: Whether the named player starts, enters as a substitute, or does not play at all determines his minutes distribution: starters average 80-90 minutes, substitutes 15-30. Because an active player who never enters settles at fair price, the relevant quantity for that group is the output conditional on playing, weighted by when he enters (an early sub is almost a starter) and by late lineup information on starting status; players outside the matchday squad are a separate case the texts do not state. For club first-goalscorer texts entry after the opener voids to fair price, while World Cup first-goal texts resolve such a substitute on his goals.
stages.distribution: Three-point mixture: starter (about 85 minutes), substitute (about 20 minutes), unused; substitution times right-skewed.

stages.name: Team goal volume in this fixture
stages.description: The player's team has an expected goal total set by its opponent-adjusted attack against this opponent's defence and keeper; a player's chance is a share of that, so the same striker has a 55% scoring chance in a 3.0-xG home game and 25% in a 0.9-xG away game. Tempo and game state influence the team's volume.
stages.distribution: Team goals as an overdispersed count; the player's count conditional on team count is binomial-like with allocation by share.

stages.name: Player's share and conversion
stages.description: Share of team shots and chances, shot quality (location, header vs foot), finishing relative to xG and role in set pieces and penalties determine the player's goal rate per 90; penalty duty adds roughly 0.1 goals per match for the taker (about 0.15 team penalties per match x about 0.78 conversion; about 0.3 penalties per match is the two-team total), and set-piece aerial threats add a lumpy component. Finishing must be regressed.
stages.distribution: Per-90 rate with heavy shrinkage (finishing persistence about 20-30%); zero-heavy count (P(0)>55% for forwards).

stages.name: Assist and chance-creation structure
stages.description: Assists depend on the player's creation (key passes, crosses, set-piece delivery) and on the finishing of the teammates who receive the chances; the set-piece taker (corners and free kicks) holds a disproportionate share of assists; an assist requires a goal to be scored, so assist probability is bounded by team goals and the player's share of creation.
stages.distribution: Compound process: team goals times player's share of assist credit; assists are rarer than goals (about 0.08 per 90 for creators), with large provider-definition noise.

stages.name: First-goal race and combo structure
stages.description: First goalscorer is a joint event: the team scores first (a competing-risk race), the scorer is the specific player (a share of first-goal routes weighted toward set pieces and penalties early), and for substitutes he must be on the pitch. The combo 'scores first and team wins' adds the positive dependence between scoring first and winning (the first scorer wins roughly 70% of the time and win-or-draw is nearer 85-90%; both are unsourced hypotheses, and in the combo the win includes any officially recognised tiebreak).
stages.distribution: Competing-risk race then categorical allocation; P(no goal) about 8%; conditional dependence between first goal and result.

stages.name: Settlement mapping
stages.description: Settlement maps official event logs to each player-level contract with specific DNP/fair-price, extra-time and own-goal rules; labelling errors arise from treating a fair-price settlement as a loss and from using different first-goal definitions in the combo and the team-level market.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from event feed; ambiguity in provider definitions.

stages.name: Team-conditional and tournament-span first scorer
stages.description: Two variants change the first-goal race: the first goal for a named team in a match is a race only among that team's players, so it equals the player's share of his team's expected goals adjusted for entry time and penalty duty, plus the team's no-goal probability; the first goal for a country over the whole World Cup chains this race across matches until the country first scores, so exposure is the number of matches until the first goal, which depends on group opponents and the team's goal rate.
stages.distribution: Within-team multinomial over players with a no-goal leg; for the tournament version a geometric-like number of matches until the first goal, mixed over lineups per match.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent's chances conceded by zone and position, keeper quality.

role_personnel.note: Role in chance creation, set pieces and penalties.

availability_news.note: Starting status and entry; confirmed lineups about an hour before kickoff.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach substitution timing and rotation habits.

environment.note: Weather and venue change team goal rates by a few percent, which the team lambda already carries; no player-specific environmental input has evidence, so none is added for goal/assist props.

game_context_script.note: Competing-risk race for the first goal and its link to the result.

pace_volume.note: Shots and touches in the box per 90.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing over/under-performance regressed to the player's baseline.

distribution_variance.note: Zero-heavy count and union events (goal or assist).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Dead-rubber, congestion and cup-priority effects on whether a star plays 90 minutes or is substituted early depend on stakes, but no pregame stakes input is attached to this archetype and the effect on a player's minutes is only partly in rotation_index.

officiating_rules.note: Referee penalty tendency determines penalty opportunities for the taker.

soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.label: Starter/substitute/DNP mixture and settlement-adjusted probability
soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.mechanism: Probabilities of starting, entering as a substitute at each minute, and not playing, with the contract's fair-price rule applied.
soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.rationale: Because a DNP settles at the fair price and a pre-first-goal substitution voids first-goalscorer contracts, the effective probability must be computed as a conditional on playing; mixing in a DNP loss biases prices of bench players downward.
soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.measurement: p_start from a logistic model on prior 5 starts, minutes, injury flags and rest (calibrated), p_sub|bench from historical sub rates by position and score state; substitution minute distribution from league data (median about 65 for attackers); P(plays) = p_start + (1-p_start)*p_sub; effective price probability P_eff = P(goal|plays) with the refund rule; for first goalscorer also P(on pitch at first goal); as-of strictly lineup release.
soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.why: Embedded refund rule is peculiar to this contract and changes the correct probability for every non-starter.

soc.assist_set_piece_role.label: Assist share by set-piece delivery and open-play creation
soc.assist_set_piece_role.mechanism: Player's share of team assists and key passes split by route (set-piece delivery, crosses, through balls).
soc.assist_set_piece_role.rationale: Assists are concentrated in a few creators and in the corner/free-kick taker, whose assist rate per 90 is 2-3 times that of a typical midfielder; the provider's definition of assist also matters.
soc.assist_set_piece_role.measurement: Over the player's last 40 club matches (half-life 20): set-piece xA/90 and open-play xA/90 from Understat shots (situation in {FromCorner,SetPiece,DirectFreekick} vs OpenPlay, credited to the assisting player), each shrunk to position mean with k=900 minutes. Expected assists = player xA share of team xA (shrunk, k=10 matches) x team expected xG for this match x team assisted-goal ratio (league mean, estimated not fixed at 70%). Set-piece taker flag = taker of >=50% of team corners in the window. As-of kickoff-1h; recompute with confirmed XI.
raw_data: player xA, key passes, assists per match
soc.assist_set_piece_role.why: Needed because assist props are driven by creators and set-piece takers, not by xG/90.

soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.label: First goalscorer allocation model with competing risks and sub timing
soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.mechanism: Joint probability that the player's team scores first and that he is the scorer, including time-varying intensity and substitution.
soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.rationale: P(first goalscorer) = integral over time of team first-goal intensity × player's share of that team's goals at that time × P(on pitch at t), which is not equal to team probability × season goal share, especially for early set-piece takers and substitutes.
soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.measurement: Combine first_goal_hazard per team with the player's share of team goals by minute bucket (open play, set piece, penalty) from last 40 matches (shrink k=10) and P(on pitch at t) from the substitution model; P_first = ∫ h_team(t)·S(t)·share_i(t)·P_on(t) dt; also P(no goal) from joint survival; Monte Carlo 20k per match; as-of lineup release.
raw_data: goal events with minute and scorer
soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.why: Provides coherent probabilities for the first-goal and first-goal-win contracts.

soc.country_first_tournament_goal_race.label: Within-team first-goal race across one match or a tournament
soc.country_first_tournament_goal_race.mechanism: Team-first and country-first goalscorer markets are races among one team's players, repeated across matches until the team scores.
soc.country_first_tournament_goal_race.rationale: Match-level first-goalscorer models race all 22 players; the team-first and country-first versions condition on one team and (for the tournament) roll over to the next match if the team does not score, so a starter in the opening game has a large edge and the no-scorer leg depends on the team's goal rate over its schedule.
soc.country_first_tournament_goal_race.measurement: Per player per match: share of team npxG (last 12 internationals or 20 club matches, shrunk to positional prior with k=8) times start probability and expected minutes share, plus penalty share times team penalty rate; per match the team's goal hazard from the match model; simulate matches in order (N>=100,000) until the first non-own team goal, recording the scorer or 'no goalscorer' if the team exits without scoring.
raw_data: player international goals, npxG proxy, minutes, starts
soc.country_first_tournament_goal_race.why: Prices the team-first and country-first-in-tournament goalscorer series.

soc.player_xg.reason: Non-penalty xG/90 and xA/90 supply the player-level rate; must be combined with minutes and match-specific team volume.

soc.player_shot_share.reason: Share of team shots/SOT is the allocation variable that turns team volume into player probability.

soc.lineups_pit.reason: Starter status at lineup release is the largest single determinant of player-prop probability.

soc.player_minutes_expectation.reason: Minutes distribution multiplies every rate; for substitutes the entry minute matters.

soc.penalty_taker_status.reason: Designated penalty taker has a distinct discrete scoring route (about 0.15 penalties per team per match, 0.3 for both teams combined, converted around 78%).

soc.penalty_rate.reason: Penalty awards rate by team and referee changes the taker's probability by a few points.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.reason: Team expected goals in this fixture set the scale to which player shares apply.

soc.opp_shot_profile_by_zone.reason: Opponent's concession by zone and attacker position gives matchup adjustment for the specific player.

soc.gk.reason: Opponent keeper effect is small relative to team defence strength and mostly shrinks away.

soc.finishing_regression.reason: Prevents over-weighting hot streaks; shrinkage constant is essential.

soc.rotation_index.reason: Predicts lineup changes before release, useful for early-day prices.

soc.referee.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on soc.penalty_taker_status x soc.referee: A penalty taker's goal probability rises when the referee awards penalties at a high rate.) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

soc.formation.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on soc.player_shot_share x soc.formation: Formation changes redistribute shot share among forwards and wingers.) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

soc.set_pieces.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s4) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: A substitute's minutes fall mostly in game states where his team is trailing or protecting a lead, so the team lambda during his minutes differs from the full-match lambda; his expected goals are not per-90 rate x minutes x full-match team lambda but a state-conditional minute-weighted rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predicted versus realised goals for substitutes split by score state at entry and by team rating gap.

interactions.mechanism: The player's goal chance depends on whether the zones and shot types he occupies (box central, headers) match what the opponent concedes: the same shot share yields more expected goals against a defence that concedes box-central chances than one that concedes wide shots.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit player xG per shot on his zone profile interacted with the opponent concession profile by zone.

interactions.mechanism: The taker's extra probability exists only if a penalty is awarded (about 0.15 per team per match, 0.3 for both teams combined, higher with referees and teams that win penalties); the effect is a discrete bump, conditional on the taker being on the pitch.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare taker scoring rate in matches with penalties vs without.

interactions.mechanism: For first goalscorer a substitute's chance is conditional on entering before the first goal, which depends on rotation and the timing of the first goal: if the first goal comes early, subs are excluded, so the fair-price void changes the effective denominators.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(on pitch at first goal) by role and minute distribution of first goals.

interactions.mechanism: Assist probability scales with team goals and with the set-piece taker's share; in a high-xG match the taker's chance grows roughly linearly while a non-taker's grows more slowly, so team volume interacts with role.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit assists on team xG interacted with set-piece-taker flag.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating 1-exp(-lambda) from team volume to player P(1+)
nonlinearities.why: Player goal probability saturates: a doubling of lambda from 0.3 to 0.6 raises P(1+) from about 0.26 to about 0.45 (a rise of about 0.19) rather than doubling.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise in minutes with substitution at 60-70
nonlinearities.why: Expected goals are roughly linear in minutes but entry minute distribution is bimodal (starters vs substitutes), so mean minutes misprices both groups.

nonlinearities.shape: Shrinkage weight rising with shots
nonlinearities.why: Weight on realised finishing grows with the sample of shots, n/(n+k) with k around 100.

contract.settlement_definition: HYPOTHETICAL TEMPLATE, NOT A LISTED CONTRACT: No live Kalshi series maps to this archetype in the ledger, so there is no contract text to read. The catalog target is a player's shot or shot-on-target count, or a goalkeeper's saves, relative to an N+ threshold over a match. Settlement details (which shots count, whether blocked shots and headers are included, whether penalties count in shots and saves, regulation-only versus entire game with extra time, the DNP/substitute rule, the data provider's definitions) cannot be stated and are recorded as unresolved rather than inferred from the neighbouring goal/assist props, whose texts do say 'entire game' with fair-price DNP settlement.
variants_and_edge_cases: Shot definition: provider counts differ on blocked shots (an Opta 'shot' includes blocked, a 'shot on target' excludes them), on headers and on penalties; a shots threshold of 3+ for a striker is a different event under each, so the data provider must be identified before any calibration.

Goalkeeper saves count only shots on target that did not become goals, so saves = shots on target faced minus goals conceded (and own-goal and penalty details), making the contract a function of the opponent's SOT volume and of the goals actually conceded; a 4-0 loss can still have 4 saves while a 1-0 win can have 6.

DNP/substitute handling, extra time inclusion and abandoned matches are unknown; if the family follows neighbouring goal/assist props it would be entire-game with fair-price settlement for non-participants, but that is an assumption.
The catalog lists both players and keepers in one archetype although their drivers differ (player share of team shots versus opponent volume), so any live series would probably need separate keys.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not verified; presumably an official data-feed event log (shots, shots on target, saves per player) from the league's data provider used by Kalshi.

mechanism.summary: HYPOTHETICAL TEMPLATE (no live series, no rules text; nothing here is evidence that Kalshi lists shots or saves props). A player shot count thins the team's shot volume: minutes on the pitch (starter, early substitution), the team's expected shots against this defence, the player's share by role and set-piece duty, and a score-state multiplier since trailing teams shoot more. Shots on target add an accuracy layer. A goalkeeper's saves are a difference: opponent shots on target minus goals conceded, so the count depends on opponent SOT volume, shot quality and the actual goals, and it is non-monotone in opponent quality. Definitions of shots and saves depend on the data provider, and no live series exists to fix settlement.

stages.name: Playing time and role
stages.description: A shot count scales with minutes on the pitch and with the player's role: central forwards and wide attackers take 2-4 shots per 90 while defenders take under one; starting status, expected minutes and whether the player is subbed off in a game that is decided shift the count; for a goalkeeper the role is binary (starter or not), which makes minutes almost deterministic.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated by non-participation; for outfield players minutes distribution right-skewed; keeper minutes nearly constant at 90.

stages.name: Team shot volume in the fixture
stages.description: The team's total shots in this match come from its opponent-adjusted attacking volume, tempo and game plan against this defence; strong teams against low blocks produce 18+ shots, while counter-attacking teams produce fewer but better ones; the player's expected shots are the team volume times his share of shots, and shots on target multiplies by accuracy.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial team counts with mean and sd to be estimated per league (12 and 4 are illustrative placeholders); player counts thin the team count with a binomial-like allocation, giving heavy overdispersion.

stages.name: Game-state response of shot volume
stages.description: The trailing team shoots more and from lower-quality positions, while the leader's volume declines; in blowouts the winner's volume often falls late while the loser's rises. So the player's shot count depends on whether his team leads, and the keeper's saves depend on the trailing opponent's late volume, making the final count a function of the match's score path.
stages.distribution: Time-varying intensity with state multipliers of placeholders of +20% to +40% to be estimated for the trailer; joint distribution of goals and shots (negative correlation within team).

stages.name: Shot conversion to on-target and to goals (keeper side)
stages.description: Shots on target depend on shot quality and the shooter's accuracy; a keeper's saves are SOT faced minus goals conceded, so strong shot quality (high PSxG) turns SOT into goals rather than saves, and the keeper's own shot-stopping quality shifts saves by a few tenths per match. Penalties add a rare high-conversion event.
stages.distribution: Binomial thinning of shots into on-target (illustrative 33%) and then into goals (illustrative 30% of SOT); saves mean and sd to be estimated (about 3 and 1.7 are illustrative).

stages.name: Formation, personnel matchups and settlement definitions
stages.description: Which opposing defenders and tactical system face the shooter (central or wide, high line or deep block) affects his shot opportunities; the settlement counts depend on the provider's definitions of shots, blocked shots and saves, on extra time inclusion and on the participation rule.
stages.distribution: Matchup multipliers about 0.8-1.25; definition ambiguity is a deterministic offset (blocked shots count or not).

talent_strength.note: Team shot volume and player shot share.
