soc.player_shot_volume_state_response.label: Player shot rate multiplier by team score state
soc.player_shot_volume_state_response.mechanism: Multipliers on a player's shots per 90 when his team is trailing, level or leading.
soc.player_shot_volume_state_response.rationale: Strikers on trailing teams shoot more, and role-dependent: a poacher's share rises when his team chases while a creator's rises less, so state-conditional rates are needed in addition to season averages.
soc.player_shot_volume_state_response.measurement: From events: player shots per 90 in each state by minute bucket relative to level; Poisson regression with offset log(minutes) and player random effect, 4 seasons; shrink to position mean with k=400 minutes in-state; combine with pregame team win probability to compute expected state mixture of shots.
raw_data: shot events with minute, player, score state
soc.player_shot_volume_state_response.why: Allows a pregame forecast that reflects the favourite or underdog role of the player's team.

soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.label: Expected saves from opponent SOT and shot quality
soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.mechanism: Expected saves = expected opponent SOT minus expected goals conceded, using shot quality.
soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.rationale: Keeper saves are a difference of two counts: high SOT volume with many easy shots gives many saves, while the same volume of high-quality shots gives goals, so two matches with equal SOT can differ by two saves.
soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.measurement: E[saves] = E[SOT faced] - E[goals conceded]; E[SOT faced] = opponent expected shots × SOT rate (opponent-adjusted, last 25 matches, half-life 12); E[goals] = E[SOT] × mean(PSxG per SOT) × keeper adjustment (shrunk PSxG-GA/SOT with k=60 SOT); includes penalty probability; variance via compound negative binomial; as-of lineup release.
raw_data: team shots, SOT, goals conceded, PSxG
soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.why: Extends soc.keeper_workload (whose catalog measurement already multiplies expected SOT by a shrunk PSxG-based save probability): it adds only the goals-conceded subtraction and a compound-count variance, and is not independent of it.

soc.shot_event_definition_mapping.label: Provider shot, shot-on-target and save definition mapping
soc.shot_event_definition_mapping.mechanism: Flags and conversion ratios between provider definitions of shots, on-target shots and saves.
soc.shot_event_definition_mapping.rationale: Different providers count blocked shots, headers and penalties differently, changing shot counts by 10-20%; calibrating on a different definition than the settlement feed produces systematic bias.
soc.shot_event_definition_mapping.measurement: For a sample of 200+ matches with two providers, estimate ratio r = shots_settlement / shots_training by player position, blocked-share and penalty treatment; store mapping per league; apply multiplicative correction and widen variance; version-hash the definitions. Practical caveat: this needs shot counts from two providers for the same 200+ matches, which the free sources listed cannot supply, so the mapping is likely undefined in practice until a contract names its provider.
raw_data: two-provider shot counts for the same matches
soc.shot_event_definition_mapping.why: Label consistency is a prerequisite for calibration given no rules text exists.

interactions.mechanism: A striker's expected shots are team volume times share times a state multiplier; an underdog's striker has a lower base volume but a large trailing-state boost, and the three factors multiply, so the expected count is not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit player shots with interaction of team win probability and role in a Poisson regression.

interactions.mechanism: At fixed conversion saves are monotone increasing in shots on target faced; a non-monotone pattern across opponents arises only if shot quality (and so conversion) rises with opponent attack faster than SOT volume, which is a hypothesis; opponent zone concession shifts both volume and quality at once.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare saves against SOT and PSxG deciles, then split by opponent zone-concession profile to see whether quality outruns volume.

interactions.mechanism: A substitute or early-substituted striker accumulates his minutes mostly in trailing or protecting states, so his shot rate during those minutes is the state-specific rate, not the full-match average; the product of minutes and state multiplier differs from minutes x average rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised shots for substitutes and early-hooked starters with a model using full-match rate versus a state-weighted rate by score state at entry.

interactions.mechanism: A winger's shots depend on the opposing full-back and the system: against a back five the wide player takes fewer shots and more crosses, so the matchup effect is conditional on the opponent's formation.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact shot rate with opposing formation indicator by position.

nonlinearities.shape: Non-monotone in opponent shot quality
nonlinearities.why: Saves are SOT minus goals: at fixed conversion they are monotone in SOT, and they decline in opponent quality only if conversion rises faster than SOT volume (hypothesis to test), so the shape is not asserted to be non-monotone.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in the goal deficit
nonlinearities.why: Trailing by one lifts shots by an amount to be estimated (20-30% is a placeholder) but trailing by three adds little since players shoot from low-quality positions with fatigue.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise in entry minute for substitutes
nonlinearities.why: Shot count is near-linear in minutes for starters but a substitute entering after 75 minutes has a sharply smaller expected count.
